title: A physics-informed recurrent neural network for long sequence remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearing with implicit function
exported_title: A physics-informed recurrent neural network for long sequence remaining useful life prediction of rolling bearing with implicit function

metadata.abstract: Accurate long-sequence remaining useful life (LSRUL) prediction for rolling bearings is crucial for providing a broad operational horizon, enabling proactive decision-making and catastrophic failure prevention. However, prevailing data-driven approaches often suffer from limited accuracy due to dynamic perturbations and error accumulation during multistep prediction, as well as poor interpretability from a lack of physical guidance. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a physics-informed recurrent neural network (PIRNN). The PIRNN architecture integrates a variational recurrent neural network (VRNN) and an implicit function solver (IFS). The former captures long-range temporal dependencies for robust LSRUL forecasting, while a novel weighted multistep prediction mechanism mitigates error propagation. Concurrently, the IFS constrains the solution space by approximating the implicit functions within the time-dependent partial differential equations (PDEs) governing the rolling bearing's physics, which enhances the model's interpretability, improves prediction accuracy, and accelerates convergence. The effectiveness and superiority of the proposed PIRNN are validated through comprehensive experiments on both open-source and real-world rolling bearing run-to-failure datasets, demonstrating its outperformance over other state-of-the-art prediction models.
keywords: Long sequence remaining useful life prediction

title: Response of multi-dimensional dynamical system under combined Gaussian and Poisson white noise using tensor neural networks
exported_title: Response of multi-dimensional dynamical system under combined Gaussian and Poisson white noise using tensor neural networks

metadata.abstract: Predicting the response density function of multi-dimensional systems under combined Gaussian and Poisson white noise excitations is of practical significance for characterizing the dynamic behavior of engineering systems. However, the forward Kolmogorov equation that governs the probability density function (PDF) of the system response is essentially an integro-differential equation (IDE) due to the jump characteristics of Poisson noise, posing significant challenges to the computational complexity and accuracy of traditional numerical methods in high-dimensional scenarios. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel Tensor Neural Networks-Physics-Informed Neural Networks (TNN-PINNs) learning framework, which integrates the low-rank decomposition properties of Tensor Neural Networks (TNNs) with the physics-constrained mechanisms of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to efficiently solve the reduced forward Kolmogorov equation of high-dimensional systems under Gaussian and Poisson white noises. The core of this framework lies in leveraging the low-rank decomposition properties of TNNs to achieve efficient and accurate computation of the integral terms, while utilizing the physics-constrained characteristics of PINNs to enhance the reliability and generalization ability of the solutions. The effectiveness of the framework is systematically validated in two-dimensional to six-dimensional spaces, addressing the challenge of balancing computational complexity and accuracy in traditional methods for high-dimensional problems.

title: Multi-action predictive maintenance for lithium-ion batteries based on stacked bilinear neural network
exported_title: Multi-action predictive maintenance for lithium-ion batteries based on stacked bilinear neural network

metadata.abstract: Accurately predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of batteries and formulating predictive maintenance (PdM) decisions are essential for ensuring their reliable and efficient operation. However, most existing PdM studies rarely consider a unified framework that integrates probabilistic RUL prediction with short-term maintenance decision-making, making it difficult to meet the growing demands of modern industrial systems for intelligent maintenance. To address this gap, we propose a short-term multi-action PdM strategy driven by probabilistic RUL prediction. First, a stacked bilinear neural network (SBNN) is developed to extract both feature interactions and temporal degradation patterns from the measurement data. Then, by integrating quantile regression (QR) with kernel density estimation (KDE), a fully data-driven probabilistic representation of RUL is obtained. Based on the predicted RUL distribution, multi-action maintenance models are formulated for both single and multi-component systems, considering downtime, spare-part inventory and operating cycle length. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed approach is validated using two real lithium-ion battery degradation datasets from MIT and Oxford. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed RUL prediction method achieves the best performance in both point estimation and uncertainty quantification. Specifically, it attains an average RMSE of 13.7672 and an average PICP of 0.9552, outperforming several state-of-the-art baseline algorithms. Moreover, the proposed predictive maintenance strategy can effectively prevent component-level failures and reduce system-level maintenance costs.

title: Physics-informed multi-task generation: Toward automated risk control optimization
exported_title: Physics-informed multi-task generation: Toward automated risk control optimization

metadata.abstract: Automated risk control measure generation is crucial for safety and reliability in complex engineering systems. Traditional expert-based methods are labor-intensive and subjective. While large language models (LLMs) exhibit strong general capabilities, their specialized-domain outputs lack reliability due to limited domain knowledge. To address these challenges, we propose a physics-informed multi-task generation (PIMTG) framework that integrates physical constraints of risk propagation with deep learning. PIMTG enables co-optimized generation of three risk control measures: engineering interventions, safety management strategies, and emergency preparedness protocols, enhancing both textual quality and physical rationality. Specifically, we first develop a gated fusion mechanism with adaptive attention for heterogeneous features (textual, numerical, categorical). Additionally, we propose a multi-task prefix adapter to generate different risk control measures. Finally, we develop a training objective incorporating risk energy and evolution constraint equations, jointly minimizing text generation loss and physical consistency loss. This ensures that risk source terms, diffusion terms, absorption terms, and inherent risk values comply with first principles. On real industrial cases, PIMTG achieves an average BERTScore of 78.75%, a physical consistency index of 99.9%, and a symmetric mean absolute percentage error (SMAPE) of 0.0448, demonstrating its accuracy and reliability in automated risk control.

title: Active learning reliability analysis of highly non-stationary geotechnical systems using adaptive compressive sensing-enhanced Kriging and Monte Carlo simulation
exported_title: Active learning reliability analysis of highly non-stationary geotechnical systems using adaptive compressive sensing-enhanced Kriging and Monte Carlo simulation

metadata.abstract: Kriging has been widely used to develop active learning methods for improving the efficiency of reliability analysis, owing to its capability to provide both response prediction and uncertainty quantification. However, conventional Kriging methods rely on the assumption of stationarity, limiting their effectiveness in interpolating non-stationary data. To address this challenge, this study develops an innovative active learning method using adaptive compressive sensing (CS)-enhanced Kriging (ACSK) and Monte Carlo simulation (MCS), termed ACSK-MCS, for reliability analysis of highly non-stationary geotechnical systems. In ACSK-MCS, a novel CS-enhanced Kriging response surface method (RSM) is first proposed by employing a non-parametric CS approach based on discrete cosine transform basis functions to construct the non-stationary trend function. It incorporates both the advantage of Bayesian compressive sensing-based RSM in accurately modeling highly non-stationary response surface from sparse sampling data, and the exact interpolation capability of Kriging-based RSM, thereby enabling a powerful active learning capability. Subsequently, CS-enhanced Kriging RSM is integrated with a learning function to adaptively determine the minimum number of sampling points required and their corresponding locations for achieving the target accuracy of reliability analysis. Numerical investigations on three highly non-stationary analytical benchmark examples and an engineering application demonstrate the effectiveness of ACSK-MCS.

title: Risk-evolution forecasting of epidemic transmission with physics-informed neural networks for a modified susceptible–infected–quarantined–recovered–susceptible model
exported_title: Risk-evolution forecasting of epidemic transmission with physics-informed neural networks for a modified susceptible–infected–quarantined–recovered–susceptible model

metadata.abstract: Epidemic transmission involves nonlinear mechanisms, heterogeneous contacts, and multiple delays, which challenges conventional approaches to balance mechanistic fidelity and predictive accuracy. An integrated framework is developed by coupling a modified Susceptible–Infected–Quarantined–Recovered–Susceptible compartmental model with physics-informed neural networks. The model introduces an adaptive nonlinear incidence function and dual delay mechanisms, including incubation delay and decision-to-quarantine delay. The basic reproduction number is derived analytically via the next-generation matrix method, with stability proofs for both disease-free and endemic equilibria. A physics-informed neural-network-based inverse-problem solver is constructed to infer latent states and time-varying parameters by minimizing a composite objective that penalizes both data mismatch and equation residuals, while uncertainty is assessed through repeated training under perturbed observations. Numerical experiments examine how alternative delay values reshape epidemic outcomes, including final size, peak magnitude, and outbreak duration, thereby clarifying the distinct transmission pathways regulated by each delay. Validation with early-phase empirical data from the Wuhan coronavirus disease 2019 outbreak indicates that the framework yields accurate reconstruction of time-varying parameters and reliable short-term trend forecasting, supporting risk-informed decision making and safety evaluation in epidemic scenarios.

title: Uncertainty-informed cascaded diagnosis of compound faults in electromechanical systems via a physics-informed hypergraph framework
exported_title: Uncertainty-informed cascaded diagnosis of compound faults in electromechanical systems via a physics-informed hypergraph framework

metadata.abstract: Compound fault diagnosis is essential for the reliability management and operational safety of complex electromechanical systems. However, existing data-driven methods often treat diagnosis as a flat classification task, failing to capture higher-order physical interdependencies among components and disregarding the cascaded diagnostic logic where system-level health states should logically govern component-level attributions. To address these challenges, we propose an uncertainty-informed cascaded diagnosis framework, which reformulates compound fault diagnosis as a hierarchical reasoning process. The framework first introduces a deterministic Bond-Graph-to-Hypergraph Priors (BG2HP) protocol that converts coarse physical context into two learning-ready priors: a physics-informed hypergraph and a weak constraint set. Building on these priors, a Physics-informed Hypergraph Multi-Task Network (PHG-MTNet) is developed to explicitly model multi-component interactions as higher-order hyperedges and to enforce weak physics consistency through regularization in the latent space. An Uncertainty-informed Cascaded Inference (UCI) strategy is then designed to govern a top-down diagnostic workflow using calibrated predictive uncertainty, efficiently resolving high-confidence system-level syndromes while escalating ambiguous or safety-critical samples to fine-grained component attribution. Validation on a multi-component hydraulic test bench demonstrates that the proposed framework achieves 99.55% accuracy. Ultimately, by providing uncertainty-quantified and physically consistent diagnostic evidence, the proposed framework serves as an actionable and effective tool for optimizing system-wide reliability management and risk-aware maintenance decisions.

title: Dynamic functional failure traceability model and diagnosis approach for intelligent manufacturing systems with physics-informed spatiotemporal causal graph
exported_title: Dynamic functional failure traceability model and diagnosis approach for intelligent manufacturing systems with physics-informed spatiotemporal causal graph

metadata.abstract:
ABSTRACT
Functional failure dynamic traceability and reliability assurance have become critical bottlenecks to achieving smart maintenance synergy for intelligent manufacturing systems. Most existing approaches rely on correlation-based statistical monitoring of physical equipment failures, failing to holistically consider the interplay between process parameter deviations and workpiece quality defects during functional failure evolution. This limitation undermines both the accuracy and interpretability of failure diagnosis in complex manufacturing environments. To address this gap, this study proposes a novel Causal Maintenance Control (CMC) framework grounded in the Equipment–Process–Quality (E-P-Q) causal chain. The main contributions are threefold: (1) establishing a dynamic E-P-Q causal chain model that systematically characterizes the cross-process propagation of equipment degradation, parameter deviation, and quality defects in functional failure scenarios; (2) developing a physics-informed spatiotemporal causal graph that integrates thermodynamic constraints, neural differential equations, and process-topology attention to reveal the dynamic causal pathways through which functional failures induce quality anomalies; (3) designing a causal-aware adaptive control framework that combines a two-stage traceability mechanism, a Dynamic Criticality Index (DCI), and constrained Bayesian optimization to achieve real-time root-cause localization and proactive compensation. The proposed approach is validated through an industrial case study of aero-engine turbine blade production line.

title: Physics-Informed Multi-Projection Regression for Roller Bearing Remaining Useful Life Prediction
exported_title: Physics-Informed Multi-Projection Regression for Roller Bearing Remaining Useful Life Prediction

metadata.abstract: Traditional matrix-form data-driven approaches for roller bearing remaining useful life (RUL) prediction suffer from two fundamental challenges, namely the inability to capture the geometric evolution of multi-stage degradation dynamics and the lack of physical consistency under data-scarce conditions. To address these limitations, a novel physics-informed multi-projection regression (PIMPR) model is proposed in this paper, which synergistically integrates physical mechanism priors with a structure-preserving learning framework. First, to bridge the gap between physical mechanisms and data-driven models, a four-degree-of-freedom roller bearing dynamic model incorporating an improved Paris law is constructed. This model characterizes the full-lifecycle degradation process, providing high-fidelity privileged information to guide the learning process. Second, unlike traditional vector-based methods, a structure-preserving matrix regression is introduced to retain the correlation within time-frequency data. Meanwhile, a key novelty is the multi-projection mechanism, which geometrically aligns the data subspaces with the three physical degradation stages, thereby enhancing model interpretability and representation capability. Third, a learning using privileged information paradigm is adopted, where the physically predicted lifespan serves as auxiliary guidance to regularize the training manifold. Comprehensive evaluations on two roller bearing datasets demonstrate the favorable performance of the proposed PIMPR, particularly under data-scarce scenarios.

title: Synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE)-enhanced adaptive sampling physics-informed neural networks for efficient reliability analysis
exported_title: Synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE)-enhanced adaptive sampling physics-informed neural networks for efficient reliability analysis

metadata.abstract: Although significant progress has been achieved in adaptive sampling methods for reliability analysis based on Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), computational redundancy caused by fixed-size candidate sample sets and the sparsity of samples near the failure domain still constrain their accuracy and efficiency. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes synthetic minority over-sampling technique (SMOTE)-enhanced adaptive sampling PINNs for efficient reliability analysis (SAS-PINN-RA). Two key mechanisms are introduced: (1) a dynamically updated candidate set that balances global exploration and local refinement by combining globally drawn random samples with near-failure samples carried over from the previous iteration; and (2) a near-failure domain oversampling strategy, where SMOTE is employed to enrich the sample density around the limit state, continuously improving the representation of critical regions. During training, adaptive samples are updated periodically rather than per epoch, reducing the sampling frequency while allowing the model to converge on the current training set between updates. Systematic verification on five benchmark problems demonstrates that SAS-PINN-RA achieves accurate structural response predictions in the near-failure region and efficient failure probability estimation without requiring extensive finite element analyses, highlighting its high computational efficiency and practical potential for engineering applications.

title: Deep learning-based failure rate prediction of sewer networks with uncertainty quantification under climatic variations: A Hong Kong case study
exported_title: Deep learning-based failure rate prediction of sewer networks with uncertainty quantification under climatic variations: A Hong Kong case study

metadata.abstract: Reliable operation of sewer networks (SNs) is essential for protecting public health and the environment, which makes accurate failure prediction of SNs increasingly important under pipe aging and climate change. This paper focuses on separate sewer systems in Hong Kong and develops failure rate prediction models for both sewage and stormwater systems at the regional level while considering climatic variations. First, a multi-source integrated dataset is established that incorporates historical sewer inspection records, climate conditions, regional sewer characteristics, and regional environmental properties. Second, significant factors affecting the failure rate are identified using Granger causality tests. Third, different models are developed and compared for predicting sewer failure rates. Finally, Monte Carlo Dropout and kernel density estimation are applied to quantify the predictive uncertainty of the proposed models. The results indicate that factors, such as six-month cumulative rainstorm warnings, pipe age over 30 years, and pipe diameter over 800 mm, have significant impacts on the failure rate of SNs. Additionally, the long short-term memory-based models demonstrate better predictive performance, with mean absolute percentage error values below 16.28% and 12.74% for the sewage and stormwater systems, respectively. The findings also reveal that prediction uncertainty fluctuates over time, with the sewage system exhibiting regular seasonality that reaches relative peaks during the summer, whereas the stormwater system remains more stable with minor increases in autumn and winter. This study offers a new perspective for understanding the long-term interactions between climate change and sewer failures, thereby helping decision-makers formulate proactive maintenance strategies and optimize resource allocation to enhance the resilience of SNs.

title: A degradation-enhanced physics-informed neural network for state of health estimation of lithium-ion batteries
exported_title: A degradation-enhanced physics-informed neural network for state of health estimation of lithium-ion batteries

metadata.abstract: Accurate estimation of the state of health (SOH) of lithium-ion batteries is essential for ensuring the safety and longevity of energy storage systems. However, the inherent complexity of degradation processes and the lack of directly observable indicators pose significant challenges to estimation accuracy and physical interpretability. To address these issues, this study proposes a degradation-enhanced physics-informed neural network (DE-PINN), which aims to improve SOH estimation accuracy and generalization by deeply extracting degradation-related features and reinforcing physical constraint modeling. Specifically, DE-PINN separately extracts multi-dimensional degradation information from the charging and discharging stages, constructs a dual-channel structure to accommodate stage-dependent differences, and performs collaborative modeling through information fusion. In addition, empirical degradation formulations are derived from historical data and embedded into the training process as physical consistency constraints. The degradation rate is further learned via neural networks to improve physical interpretability. A staged training strategy is employed to mitigate interference from multi-source features, thereby improving training stability and adaptability across varying operating conditions. Experimental results on same-condition and cross-condition datasets demonstrate that DE-PINN achieves superior accuracy, robustness, and generalization compared to existing methods, providing a reliable approach for physically consistent SOH modeling.

title: Physics-informed neural networks for Fokker–Planck–Kolmogorov equations corresponding to systems with tempered stable Lévy noise
exported_title: Physics-informed neural networks for Fokker–Planck–Kolmogorov equations corresponding to systems with tempered stable Lévy noise

metadata.abstract: Tempered stable Lévy noise has a greater advantage in fitting real systems due to its finite variance, compared with α-stable Lévy noise. The responses of a system under tempered stable Lévy noise are governed by a tempered fractional Fokker–Planck-Kolmogorov (FPK) equation, which is difficult to solve due to the nonlocal property of the tempered fractional derivative. In this paper, we propose the tempered fractional physics-informed neural networks (TF-PINNs) for solving the FPK equations corresponding to systems driven by tempered stable Lévy noise. Firstly, we derive the corresponding tempered fractional FPK equation by means of characteristic function, Chapman–Kolmogorov-Smoluchowski equation, and Fourier transformation. Secondly, we extend the PINNs to solve the tempered fractional FPK equation by incorporating discretized tempered fractional derivatives into the loss function of the neural network. In particular, in addition to solving the system response, the proposed TF-PINNs framework can also identify the unknown parameters in the system. Finally, three typical examples are implemented to verify the effectiveness and accuracy of the presented algorithm compared with finite difference solutions and Monte Carlo simulations.

title: Economically driven multi-dimensional strategies for enhancing substation seismic resilience: Integrating machine learning and heuristic optimization algorithms
exported_title: Economically driven multi-dimensional strategies for enhancing substation seismic resilience: Integrating machine learning and heuristic optimization algorithms

metadata.abstract: Developing seismic resilience enhancement strategies for substations requires not only improving system functionality but also integrating economic analysis to support investment decisions. This study proposes an economic-driven framework for substation seismic resilience enhancement. Spare parts inventory and equipment mobilization mechanisms are incorporated to extend a shortest-path-based repair strategy, capturing post-earthquake recovery under complex operating conditions. Typical scenarios are constructed and large sample sets are generated to train machine learning models, which serve as surrogate models for rapid resilience assessment and iterative strategy optimization. A global economic evaluation model integrates resource inputs and post-earthquake returns to quantify the cost–benefit characteristics of different strategies. Heuristic algorithms are used to optimize strategy variables and systematically analyze the evolution of economic benefits and investment preferences under complex scenarios involving varying earthquake intensities and resource constraints. The framework is demonstrated on a 220 kV substation system, and the results confirm the substantial return on investment of seismic resilience enhancement strategies. Furthermore, equipment reinforcement is shown to provide greater economic benefits than spare parts inventory, highlighting the importance of rational cost allocation. Overall, the proposed framework enables quantitative cost–benefit analysis and supports practical investment decision-making in seismic resilience enhancement.

title: Probabilistic deep learning regression framework for post-hazard hurricane wind damage assessment of buildings
exported_title: Probabilistic deep learning regression framework for post-hazard hurricane wind damage assessment of buildings

metadata.abstract: Hurricanes significantly affect coastal communities, causing substantial disruption to their socio-economic systems. Therefore, post-hurricane rapid assessment is essential for effective disaster response and recovery. Traditional human-based assessments through field reconnaissance are time-consuming, leading to delays in critical decision-making. Therefore, machine learning and deep learning have emerged as powerful alternatives enabling automated, near-real-time damage evaluation. By leveraging data from past expert-classified and systematically organized events, new models can predict damage either immediately after or even during a hurricane event. This study introduces a probabilistic deep learning regression framework that predicts component-level building damage percentages using multi-view geo-coded post-disaster imagery. Unlike conventional classification models, the proposed approach estimates continuous damage ratios for eight key envelope components, enabling more detailed and loss-relevant characterization of structural damage. A pretrained convolutional backbone is integrated with a regression head to fuse features extracted from multiple building views, while a systematic hyperparameter sensitivity analysis is performed to optimize model performance. To enhance the reliability of the developed model, uncertainty quantification was incorporated using Monte Carlo dropout and bootstrapping techniques, producing confidence intervals for each prediction. Post-disaster images from Hurricane Harvey (2017), covering 436 buildings, were used as a case study to build this model. Results demonstrate that the distribution of training data strongly influences prediction accuracy across components. Both uncertainty quantification methods performed well in capturing mean values, though they diverged in their confidence intervals. Bootstrapping offered superior uncertainty characterization, albeit with a higher computational cost compared to the Monte Carlo approach.

title: Monotonicity-constrained ordinal Gaussian process for seismic fragility modeling
exported_title: Monotonicity-constrained ordinal Gaussian process for seismic fragility modeling

metadata.abstract: This study proposes a unified ordinal Gaussian process (GP) framework that places a GP prior on latent functions and integrates three classical ordinal regression models, namely cumulative, sequential, and adjacent-category models, thereby providing a flexible nonparametric alternative to lognormal fragility models. Using the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake bridge damage dataset, eleven models are compared under a standardized training and evaluation protocol. The results show that the category specific sequential GP model, SequentialGP-CS, achieves the best overall predictive performance, reducing the ranked probability score (RPS) by 3.4%, reducing the mean binary score (MBS) by 1.2%, and improving the quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) by 6.4% relative to the ProbitOP baseline, while preventing fragility curve crossings by construction. To mitigate local fluctuations that may arise in nonlinear GP models trained on highly scattered samples, three strategies are examined to encourage monotonic fragility curves: a smoothness prior on the kernel hyperparameters, difference-based regularization of the output probabilities, and derivative-based constraints on latent functions. These strategies substantially reduce monotonicity violations, although they are accompanied by slight decreases in predictive performance; among them, the derivative-based constraint reduces the mean violation rate from 10.00% to 0.00% and yields RPS/MBS/QWK of 0.0884/0.6933/0.5870 under the monotonicity requirement.

title: Resilient groundwater flow modeling in heterogeneous porous media using mixed-form physics-informed neural networks and transfer learning
exported_title: Resilient groundwater flow modeling in heterogeneous porous media using mixed-form physics-informed neural networks and transfer learning

metadata.abstract: Reliable modeling of groundwater flow in heterogeneous porous media is crucial for the safety and risk assessment of geotechnical and underground infrastructures, where strong subsurface heterogeneity and frequent scenario updates often constrain the effectiveness of conventional numerical solvers and data-driven surrogates. This study develops a mixed-form physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) framework that simultaneously solves for hydraulic head and Darcy velocity, avoiding second-order derivatives and enhancing numerical stability under strongly heterogeneous permeability fields. Spatial heterogeneity is represented via Karhunen–Loève (KL) expansions with controllable correlation lengths, enabling systematic evaluation across statistically consistent permeability realizations. Benchmark tests involving natural gradients and pumping scenarios demonstrate that the mixed-form PINNs can provide more robust predictions under different heterogeneous permeability distributions. To enhance adaptability, transfer learning is incorporated to reuse trained representations across boundary conditions, pumping configurations, and heterogeneous fields, yielding substantial reductions in retraining cost while preserving prediction quality. The results also reveal that transfer directionality (e.g., from more heterogeneous to less heterogeneous fields) is a key factor affecting generalization efficiency. Rather than replacing conventional solvers, the proposed framework offers a flexible, mesh-free alternative for applications requiring frequent model updates or involving intricate subsurface variability, contributing to more resilient and adaptable groundwater modeling in geotechnical practice.

title: Modeling the port-shipping company game under extreme weather event impact: A multi-agent reinforcement learning-based approach
exported_title: Modeling the port-shipping company game under extreme weather event impact: A multi-agent reinforcement learning-based approach

metadata.abstract: Extreme weather events (EWEs) significantly disrupt port operations, creating highly uncertain environments that challenge effective recovery planning for both ports and shipping companies. Existing approaches, particularly those based on evolutionary game theory (EGT), typically rely on static payoff structures and myopic decision-making, limiting their ability to capture system dynamics and long-term strategic interactions. To address these limitations, this study proposes a Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) framework based on the Multi-Agent Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (MADDPG) algorithm. The framework models recovery investment decisions by port authorities and cargo transfer strategies by shipping companies as continuous, state-dependent actions that evolve over time in a stochastic recovery process. Comparative experiments against a state-dependent EGT (s-EGT) benchmark demonstrate that the proposed approach achieves superior performance in terms of cumulative returns and recovery efficiency. Specifically, the MARL framework learns forward-looking policies that explicitly account for how current decisions influence future system states, even when optimal strategies involve short-term sacrifices. In contrast, the s-EGT model fails to capture these intertemporal effects due to its limited representation of state transitions. The results show that the proposed method accelerates system recovery, improving port efficiency recovery rates by approximately 30% and reducing average vessel waiting times by nearly 80%. Furthermore, cross-scenario fine-tuning experiments indicate that the learned policies generalize well to new disruption scenarios while maintaining stable behavioral patterns. The findings highlight the potential of MARL as an effective decision-support tool for adaptive recovery management in port-shipping systems under extreme weather disruptions.

title: A graph neural network-based multi-agent reinforcement learning model for efficient power distribution system recovery after hurricanes
exported_title: A graph neural network-based multi-agent reinforcement learning model for efficient power distribution system recovery after hurricanes

metadata.abstract: The rising severity and frequency of hurricanes threaten the resilience of power distribution systems and increase the urgency of improving post-disaster recovery. Beyond capital-intensive grid hardening, fast and cost-effective restoration strategies are essential for reducing outage impacts. Effective recovery requires an optimized sequence of repairs that accounts for network topology, multi-crew coordination, and load prioritization. Traditional optimization and heuristic methods struggle to scale due to the combinatorial repair space and computational burden. To address this challenge, we propose MAGNN–A2C, a graph-based multi-agent actor–critic framework that integrates reinforcement learning, graph neural networks, and centralized training with decentralized execution to learn coordinated, topology-aware repair policies. Reinforcement learning enables reusable repair policies for rapid decision-making, the multi-agent formulation reflects parallel field crews, and graph neural networks encode system interdependencies to support scalable coordination. Evaluation on a real-world-scale case study of Galveston Island, Texas, using public infrastructure and hazard data, shows that MAGNN–A2C consistently outperforms rule-based heuristics and genetic algorithms in restoring load, reducing socioeconomic outage costs, and accelerating recovery trajectories. The learned policy also generalizes to unseen storm tracks and damage patterns, demonstrating robust performance across scenarios. These results highlight a scalable and practically deployable approach for improving distribution system restoration under increasingly severe hurricanes.

title: Flow matching-guided adaptive Markov Chain Monte Carlo with deep generative proposals for Bayesian model updating in structural health monitoring
exported_title: Flow matching-guided adaptive Markov Chain Monte Carlo with deep generative proposals for Bayesian model updating in structural health monitoring

metadata.abstract: Bayesian model updating (BMU) is essential to probabilistic parameter estimation and system identification in structural health monitoring (SHM). Although Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods are widely regarded as the gold standard for BMU, their high computational cost often limits practical application to large-scale engineering structures. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a novel BMU framework termed Flow Matching-Guided MCMC (FM-G-MCMC). The framework integrates a multi-chain adaptive MCMC scheme with a deep generative model through an iterative cycle of local sampling, flow training, and global proposal generation. Specifically, local samples generated by gradient-based MCMC kernels are used to train and fine-tune a continuous normalizing flow (CNF) which is learned using flow matching. The trained CNF is then embedded into an independent Metropolis–Hastings kernel to provide efficient global proposals that enable non-local exploration of the parameter space. Accepted samples from both local and global moves are aggregated to adaptively refine the CNF and local proposals in a bidirectional manner, allowing the two components to co-evolve toward the target posterior. Three engineering examples, involving an 18-story steel frame, a steel pedestrian bridge, and an experimental study, demonstrate that the proposed method achieves more accurate parameter estimates with substantially reduced computational cost than conventional MCMC.

title: Credible long-term degradation prediction for proton exchange membrane fuel cell: A physics-informed neural network with conformal prediction approach
exported_title: Credible long-term degradation prediction for proton exchange membrane fuel cell: A physics-informed neural network with conformal prediction approach

metadata.abstract: The insufficient durability of Proton Exchange Membrane Fuel Cells (PEMFCs) hinders their commercialization, making accurate long-term prognosis essential. However, existing methods struggle to balance physical interpretability, accuracy, and uncertainty quantification. This paper proposes a novel framework, Physics-Informed Neural Network with Conformal Prediction (PINNCP). First, to address black-box limitations, we develop a gray-box modeling paradigm that integrates physical mechanisms with data. Instead of directly fitting voltage curves, a neural network adaptively learns the meta-parameters of a generalized power-law model. By embedding electrochemical equations into the loss function, the method accurately inverts and decouples key internal physical states without parameter labels. Second, to quantify risks, a physics-informed calibrated conformal prediction strategy is introduced. By calibrating nonconformity scores with physical constraints, it generates prediction intervals with strict statistical guarantees and physical consistency. Extensive validation under static, quasi-dynamic, and dynamic conditions demonstrates that PINNCP accurately predicts long-term voltage degradation trajectories and provides high-quality confidence intervals. Furthermore, by leveraging extracted physical parameters, the method enables degradation prediction transfer across same-type PEMFCs, significantly enhancing practical applicability.

title: Weather-aware anomaly detection for ship behavior based on Transformer
exported_title: Weather-aware anomaly detection for ship behavior based on transformer

metadata.abstract: Anomaly detection in ship behavior is crucial for maritime safety and intelligent shipping systems. However, the weather conditions surrounding the ship are typically neglected by existing anomaly detection methods. In this study, a Weather-Aware Ship Anomaly Detection (WASAD) model is proposed to enhance ship anomaly detection by incorporating real weather conditions from ERA5 reanalysis data aligned with AIS trajectories. First, AIS trajectories are spatiotemporally aligned with ERA5 weather data using cubic spline interpolation, followed by bilinear interpolation. The data are subsequently mapped into high-dimensional embeddings. A gated fusion module is then utilized to adaptively adjust the weights of environmental influences. Complex long-term spatiotemporal dependencies within the behavior patterns are captured by a six-layer Transformer encoder. Finally, anomalies are precisely identified by evaluating context-modulated anomaly scores. The model is validated using real-world AIS data combined with ERA5 data. Under all weather conditions, an anomaly detection accuracy exceeding 98% is achieved by the proposed framework, and the False Positive Rate is reduced to approximately 1.2%. This framework could be used to enhance intelligent maritime surveillance, thereby improving the safety and reliability of autonomous navigation systems.

title: Physics-informed shield attitude prediction and uncertainty-aware safety regulation: conformal-calibrated robust control barrier functions
exported_title: Physics-informed shield attitude prediction and uncertainty-aware safety regulation: conformal-calibrated robust control barrier functions

metadata.abstract: Accurate shield-attitude prediction and reliable safety regulation are essential for intelligent tunneling, yet existing methods often lack physical consistency, calibrated uncertainty, and effective uncertainty propagation into safety control. This study proposes an integrated framework combining a Physics-Informed State Space Model (PI-SSM), trajectory-level conformal prediction, and a Conformal-Calibrated Robust Control Barrier Function (CC-RCBF). The PI-SSM adopts physically meaningful state-space initialization and non-invasive Generalized Spring-Mass-Damper (G-SMD) calibration, while a physics-anchored multi-horizon structure mitigates recursive error accumulation. Predictive uncertainty is quantified using a validation-weighted deep ensemble and calibrated by trajectory-level conformal prediction with causal sequential adaptation. The calibrated uncertainty is further incorporated into an energy-based CC-RCBF for actuator-constrained safety filtering. Using 50,857 operational samples from the Qingdao Second Sub-sea Tunnel, the proposed model achieves one-step R2 values of 0.9783 and 0.9789, and retains 0.9504 and 0.9173 at a 20-step horizon. The predictive performance of the PI-SSM is further validated using operational data from another shield tunneling alignment within the same project. G-SMD calibration reduces the physical residual by approximately three orders of magnitude, while CC-RCBF eliminates observed physical-limit violations in reduced-order stress testing and increases the minimum clearance to 0.92 mm. The framework is further integrated into a shield-attitude safety decision-support platform.

title: Can concrete pumping pressure be predicted from mixture composition? Insights from machine learning on full-scale pumping experiments
exported_title: Can concrete pumping pressure be predicted from mixture composition? Insights from machine learning on full-scale pumping experiments

metadata.abstract: Pumping pressure loss is a key technical indicator in concrete pumping. In this study, a machine learning-based model was developed to predict pumping pressure from concrete mixture composition and operational parameters. A total of 410 full-scale coiled pipeline pumping tests were conducted, covering a wide range of flow rates (1.8–18.9 L/s), pumping distances (325–1044 m), and concrete strength grades (C30–C100). A hybrid modeling strategy combining unsupervised clustering and supervised learning was adopted. Specifically, density-based clustering was first employed to group the data by feature similarity, and the resulting cluster labels were incorporated into the supervised learning model as additional input features. Subsequently, Euclidean distance analysis, grid search, and five-fold cross-validation were used to optimize the hyperparameters of both the clustering and the Extremely Randomized Trees regression model. The developed model exhibited good prediction accuracy (R2 > 0.9). SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) analysis was further applied to reveal the influence of individual mixture parameters on the predicted pumping pressure. Publicly available full-scale pumping data from the literature were used to evaluate the applicability of the model, and key factors influencing cross-project prediction accuracy were analyzed. Finally, a strategy for cross-project application of the pressure prediction model was proposed. This study highlights the potential of using mixture composition to predict concrete pumping pressure and provides insights for the optimized design of pumpable concrete and pumping operations.

title: An intelligent optimization and comprehensive performance decision-making method for ECC mix proportion based on machine learning
exported_title: An intelligent optimization and comprehensive performance decision-making method for ECC mix proportion based on machine learning

metadata.abstract: Engineered Cementitious Composite (ECC) has been increasingly adopted in frame columns due to its excellent mechanical properties. However, in engineering practice, how to quickly select an appropriate mix design that balances performance and cost-effectiveness remains a challenge. In this study, a machine learning and mechanical performance-driven selection method was established. First, a high-fidelity dataset comprising 240 sets of data with 18 input variables was constructed. Next, hyperparameter tuning of the algorithmic model was performed using random search combined with Fourier optimization, followed by Pearson correlation analysis, prediction accuracy evaluation, and Shapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis on the dataset. Finally, multiple possible mix designs were generated based on the prediction model and the target concrete compressive strength. These were sequentially processed through a constructed mechanical model, the weight coefficient allocation and normalization calculation process, and a comprehensive performance index model, ultimately obtaining the optimal mix design. A case study was presented to demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed method. In the prediction model, the CatBoost algorithm model developed achieved high prediction accuracy for ECC performance, with R-values of 0.97, 0.95, and 0.91 for compressive strength, tensile strength, and tensile strain, respectively.Factors affecting ECC's mechanical properties mainly include the water-to-binder ratio, cement, silica fume, and fiber fracture elongation, with their average SHAP values over twice those of other inputs. Additionally, a design case validates the rationality of the design method proposed in this study. This study can provide guidance for the broader application of ECC in practical engineering.

title: Coal and Municipal Solid Waste Incineration Bottom Ash in Concrete: Governing Mechanisms and Data-Driven Synthesis
exported_title: Coal and municipal solid waste incineration bottom ash in concrete: Governing mechanisms and data-driven synthesis

metadata.abstract: The sustainable utilization of bottom ash in cementitious materials requires understanding how source characteristics and replacement function govern engineering performance. This review comparatively evaluates coal bottom ash (CBA) and municipal solid waste incineration bottom ash (IBA) by integrating mechanistic literature synthesis with interpretable machine learning. Their physical, chemical, and mineralogical characteristics and performance as cement and fine-aggregate replacements are assessed to synthesize relationships among intrinsic properties, processing conditions, and concrete behavior. A curated database containing 630 experimental observations was assembled, of which 493 BA-containing observations formed four application-specific datasets—CBA-Cement, CBA-Fine, IBA-Cement, and IBA-Fine—for analysis using Random Forest, XGBoost, and CatBoost. Mixture-level and reference-grouped testing distinguished within-domain predictability from cross-study transferability, while SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) identified influential variables and directional relationships. All four domains exhibited strong within-domain predictability, whereas cross-study transferability was consistently greater for CBA than IBA across the three algorithms, revealing a substantially larger generalization gap for IBA. Curing age and water-to-binder ratio were dominant factors in CBA systems, whereas IBA performance showed stronger dependence on application-specific mixture and material characteristics. Cross-algorithm SHAP analysis further showed that several dominant associations were consistent with mechanisms established in the experimental literature. In general, CBA and IBA should not be treated as interchangeable resources; their performance must be evaluated according to both ash source and replacement function. The integrated framework demonstrates how interpretable machine learning can complement mechanistic synthesis while explicitly assessing cross-study transferability.
keywords: Municipal solid waste incineration bottom ash

title: A transfer learning-driven paradigm for understanding cryogenic freezing mechanisms in low water/binder cement-based composites
exported_title: A transfer learning-driven paradigm for understanding cryogenic freezing mechanisms in low water/binder cement-based composites

metadata.abstract: Data scarcity and dispersion constrain the accurate assessment of cryogenic concrete performance and impede the investigation of its microstructural evolution. This study first developed a physics-informed transfer learning framework to predict low water/binder cement-based composites (LWCC) behavior across a wide temperature range and reveal coupled macro–micro freezing mechanisms. The results demonstrated that transfer learning, by integrating hydration and freezing features, effectively overcame data scarcity and enabled accurate prediction of LWCC low-temperature performance (R2 > 0.90). The model exhibited self-adaptive capability, extending its applicable temperature range to be extended from the training range of 0 to −80°C down to −196°C. Based on the data-driven model, a freezing model was proposed, identifying strength gain, damage–densification balance, secondary strengthening, and interfacial debonding stages, with transitions influenced by w/b ratio and solid skeleton structure. This work achieves AI-driven precise prediction of cryogenic concrete, offering insights into material design and freezing mechanisms under extreme conditions.

title: A photometric stereo and Vision Transformer-based framework for automated air void analysis in hardened concrete
exported_title: A photometric stereo and Vision Transformer-based framework for automated air void analysis in hardened concrete

metadata.abstract: Air void analysis in hardened concrete typically requires the Linear Traverse Method (Procedure A) or the Modified Point-Count Method (Procedure B), as described in ASTM C457, to assess the content and distribution of entrapped and entrained air voids. These parameters are critical for assessing freeze–thaw resistance, workability, and mechanical properties. Conventional approaches rely on manual sampling and inspection by trained technicians, which are not only time-consuming and labor-intensive but also inherently subjective due to operator-dependent interpretations. This study proposes a novel framework integrating Photometric Stereo and Vision Transformer models to automate air void analysis with enhanced speed, accuracy, and generalizability. By leveraging a newly designed photometric stereo system and a computer vision-based image processing pipeline, the proposed method addresses key limitations in existing techniques, such as the inability to detect shallow or deep voids, incomplete boundary identification, and challenges in distinguishing air voids from aggregates. The framework seamlessly integrates image acquisition, recognition, extraction, and analysis, completing the entire process within approximately 10 min, excluding initial specimen preparation. When compared to current automated petrographic analysis methods, this approach achieves state-of-the-art precision, with mean accuracies of 97.970% for air void content and 97.176% for spacing factor, while eliminating the need for surface treatments or extensive model training. Furthermore, the study reports a comprehensive sensitivity analysis of parameter selection in Procedures A and B, offering deeper insights into ASTM C457 specifications. The proposed solution significantly reduces time and labor costs associated with air void analysis, enhances result reliability, and demonstrates potential for broader applications in micro-scale 3D surface reconstruction and property evaluation.

title: Green strength characterization of 3D printable mortar using spherical penetration tests and Bayesian inverse modeling with an artificial neural network surrogate
exported_title: Green strength characterization of 3D printable mortar using spherical penetration tests and Bayesian inverse modeling with an artificial neural network surrogate

metadata.abstract: Accurate identification of the early-age mechanical properties of fresh cementitious material is essential for predicting stability of concrete 3D printed elements. This study presents a hybrid experimental numerical methodology for determining key constitutive parameters of 3D printable mortar. Within the framework of the Mohr Coulomb (MC) plasticity model, the time evolution of Young's modulus, cohesion, internal friction angle, and dilatancy angle is characterized. Following the proposed methodology, the spherical penetration test is conducted at different early hydration stages. An inverse analysis based on artificial intelligence is then carried out to determine the concrete properties. For this purpose, the synthetic dataset of the penetration test responses is generated through finite element (FE) simulations using Abaqus to train an artificial neural network (ANN). The accuracy of this ANN based surrogate model to derive the force depth curve of penetration test and its high efficiency to solve the inverse problem are demonstrated. The developed methodology enables fast, simple, and reproducible mechanical characterization of fresh mortar, offering a practical tool for early-stage material calibration in both laboratory and on-site applications.

title: Deep learning-based thermal motion estimation and lay-up reconstruction framework towards machine-independent real-time AFP process monitoring and inspection
exported_title: Deep learning-based thermal motion estimation and lay-up reconstruction framework towards machine-independent real-time AFP process monitoring and inspection

metadata.abstract: Automated Fiber Placement (AFP) continues to advance composite manufacturing, yet real-world throughput and quality assurance remain constrained by labor-intensive inspection and the absence of automated, in-situ monitoring solutions. Existing methods are partial–confined to local, frame-level analysis lacking global motion context required for comprehensive lay-up inspection, or reliant on machine-coupled data that introduces synchronization errors and hinders generalizability. We present a novel, machine-independent framework for real-time, motion-aware AFP monitoring and inspection. We introduce ThermoRAFT-AFP, a custom deep learning-based motion estimation core, tailored with AFP-specific augmentations and process-aware runtime optimizations to enable stable and precise thermal flow tracking. These estimates power a two-stage reconstruction pipeline that first stitches course-wise thermal mosaics, then assembles them into ply-level, high-fidelity, and interpretable laminate visualizations–recovering global motion context. We validate the framework on a large-scale, diverse AFP thermal dataset comprising over 13,000 frames with varying lay-up conditions, speed profiles, and defect types. A comprehensive analysis of motion accuracy, runtime efficiency, and deployment robustness shows that ThermoRAFT-AFP achieves state-of-the-art subpixel accuracy with a mean RMSE below 5mm/s and relative cumulative drift under 0.1%, all while operating at 25fps on a commodity CPU. The system maintains robust performance under severe thermal noise and reliably generalizes across diverse process conditions. Qualitative evaluation against realistic AFP case studies highlights the framework’s capabilities for thermal anomaly visualization and tracking, inter-layer thermal behavior propagation analysis, and enabling operator-informed decision-making. These findings establish a reliable foundation for next-generation intelligent AFP process monitoring and quality inspection systems.

title: Optimization analysis for hole diameter consistency in BCF/PEEK and PEEK stacks based on a multi-scale thermo-mechanical coupled model and XGBoost algorithm
exported_title: Optimization analysis for hole diameter consistency in BCF/PEEK and PEEK stacks based on a multi-scale thermo-mechanical coupled model and XGBoost algorithm

metadata.abstract: This study introduces a novel step-variable parameter optimization method to optimize drilling parameters for hole diameter consistency. First, a comprehensive multi-scale thermo-mechanical coupled finite element (FE) model was developed for drilling Braided Carbon Fiber-reinforced Polyether Ether Ketone (BCF/PEEK) and Polyether Ether Ketone (PEEK) stacks, incorporating a newly proposed modified micro-mechanics of failure criterion. Subsequently, extensive simulation datasets were leveraged to train an XGBoost model. GridSearchCV was employed for hyperparameter optimization to enable a detailed analysis of the relative importance of various process parameters in inducing stepped hole defects. Finally, a Taguchi orthogonal experimental design was implemented in variable parameter drilling experiments, experimentally validating the XGBoost optimization outcomes and conclusively determining the optimal parameter combination. The results demonstrate that the proposed multi-scale FE model accurately predicts drilling morphology and precisely quantifies thrust force and temperature field. A key finding is that the stacking sequence significantly impacts thermal deformation and hole quality: a BCF/PEEK→PEEK sequence reduces thermal deformation and enhances hole diameter consistency. Specifically, the identified optimal parameters are a step position of −0.5 mm, a spindle speed of 2000 r/min and a feed rate of 40 mm/min for BCF/PEEK, and a spindle speed of 5000 r/min and a feed rate of 30 mm/min for PEEK. Experimental validation confirmed that this optimized parameter set successfully controls the hole diameter difference within 0.02 mm, achieving a remarkable improvement in hole diameter consistency.

title: Deep learning-powered composite foam smart glove with cross-dimensional conductive networks for sign language recognition
exported_title: Deep learning-powered composite foam smart glove with cross-dimensional conductive networks for sign language recognition

metadata.abstract: The development of wearable sensor-based sign language recognition systems has become a solution to facilitate effective communication among hearing-impaired groups, but achieving high integration, sign language standardization, and anti-environmental interference remains challenging. Here, we design a smart glove system for real-time sign language interpretation based on a composite foam with a cross-dimensional conductive network, integrating flexible switches, pressure sensors, custom miniaturized circuits, and deep learning modules. The sensor exhibits electromagnetic shielding, thermal management, and antibacterial capabilities, enhancing the smart glove's adaptability to the external environment. The elastic conductive framework of the foam allows the system to realize the start/stop function and fast response to gestures. In addition, a deep learning model of multi-component collaboration and mechanism fusion is constructed, along with the establishment of a comprehensive set of sign language rules, which realizes 99.4 % accurate recognition of 26 letters through only three pressure sensors. Overall, our proposed strategy provides a new way for smart gloves to work stably in harsh environments, and is expected to eliminate communication barriers among hearing-impaired groups due to sign language diversity and cultural differences.

title: Deep-learning-based image-driven modelling of woven ceramic matrix composites: incorporating real void morphology and damage-induced behaviour
exported_title: Deep-learning-based image-driven modelling of woven ceramic matrix composites: incorporating real void morphology and damage-induced behaviour

metadata.abstract: An image-driven method for generating high-fidelity finite element models for woven ceramic matrix composites is presented in this paper. The model incorporates the real morphologies of fibre tows, matrix, and inter-tow voids. With high-resolution X-ray CT scans of plain woven Cf/SiC composites, a deep-learning-based image segmentation method was employed to accurately segment the fibre tows from the CT images. A convex hull-based algorithm, alongside a thorough tow trajectory tracking method, was developed to handle fibre tow intersections and categorise the cross-sections of the fibre tows in the segmented images. For void identification, a rapid approach based on the watershed transform was implemented. The resulting geometric model demonstrates a high degree of morphological fidelity with the 3D CT image of the material. Furthermore, a progressive damage-induced nonlinear stress-strain relation for fibre tows was developed and incorporated into the CT image-driven finite element model. The predicted stress-strain curve has excellent correlations with experimental results, demonstrating higher accuracy compared to the ideal model, and therefore more accurately reflects the stress distributions.

title: Delamination-informed lifecycle decisions: A dielectric and machine learning framework for composite sorting and recycling
exported_title: Delamination-informed lifecycle decisions: A dielectric and machine learning framework for composite sorting and recycling

metadata.abstract: Composite materials are widely used in aerospace, marine, and automotive sectors due to their high strength-to-weight ratio and durability. However, their long-term reliability can be compromised by damage accumulation. Specifically, delamination initiation serves as a precursor to structural failure, which is often difficult to detect during damage inspection. Identifying and sorting delamination initiation in samples not only increases operational safety while providing critical information for end-of-life decisions, which influences both the service life extension value and the efficiency of fiber extraction during recycling. This research addresses two challenges: (1) developing a nondestructive, ex-situ framework to sort composite materials based on damage severity, particularly delamination, and (2) understanding how damage in composites influences resin removal during pyrolysis. Both experimental work and finite element analysis were performed to predict critical stress levels that are associated with delamination onset. Based on these results, three loading levels 50 %, 75 %, and 90 % of maximum stress, were selected for controlled experiments, generating composite samples with varying extents of damage for machine learning model training. Microscopic imaging of these samples confirmed the damage progression from matrix cracking to delamination, validating the computational predictions. We explored supervised machine learning using dielectric measurements to classify damage states. Preliminary results show an artificial neural network can identify early delamination which is a potential precursor to failure, with 94.44 % accuracy on our dataset. A parallel investigation into the effect of damage severity on pyrolysis recycling showed that heavily delaminated samples required significantly less energy for comparable matrix removal than undamaged samples.

title: Early fatigue failure detection in composites using autoencoder-based anomaly detection
exported_title: Early fatigue failure detection in composites using autoencoder-based anomaly detection

metadata.abstract: Despite the widespread adoption of composite materials across various industries, accurately evaluating their durability—particularly under fatigue loading—remains a major challenge. A key difficulty lies in the substantial scatter in fatigue life among seemingly identical specimens. This variability elevates the risk of sudden, catastrophic failures and necessitates conservative, schedule-based maintenance plans that are designed around worst-case scenarios. This study presents a novel approach to identify composite specimens with short fatigue lives at the early stage of loading by integrating piezo-resistivity-based structural health monitoring (SHM) with autoencoder-based anomaly detection techniques. Glass fiber–epoxy composites, made electrically conductive by incorporating carbon nanotubes (CNTs), were subjected to fatigue loading until failure, while their electrical resistance (ER) was continuously monitored. The ER data from the early stage of loading were extracted and used to train and optimize autoencoders to detect early fatigue failure (i.e., short-life specimens). The results demonstrated an F1 score of 95 % and an accuracy of 97 % in correctly identifying short-life specimens, underscoring the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

title: The defect quantification in additive manufacturing composites using fused infrared thermography and artificial intelligence
exported_title: The defect quantification in additive manufacturing composites using fused infrared thermography and artificial intelligence

metadata.abstract: Carbon fiber reinforced composites (CFRC) are widely used in various fields. However, internal defects formed during manufacturing can compromise structural integrity. This study utilized additive manufacturing to fabricate CFRC specimens with predefined internal defects. The specimens were subsequently analyzed through active infrared thermography (IRT) to characterize defect-induced thermal differences. Under thermal excitation, the defect area exhibited a prominent temperature increase compared to non-defective regions. During cooling, the temperature in the defect area underwent two-stage attenuation: an initial rapid decrease, primarily due to convective heat transfer, followed by a slower decline as heat diffused internally from defective to non-defective zones. As the thermal difference between the specimen surface and the ambient air diminished, convective cooling weakened, and the system gradually approached overall thermal equilibrium, asymptotically converging toward ambient temperature. Based on thermal imaging, an improved deep learning method was proposed to detect defects in CFRC. The raw thermal images were first preprocessed to facilitate the extraction of infrared defect features. The processed datasets were then trained to identify defect characteristics until high prediction accuracy was achieved. The method accurately predicts defect information, including contour, type, and area. Experimental results demonstrated excellent performance, with mean average precision (mAP) values of 99.3 % for both instance segmentation and image classification, and a defect area error within 6 %. This approach presents an efficient, accurate, and cost-effective solution for rapid defect geometry and dimension assessment in composites.

title: A piezoelectric micro-pyramid array sensor based on PVDF/WS2 nanosheets for high-precision deep learning-assisted pattern recognition
exported_title: A piezoelectric micro-pyramid array sensor based on PVDF/WS2 nanosheets for high-precision deep learning-assisted pattern recognition

metadata.abstract: The piezoelectric pressure sensors, which have emerged as core components of intelligent sensing systems, exhibit significant application values in flexible electronics and human-machine interaction. In this study, we innovatively developed a micro-pyramid array sensor (MPAS) based on PVDF/WS2 nanosheets (NSs) nanocomposites. The PVDF/WS2 NSs nanocomposites were prepared by using the solid-state shear milling (S3M) technology and then elaborately integrated into a precisely designed micro-pyramidal architecture through microinjection molding (μIM) strategy. Under the very strong shear stress fields of μIM process, the spontaneous alignment of PVDF molecular chains and WS2 NSs along the flow direction has been achieved. The fabricated sensing microdevices exhibit high sensitivity (128 mV/kPa) within a 10 N pressure range, along with 1 mm spatial resolution comparable to the level of human tactile perception. Furthermore, based on fabrication of the above microdevice, we also established an intelligent recognition system through combining multi-stage signal processing algorithms with a convolutional neural network (CNN). The resulting MPAS could achieve 100 % classification accuracy for three English letters. By setting an intensity threshold for the sensor arrays, the constructed recognition system could achieve 237 (≈1.37 × 1011) password combinations, which is equivalent to the security level of an 11-digit decimal password lock system. Such an interesting and smart approach has demonstrated a unique security authentication methodology for intelligent electronic devices, and exhibits the promising application prospects in artificial intelligence-based precision recognition systems and advanced human-machine interaction interfaces.

title: A data-driven synergistic optimization framework for thermo-mechanical properties of oriented fiber-reinforced aerogel composites
exported_title: A data-driven synergistic optimization framework for thermo-mechanical properties of oriented fiber-reinforced aerogel composites

metadata.abstract: In thermal protection systems particularly for aerospace and energy applications, the development of thermal insulation materials that simultaneously maintain mechanical robustness and dimensional stability under extreme conditions remains a challenge. Although oriented fiber-reinforced silica aerogel composites exhibit superior thermal and mechanical performances, their further application is hindered by the intrinsic trade-offs between microstructure and macroscopic properties. To address this limitation, this work proposes a data-driven synergistic optimization framework for oriented fiber-reinforced silica aerogel composites, facilitated by multiscale structure optimization to achieve a multifunctional integration. A nanoscale-informed thermo-mechanical theoretical model based on the real nanostructure of silica aerogels was developed to quantitatively correlate the density with thermal conductivity, elastic modulus, and thermal expansion coefficient. Furthermore, a hierarchically coupled multiscale modeling strategy for fiber-reinforced aerogel composites was proposed to achieve nano-micro-macro matched thermo-mechanical numerical predictions and experimentally validated using samples prepared in-house. We developed a multi-objective optimization approach that combines a finite-element (FE) database with an artificial neural network (ANN) surrogate and the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II). The integrated optimization delivers exceptional properties: ultralow thermal conductivity (0.0295 W m−1 K−1), high elastic modulus (24.06 MPa), and low thermal expansion coefficient (4.87 × 10−6 K−1), at a fiber volume fraction of 12.2% and an orientation angle of 18.5°. This work can resolve the thermo-mechanical performance–microstructure trade-offs, advancing the collaborative optimization of oriented fiber-reinforced aerogel composites. The present data-driven optimization framework could be straightforward for more general multifunctional thermal insulation composites.

title: 3D printing of machine learning-optimized continuous fiber-reinforced smart molds with a filament-withdrawal demolding strategy for extreme forming
exported_title: 3D printing of machine learning-optimized continuous fiber-reinforced smart molds with a filament-withdrawal demolding strategy for extreme forming

metadata.abstract: The fabrication of complex hollow structures with variable cross-sections and curvatures remains challenging due to the limited deformability and poor demolding performance of conventional rigid molds. This study proposes a novel strategy that integrates 3D printing of continuous fiber-reinforced smart mold with a dimension-reduction wire-drawing demolding method. A photothermal dual-crosslinked polymer network was developed to enable reversible stiffness modulation, ensuring high rigidity during molding and flexibility during demolding. To optimize fabrication performance, a machine learning framework based on gradient boosting regression was employed to model and analyze the influence of key printing parameters on both mechanical strength and dimensional accuracy. Using this approach, smart mold with a bending strength of 620.71 MPa and a printing error of 2.46 % were successfully fabricated. The method was further validated through the forming and demolding of representative geometries, including dumbbell-shaped and variable-section components. Results confirm the feasibility and robustness of the approach under extreme forming conditions. This digitally driven, material–process–structure integrated solution offers broad application potential for the precision manufacturing of complex hollow composite structures in solid rocket motors, aerospace engineering, and architectural fabrication.

title: Electrostatic field-induced core-shell nanofibers with boosted triboelectric performance for human-machine interaction and machine learning-assisted prosthetic training
exported_title: Electrostatic field-induced core-shell nanofibers with boosted triboelectric performance for human-machine interaction and machine learning-assisted prosthetic training

metadata.abstract: With the demands of medical and health physiological monitoring, triboelectric nanogenerator (TENG) based self-powered wearable electronics have been dramatically developed for real-time dynamic monitoring, while large-scale deployment is fundamentally constrained by inherent limitations in energy output efficiency. Herein, utilizing the directional dipole cluster charge-couple transfer effect in a high-voltage field to fabricate a biocompatible ZnAl layer double hydroxides (LDH)@polylactic acid (PLA) core-shell composite nanofibers, tribo-charge production, migration and storage processes are improved. ZnAl LDH is chosen as the inducer to regulate electronic structure, construct charge migrated pathway as well as charge storge sites, presenting the excellent mechanical-electric converted capability. Output voltage, current, transferred charge density, and powered density reach 160.75 V, 11.03 μA, 73.3 μC m−2, and 6.31 W m−2, respectively, voltage also exhibit the great stability over the 10000 cycles. Moreover, a modular sensor array has been engineered to enable precise actuation and autonomous control of robotic manipulator. Simultaneously, based on the triboelectric performance of ZnAl LDH@PLA nanofiber, a smart insole is self-designed to gather movements sensing signals. Combining with machine learning, it also could accurately identify various abnormal gaits, highlighting the potential in the medical diagnosis and rehabilitation training fields, especially in adaptation period of prostheses for amputee patient.

title: Identification and optimization of mechanical characteristics in graphene-reinforced aluminum matrix composites based on artificial intelligence
exported_title: Identification and optimization of mechanical characteristics in graphene-reinforced aluminum matrix composites based on artificial intelligence

metadata.abstract: The advancement of modern composite materials, especially Graphene-reinforced Aluminium Matrix Composites (GAMCs), has sparked a great deal of interest due to great mechanical properties. Possibly due to GAMC's high intrinsic strength, surface area, and better heat and electrical conduction capability, research has identified many industries such as aviation, automotive, and electronics, that use GAMCs. The integration of graphene into aluminium increases mechanical performance due to a combination of load transfer and grain refinement through the Hall-Petch effect, and Orowan looping. This research aims to improve GAMC's mechanical properties prediction using data preprocessing, and predictive modeling methods. The Sequential Average Generative Discrimination Neural Network (SAGDNN) is used to classify microstructure images achieving 98 % accuracy. The crested porcupine optimizer is used for optimization as the speed and convergence with accuracy outperformed the other optimizers. Global Coordinate-based SHapley Additive explanations (GC-SHAP) is used to interpret the SAGDNN model. The results showed that the data generated using the SAGDNN is valuable and contributes toward the accurate prediction of mechanical properties with a mean prediction error of less than 2 %. The models presented in this research are important for identifying and optimizing the GAMC composite materials.

title: A diverse and explainable machine learning framework for multi-property prediction in nanoparticle-enhanced carbon fiber/epoxy composites
exported_title: A diverse and explainable machine learning framework for multi-property prediction in nanoparticle-enhanced carbon fiber/epoxy composites

metadata.abstract: The incorporation of nanoparticles into carbon fiber/epoxy reinforced composites has emerged as an effective strategy to overcome the inherent brittleness of epoxy matrices and to enhance multi-modal mechanical performance. However, the complex relationship between nanoparticle characteristics, processing conditions, and resulting microstructures makes reliable property prediction exceptionally challenging. In this study, a diverse and interpretable machine learning (ML) framework is developed to predict three key mechanical properties of nanoparticle-modified CF/epoxy composites: tensile modulus, flexural modulus, and interlaminar shear strength (ILSS). Three comprehensive datasets comprising 952 experimental results were compiled from 74 peer-reviewed publications, covering a wide range of nanoparticle types, sizes, weight fractions (wt%), fiber orientations, and processing conditions.
