Six regression algorithms: Random Forest (RF), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Gradient Boosting (GB), Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGB), AdaBoost (AB), and LightGBM (LGBM) were systematically compared to ensure robust generalization. The results demonstrate that RF achieved the highest predictive accuracy for tensile modulus (R2 = 0.983), while KNN outperformed other models for flexural modulus (R2 = 0.994) and ILSS (R2 = 0.939). To enhance interpretability, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and partial dependency plots (PDPs) were employed. For tensile modulus, analysis revealed a distinct thermal sensitivity where stiffness remained stable up to a post-curing temperature of ∼70 °C before declining sharply due to matrix degradation. These analyses also revealed that while nanoparticle agglomeration diminishes benefits beyond ∼1 wt% and 20–40 nm size ranges, thermal processing and fiber layouts play equally critical roles. Post-curing temperatures exceeding 100 °C were found to sharply enhance flexural modulus, while ILSS performance peaked at curing temperatures near 100 °C. The proposed ML framework not only delivers accurate and generalizable predictions but also provides mechanistic insight for tailoring nanoparticle-reinforced CF/epoxy composites with enhanced structural performance.

title: Digital twin for synchronous full-field deformation reconstruction of composite trusses under dynamic load
exported_title: Digital twin for synchronous full-field deformation reconstruction of composite trusses under dynamic load

metadata.abstract: To ensure the safety and normal service of composite trusses under dynamic loads, synchronous full-field deformation monitoring is urgently needed to make structural status assessment possible, and striking a balance between efficiency and accuracy is the core problem. This paper realizes the digital twin for synchronous full-field deformation reconstruction of composite trusses under dynamic load, which mainly includes two contents. On the one hand, considering that the number and placement of sensors are the key factors affecting the efficiency and accuracy of full-field deformation reconstruction, research on the sensor placement mechanism is conducted. Spatial strain distribution analysis across multiple-order modes and static/dynamic simulated strains revealed significant reconstruction accuracy variations by measurement location: longitudinal beams outperform triangular beams, near-joint regions outperform middle of the beam, and fixed end regions outperform free end regions. On the other hand, to improve the accuracy of full-field deformation reconstruction, an adaptive regularization method is studied. First, the correlation between the reconstruction residual of the most relevant strain and the accuracy of the full-field deformation reconstruction is revealed. Then, the objective function is constructed, and the gradient algorithm is used to achieve rapid adaptive determination of the regularization coefficient. To validate the proposed method, an experiment is carried out on a representative composite truss, and finally the synchronous visualization of the digital twin full-field deformation is achieved with a time consumption of 0.007s/frame and the accuracy is 91.09 %. Based on the proposed sensor placement mechanism, the number of sensors can be significantly reduced by 92.21 % with similar accuracy of full-field deformation reconstruction. Meanwhile, the accuracy of the full-field deformation reconstruction is improved by 18.33 % compared with the non-regularized method. The reconstruction accuracies under different loads or in different directions are also validated. The above comparison indicates that the proposed method can balance the efficiency and accuracy of the full-field deformation reconstruction, thereby laying a foundation for subsequent system state assessment and other related tasks.

title: Atomistic decoding of multifaceted crack-initiated degradation mechanisms in high-temperature solder interconnects for AI-powered microelectronics
exported_title: Atomistic decoding of multifaceted crack-initiated degradation mechanisms in high-temperature solder interconnects for AI-powered microelectronics

metadata.abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) computing power demands interconnect technologies capable of enduring extreme thermal conditions in high-power electronic packaging. This study presents a comprehensive atomic-scale investigation of degradation mechanisms in high-temperature solder joints on AlN HTCC substrates for AI hardware infrastructure. Through Aberration-corrected Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy, we systematically characterized three distinct failure modes: (1) Interfacial delamination at Sn–Pb phase boundaries through thermal stress accumulation due to CTE mismatch, leading to progressive creep deformation and crack initiation. Short-range Sn diffusion was also witnessed which exhibited dependence on both local stress state and limited solubility of Sn in Pb. (2) Interlayer fracture between (NixAu1-x)3Sn4 and (NiyAu1-y)3Sn4 multi-stacked IMC architectures driven by synergistic effects of (i) CTE mismatch which induced interfacial thermal stress, and (ii) modulus and hardness disparities which created localized stress intensification factors. The actual thermal stress reached 37.781 MPa according to quantitative calculation. At the atomic scale, crack initiation proceeds via progressive lattice distortion driven by accumulated atomic displacements, which intensifies and ultimately evolves into lattice disruption once the local stability threshold is exceeded. (3) Intralayer grain-boundary cracking of IMC crystallites due to step formation under the combined effect of Au segregation and crystallographic growth misorientation, with Crack II induced deformation and lattice disruption at weakened triple junction serving as preferential nucleation sites that accelerated propagation. These insights bridge the gap between nanoscale material behavior and macroscale reliability requirements in next-generation computing systems, provide a fundamental framework for developing robust interconnect systems.

title: Artificial neural network-assisted design of 3D printed moth-eye inspired metastructure for broadband microwave absorption and infrared stealth
exported_title: Artificial neural network-assisted design of 3D printed moth-eye inspired metastructure for broadband microwave absorption and infrared stealth

metadata.abstract: The development of lightweight electromagnetic wave-absorbing materials with integrated radar–infrared capabilities is of significant importance for the advancement of stealth technology. The proposed metastructure is a hexagonal prism ring shell, inspired by moth-eye architecture. This metastructure was designed and fabricated via 3D printing, using polyetheretherketone–carbon fiber (PEEK-CF) composite filaments. During the design process of the metastructure, an artificial neural network with dual outputs was established to enable simultaneous prediction of reflection loss and effective absorption bandwidth, thereby allowing comprehensive evaluation of the microwave absorption performance across a broad parameter space. The optimized dual-coated sample exhibited a minimum reflection loss of −41.93 dB at 7.8 GHz, accompanied by an effective absorption bandwidth of 8.24 GHz. The Al (aluminum) powder coating reduced the infrared emissivity of the PEEK-CF substrate from 0.876 to 0.254, thereby enabling effective infrared stealth without compromising EMW absorption. This study provides a generalized paradigm for investigating metastructure stealth.

title: UIT-GAN: A cross-modal generative model for ultrasonic infrared thermography detection of impact damage in composites
exported_title: UIT-GAN: A cross-modal generative model for ultrasonic infrared thermography detection of impact damage in composites

metadata.abstract: Quantifying impact damage in aircraft carbon fiber-reinforced composites is critical for ensuring structural safety. Ultrasonic C-scan is widely regarded as the primary method for detecting and characterizing impact-induced delamination due to its high precision, but its inspection time cost is relatively high. Ultrasonic infrared thermography is fast and convenient, but its inspection effectiveness is limited by thermal diffusion and noise, resulting in low signal-to-noise ratio images that are difficult to quantify. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes UIT-GAN, a novel cross-modal generative framework that incorporates a diffusion-based denoising mechanism to stabilize training under limited data. The model achieves accurate translation from low-resolution thermograms to high-fidelity C-scan-like images. Using CF/PEEK laminates, we collected 88 sets of paired experimental data and expanded the dataset to 880 samples via augmentation. Experimental results demonstrate that UIT-GAN generates images highly consistent with actual C-scans, achieving a structural similarity of up to 95 %. The proposed “generate-then-segment” strategy achieves a mean intersection-over-union of 63 % and a percentage area error below 12 %, outperforming mainstream models such as pix2pix, CUT, SRC, UNSB, and ASCo. In comparison with conventional direct segmentation of thermograms, this approach effectively overcomes limitations such as low SNR and blurred boundaries, and demonstrates superior performance in damage quantification accuracy, region integrity, and boundary smoothness. This study provides an innovative solution for rapid, non-destructive quantitative assessment of impact damage in aerospace composite materials.

title: Investigation on the effect of ply orientations on the fatigue behavior of composite laminates: from the perspective of deep learning
exported_title: Investigation on the effect of ply orientations on the fatigue behavior of composite laminates: from the perspective of deep learning

metadata.abstract: Ply orientation plays a pivotal role in governing the fatigue behavior of carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) laminates. Extensive fatigue experiments on CFRP with ply orientations of D01 ([45/03/-45/90]2s), D02 ([(±45)/45/03/-45/90/45/03/-45/90]s), D03 ([0/-453/90/45]2s) and D04 ([-45/903/45/0/]2s) were conducted in this work. For all tested specimens, stiffness degradation data and fatigue life data were recorded, and a systematic comparison of fatigue-induced stiffness degradation behaviors and the associated microscopic damage mechanisms among different ply orientations was conducted. This paper then utilizes a deep learning framework that integrates a β-Variational Autoencoder (β-VAE) with Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Neural ODEs) to investigate the influence of ply orientations on stiffness degradation and fatigue life. From the latent features extracted by the β-VAE, a key latent variable capturing stiffness degradation is identified, which is clearly separable for each specific ply orientation, and can be used to construct both orientation-specific latent S–N curves and a unified master latent S–N curve covering all orientations. The deep learning model also achieves precise full-trajectory predictions by fine-tuning the encoder using early-stage data, and the master latent S–N curve is employed to predict the fatigue life of selected specimens across different ply orientations.

title: Physics-guided machine learning with an early-age durability fingerprint for GFRP long-term evaluation
exported_title: Physics-guided machine learning with an early-age durability fingerprint for GFRP long-term evaluation

metadata.abstract: Glass fiber-reinforced polymer (GFRP) bars are a promising corrosion-resistant alternative for marine structures, but their wider adoption is constrained by complex, product-dependent degradation behaviors that hinder reliable durability assessment. To address this challenge, this study develops a physics-guided machine learning framework for evaluating the long-term performance of GFRP bars. Built upon an artificial neural network (ANN), the proposed model integrates physics-driven feature engineering and an attention mechanism. Another key innovation is introducing the 30-day tensile strength retention (S30P) as an early-age durability fingerprint, which encodes intrinsic product-specific quality and enables the model to differentiate degradation trajectories among different GFRP bars. Trained on a comprehensive experimental dataset, the model outperforms conventional ANN approaches in predictive accuracy and provides clearer insights into the relative importance of degradation drives through attention-based feature attribution. To ensure the robustness of the predictions, extensive sensitivity analyses, including 10-fold cross-validation, bootstrap uncertainty quantification, and perturbation-based testing of S30P values, demonstrate that the model exhibits stable and reliable performance across multiple sources of uncertainty. Leveraging this model, a practical durability-evaluation workflow is proposed. As an illustrative application, allowable limits for one-month tensile strength reduction at 60 °C are proposed to meet 20-year marine durability requirements. The methodology provides a practical, interpretable, and reliable basis for GFRP selection and durability-oriented design in engineering practice.

title: Fractal neural network of cracks
exported_title: Fractal neural network of cracks

metadata.abstract: The performance degradation of damaged materials primarily manifests as the cross-scale evolution of microcracks. However, existing models for predicting microcrack evolution often suffer from significant discreteness and limited generalization capabilities. The Fractal Neural Network of Cracks (FNNC) is a novel model, proposed for the first time based on the common intrinsic characteristics of self-organizing, scale-invariance, and self-similarity shared by cracks, complex networks and fractal geometry, to predict the evolution of the fractal dimension of material microcracks. Specifically, we have proposed, for the first time, a suite of three novel components: a crack-oriented self-organizing convolutional algorithm (Coso) to extract high-resolution cracks; an adaptive scale-invariance power-law activation function (Asip) that adjusts according to crack distribution; and a Neighborhood-Pooling Self-Similar Graph Attention Mechanism (Nsga) to capture the multiscale weighting of cracks. In polymer creep experiments, FNNC maintains an average absolute error of approximately 6.2%, offering a novel approach for predicting fractal dimension evolution of cracks through the integration of crack structures, complex networks, and fractal geometry.

title: Deep-learning-based surrogate modeling for accelerated curing process optimization in scarf-repaired composite laminates
exported_title: Deep-learning-based surrogate modeling for accelerated curing process optimization in scarf-repaired composite laminates

metadata.abstract: Composite patch repair is an effective technique for restoring the load-bearing capability of damaged structures. However, residual stresses arising from the thermochemical-mechanical coupling during repair degrade repair quality and complicate process optimization within traditional design frameworks. To overcome these limitations, this study establishes an integrated framework that combines in-situ sensing, high-fidelity multi-physics simulation, and deep learning to accelerate process exploration. The finite element model is first validated through in-situ strain monitoring to ensure physical fidelity of the simulation data. Based on the verified dataset, a deep neural network surrogate model is then developed to predict curing degree and three-dimensional residual stress fields directly from process parameters. The surrogate model achieves a normalized mean absolute error of 7.64% in Mises stress prediction and runs four orders of magnitude faster than finite element analysis. Leveraging this efficiency, a multi-objective optimization of the curing process is conducted, yielding a Pareto front that reveals trade-offs among Mises stress peak, curing time, and degree of cure. The proposed framework demonstrates a practical route toward intelligent design and optimization of the composite repair process.

title: Data-driven prediction of process-induced deformation in CFRP composites using a convolutional neural network
exported_title: Data-driven prediction of process-induced deformation in CFRP composites using a convolutional neural network

metadata.abstract: This study proposes a data-driven surrogate framework for rapid full-field prediction of process-induced deformation in CFRP composite structures. A one-dimensional convolutional neural network is trained to map a fixed topology nodal sequence with consistent node numbering to the complete three-dimensional nodal displacement field. Convolutional weight-sharing is leveraged to promote stable learning with a compact parameterization. High-fidelity finite element (FE) curing simulations are performed to generate the ground-truth database for a CFRP spar representative of an aircraft wing component. The simulations incorporate thermo-chemo-mechanical coupling, cure kinetics, degree of cure dependent property evolution, chemical shrinkage, and user-defined subroutines. The dataset is constructed to preserve mesh-consistent nodal correspondence across parametric variations in stacking sequence, ply count, and flange radius, enabling direct full-field inference without additional projection. Using 10-fold cross-validation, the model achieves an MSE of 0.027 ± 0.010 and an R2 of 0.974 ± 0.008, while requiring approximately 12 ms per case, compared with 36.3 min per case for FE analysis. Predictive performance is further examined under interpolation and extrapolation conditions with respect to the manufacturing parameters. Principal component analysis is evaluated for input compression. However, it yields no improvement in accuracy or efficiency and reduces interpretability. The proposed framework enables computationally efficient evaluation for repetitive design studies, mold compensation, and process parameter screening within the covered design space.

title: Efficient homogenization of macroscale volume growth in CERCER composites: A physics-constrained LSTM-FE framework
exported_title: Efficient homogenization of macroscale volume growth in CERCER composites: A physics-constrained LSTM-FE framework

metadata.abstract: Ceramic–ceramic (CERCER) composite fuels, which consist of ceramic fuel particles dispersed in an MgO matrix, are dedicated fuels for advanced nuclear systems. The thermo-mechanical-irradiation induced macroscale volume growth poses a critical phenomenon influencing the composite viability. This work proposes a physics-constrained LSTM framework deeply integrated with the Finite Element (FE) solver for efficient homogenization of the time-dependent composite behavior. A multi-level homogenization model is developed that accounts for particle fission gas, grain recrystallization, and creep of both the fuel particle and matrix. Using a dataset generated from FE simulations of a representative volume element (RVE) with random particles, physics-constrained Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models are trained to predict macroscale volume growth. Online prediction has been realized by implementing the surrogate into the FE solver through a user-material subroutine (UMAT). Results indicate that: (1) the mechanistic model agrees well with experimental measurements, with simulations illustrating dominant factors influencing volume growth; (2) the LSTM predictions show mechanism consistency and exhibit high fidelity in extrapolative FE-divergent scenarios; (3) an exponential activation-based hard constraint optimally mitigates material instability; (4) LSTM-FE implementation effectively reduces the online prediction time from 192 to 12 min, achieving a 94% reduction. The work offers insights toward high-fidelity and computationally efficient methods for time-dependent composite performance under extreme conditions.

title: A data-to-failure workflow for flexible woven composite membrane: Neural network constitutive modeling and probabilistic failure surface construction
exported_title: A data-to-failure workflow for flexible woven composite membrane: Neural network constitutive modeling and probabilistic failure surface construction

metadata.abstract: The envelope is a critical component determining the structural strength of airships, with its ultimate strength highly sensitive to temperature variations and exhibiting significant statistical dispersion. However, research on the probabilistic failure modeling of envelope materials, particularly methods applicable to structural-level analysis, remains limited. To address this gap, this study proposes a data-to-failure workflow for flexible Vectran woven composite membranes, integrating artificial neural network (ANN)-based constitutive modeling with probabilistic failure surface construction. Uniaxial and biaxial tensile-to-failure tests were conducted over a temperature range of −80 °C to 80 °C, with full-field strain distributions captured using the digital image correlation (DIC) method and statistical parameters of strain non-uniformity extracted. Following a finite element (FE)-assisted stress correction, ANN–based response surfaces and interpolated probabilistic failure surfaces were developed. Strain uncertainty was propagated into the stress space via the Monte Carlo (MC) method to quantify failure probability distributions. The trained ANN models were then integrated into FE simulations through a COMSOL external material subroutine, enabling test-data-driven prediction of the envelope structural failure probability. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach effectively captures non-uniform strain distributions and associated failure probabilities. Notably, FE-assisted stress correction shrinks the failure surface, while accounting for strain non-uniformity substantially increases the predicted failure probability.

title: Tough bioinspired composites through bone - bamboo hybrid gradient designs: Simulation, deep learning, and 3D-printing
exported_title: Tough bioinspired composites through bone - bamboo hybrid gradient designs: Simulation, deep learning, and 3D-printing

metadata.abstract: Natural composites exhibit outstanding mechanical properties, refined over millions of years of adaptation through gradient architectures and hierarchical organization. Inspired by these principles, we present a strategy for designing hybrid bone–bamboo-like gradient composites and establish an integrated simulation-AI-3D-printing framework for their evaluation and validation. Using lattice spring simulation, we examine graded structures with monotonic, partially and randomly shuffled volume fraction sequences. Our results show that placing a high soft-phase volume fraction (46.80%) at the notch improves strength by ∼5% and toughness by ∼25%, due to enhanced crack deflection and distributed energy dissipation. To accelerate mechanical performance prediction, we train a deep learning model on 200 samples, achieving R2 scores of ∼0.8 for strength and toughness. The model generalizes across 1620 additional designs, capturing layer sequencing effects using only volume fraction inputs. Selected top-performing designs were 3D printed using a multimaterial printer, validating the simulation predictions. This work offers a mechanics-informed design framework that tunes notch-adjacent compliance through gradient sequencing to create hybrid gradient composites. Integrating natural design principles with AI and additive manufacturing, this study provides a pathway for developing tough bioinspired materials with tunable fracture resistance.

title: A data-driven multiphysical masking model for morphology prediction and process optimization in longitudinal–torsional ultrasonic-assisted milling of CFRP
exported_title: A data-driven multiphysical masking model for morphology prediction and process optimization in longitudinal–torsional ultrasonic-assisted milling of CFRP

metadata.abstract: This study proposes a data-driven multiphysical masking approach for predicting the cross-sectional morphology in longitudinal-torsional ultrasonic-assisted milling (LTUAM) of carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP). The coupled vibration trajectory is first analyzed to elucidate the synergistic effects of “minimum-point” and “repeated cutting” mechanisms on the formation of residual heights. Subsequently, dynamic vibration and acoustic responses are employed to infer real-time cutting states and refine the morphology predictions. A multi-criterion damage model, integrating the improved Tsai-Wu, LaRC05, and Puck fracture criteria, is developed. Furthermore, a deep Gaussian process framework with sparse autoencoding of acoustic signals is introduced to achieve probabilistic and interpretable prediction of fiber fracture heights under uncertainty. A dual-path fusion strategy is then established, which incorporates tool-tip cutting forces and spindle acceleration within a Graph Convolutional Network-Physics-Informed Neural Network hybrid architecture to create a physics-constrained morphology model. By integrating physical masking with a multi-head self-attention mechanism, a multi-source fusion predictor is constructed. Experimental results demonstrate the framework's high predictive accuracy (95.24%) across varied machining conditions and identify an optimal parameter set (n = 1600 r/min, d = 8 mm, f = 5 mm/s, MQL; Sa = 2.1 μm). The proposed framework provides an innovative solution for CFRP ultrasonic-assisted precision machining that integrates physical interpretability, probabilistic prediction capability, and uncertainty-aware learning characteristics.

title: Multiscale design and mechanical performance optimization of a bio-inspired S-shaped mortise-and-tenon honeycomb via deep learning and probability-driven modeling
exported_title: Multiscale design and mechanical performance optimization of a bio-inspired S-shaped mortise-and-tenon honeycomb via deep learning and probability-driven modeling

metadata.abstract: Mechanical metamaterials featuring high energy absorption and tunable Poisson's ratios are of significant value in engineering applications. To address the inherent trade-offs among stiffness, stability, and energy-absorbing capacity in conventional negative Poisson's ratio (NPR) honeycombs, this study proposes a bio-inspired s-shaped mortise-and-tenon honeycomb (BSMTH) inspired by the sutural interlocking features of beetle elytra. First, an s-shaped unit cell with asymmetric geometric features is constructed, and an analytical mechanical model is established based on the energy method. This model elucidates the effects of thickness (t), central angle (θ), and a thickness coefficient (k) associated with the joint distribution on the equivalent elastic constants, enabling the partial decoupling of the Poisson's ratio and structural stiffness. Second, 12 types of specimens (categorized into three groups) with diverse joint configurations were fabricated via fused deposition modeling (FDM). Tensile, compressive, and three-point bending tests were conducted across four polymer substrates to systematically analyze the effects of the material system and joint distribution on deformation evolution, failure modes, and energy absorption. The results indicate that the matrix material and configuration jointly affect the comprehensive performance of BSMTH. Within the investigated design space, a deep neural network (DNN) surrogate model was further developed and coupled with the integrated with non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA-II) to achieve global optimization of the thickness gradient distribution, resulting in a 16.8% increase in SEA and a 13% increase in mean crushing force (MCF). This study provides a valuable reference for multiscale design and property modulation.

title: A progressive damage model-assisted GW-Gaussian process SHM method for complex composite damage quantification
exported_title: A progressive damage model-assisted GW-Gaussian process SHM method for complex composite damage quantification

metadata.abstract: Accurate damage quantification of composites by using structural health monitoring (SHM) is of great significance for the life management of aerospace structures. However, damage mechanism in composite structures is always complicated and progressive due to their heterogeneity and anisotropy, leading to significant dispersion and multi-stage characteristics in damage evolution. To solve this problem, a new progressive damage quantification SHM method for composite structures by combining Gaussian process (GP)-based probabilistic mode transition and progressive damage model assistance is proposed in this paper. The dominant progressive damage mechanism transition is identified by evaluating the statistical consistency between damage features and the GP predictive distribution. By combining the assistance of progressive damage modeling in capturing the entire damage evolution process, a mode-dependent GP probabilistic model is established to quantify the progressive damage. Based on active guided wave (GW)-SHM, the proposed method is validated under quasi-static shear loading using a composite orthogrid stiffened panel with a central cutout, which is derived from an important load-carrying component in reusable launch vehicles (RLV). The validation focuses on skin-stiffener debonding and subsequent skin cracking, which are the dominant progressive damage modes in such structures. Validation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in accurately identifying the debonding-to-cracking transition at a load level of 200 kN, as well as in quantifying the debonding area with a maximum absolute error of 8.1%. A sensitivity analysis further confirms the robustness of the method under ±20% variations in key skin–stiffener interface properties.

title: 3D damage imaging and residual compressive strength prediction for arched composites: A CNT self-sensing approach with electromechanical modeling and machine learning
exported_title: 3D damage imaging and residual compressive strength prediction for arched composites: A CNT self-sensing approach with electromechanical modeling and machine learning

metadata.abstract: Fiber-reinforced polymer composites (FRPCs) are widely used in the automotive, aerospace, and energy sectors owing to their high specific stiffness and strength. However, their susceptibility to impact-induced damage motivates the development of structural health monitoring (SHM) techniques that can complement traditional non-destructive evaluation. This study presents an integrated SHM framework for non-planar arched composite structures by combining an optimized carbon nanotube sensing layer, three-dimensional electrical impedance tomography, electromechanical modeling, and ensemble machine learning. An electromechanically coupled model calibrated from experimental data was used to simulate damage evolution and piezoresistive responses. The three-dimensional generalized vector sample pattern matching (3D-GVSPM) EIT algorithm localized the dominant conductivity-reduction regions, with the normalized localization error from experimental values of 5.5%, 8.2%, and 12.7% for the 5 J, 10 J, and 15 J impact cases, respectively. A gradient-boosting regressor trained on simulation-generated data predicted residual compressive strength (RCS) with an R2 of 0.9817 on an independent experimental test set. SHAP-based interpretability analysis provided supporting evidence that the selected electrical features were physically consistent with damage-sensitive conductive paths. Overall, this study establishes a laboratory-scale diagnostic-prognostic SHM workflow that integrates damage localization and electrical-feature-based RCS prediction for arched composite structures under compression-after-impact conditions.

title: Multi-view deep learning for CT-based damage quantification in 3D woven composites
exported_title: Multi-view deep learning for CT-based damage quantification in 3D woven composites

metadata.abstract: Accurate identification and quantification of damage in 3D woven composites (3DWC) are essential for understanding damage evolution and predicting mechanical performance. However, the morphological characteristics of cracks vary significantly across different viewing directions, leading to weaker identification accuracy when relying on a single view. To address this, we propose a multi-view deep learning approach that identifies cracks from three mutually orthogonal planes, thereby improving segmentation accuracy. In addition, a data-driven predictive analysis based on quantitative crack features is conducted to estimate shear stiffness degradation. To apply and evaluate the proposed method in practice, we conducted a stepwise experimental program as described below. Initially, a stepwise out-of-plane shear test was performed to enable progressive CT data acquisition during deformation. Subsequently, the proposed approach was adopted to automatically identify cracks from CT data. Based on damage visualization and quantitative analysis, interfacial cracking was identified as the dominant damage mechanism, and the shear failure process was classified into three distinct stages. Finally, CT-derived crack descriptors were used to predict shear stiffness degradation. Comparative evaluation with different regression models showed that the CT-derived crack descriptors contain useful predictive information for stiffness degradation, and that Gradient Boosting provided the best predictive performance under the present limited-data condition.

title: Point cloud-based deep learning for tensile strength estimation of gap-defective composite laminates using FEA-generated data
exported_title: Point cloud-based deep learning for tensile strength estimation of gap-defective composite laminates using FEA-generated data

metadata.abstract: Gap defects in composite laminates can interrupt fiber continuity and cause localized stress concentrations, leading to degradation of tensile performance. Conventional finite element analysis (FEA) provides an effective means of evaluating such defect-induced strength reduction, but its high computational cost limits its applicability to large-scale defect assessment. This study develops a point cloud-based deep learning surrogate modeling framework for tensile strength estimation of gap-defective composite laminates using FEA-generated data. A numerical reference dataset containing randomly distributed and irregular gap morphologies was constructed through parametric modeling and progressive damage FEA, with controlled tensile tests on representative gap configurations used to support the finite element modeling strategy. To directly characterize complex layer-wise defect morphology, the generated gap geometries were represented as point clouds, and a layer-index feature was introduced to distinguish spatially overlapping points from different plies. A PointNet-based regression model, referred to as PC2S-Net, was adapted to learn the mapping between layer-resolved point cloud representations and tensile strength. The proposed surrogate achieved an R2 of 0.9489 and a mean absolute percentage error below 1.2% when evaluated against FEA-generated labels. Compared with modern point cloud architectures, PC2S-Net showed competitive predictive accuracy while requiring lower computational cost under the adopted preprocessing and training protocol. These results demonstrate that point cloud-based surrogate modeling provides an efficient and physically meaningful approach for numerical strength assessment of gap-defective composite laminates.

title: Data-driven acoustic emission framework with multimodal validation for resolving micromechanical damage in B4C/AA6061 composite
exported_title: Data-driven acoustic emission framework with multimodal validation for resolving micromechanical damage in B4C/AA6061 composite

metadata.abstract: A data-driven acoustic emission (AE) framework with multimodal validation is proposed to resolve micromechanical damage evolution in a particle-reinforced metal matrix composite, B4C/AA6061, under uniaxial tension. AE waveforms are represented using wavelet packet transform–based spectral features and analyzed through a hierarchical unsupervised workflow. A key feature of the framework is the establishment of a matrix-referenced baseline using pre-fracture AE data from monolithic AA6061, enabling objective separation of matrix-dominant and particle-dominant acoustic activity based on autoencoder reconstruction error. The particle-dominant subset is further partitioned into statistically distinct clusters with characteristic spectral signatures and strain-stage dependence. To provide physical interpretation and validation, complementary in situ techniques are employed. In situ scanning electron microscopy (SEM) reveals the initiation and progression of reinforcement-associated damage, including interfacial decohesion and particle cracking. In situ neutron diffraction (NED) quantifies phase-specific lattice-strain evolution and captures the development of deformation partitioning between the Al matrix and B4C reinforcement. A clear correspondence is identified between the accelerated accumulation of particle-dominant AE activity and the increase in lattice-strain divergence during post-yield deformation, indicating progressive degradation of deformation compatibility. The integrated AE–SEM–NED analysis demonstrates that the proposed framework enables time-resolved and phase-sensitive interpretation of micromechanical damage evolution without relying on predefined signal labels. The approach provides a physically grounded basis for tracking reinforcement-associated damage and its coupling to phase-level deformation behavior in particle-reinforced metal matrix composites.

title: Deep reinforcement learning-based trajectory optimization for pressure vessel filament winding and analysis of multi-payout-eye co-layer hybrid winding
exported_title: Deep reinforcement learning-based trajectory optimization for pressure vessel filament winding and analysis of multi-payout-eye co-layer hybrid winding

metadata.abstract: Filament winding trajectories govern component manufacturability and dictate mechanical properties via fiber distribution modulation. This study aims to develop more flexible and versatile trajectories by establishing a co-layer hybrid winding theory for multiple payout eyes and proposing a physics-guided deep reinforcement learning (DRL)-based optimization method. A physics-based custom filament winding simulation environment was built to evaluate various algorithms. Additionally, a comparative dome training-difficulty score was introduced to assess morphology effects under the tested geometry and parameters. Finally, filament winding trajectory experiments under different objectives were conducted using a custom-built multi-payout-eye filament winding machine, thereby verifying the feasibility of the reinforcement learning-based trajectory design. The results indicate that, compared to Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithms, the Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) algorithm exhibits the highest stability while maintaining high precision in the winding environment. DRL-based winding trajectories can achieve flexible and stable winding across different modes by employing a variable slippage coefficient. Within the tested geometry and parameter range, the score decreased with increasing aspect ratio, permitting greater offsets and design flexibility. Simultaneously, the winding of two distinct trajectories on the same helical layer is realized through the coordinated motion of dual payout eyes. This hybrid trajectory winding effectively mitigates fiber accumulation at the polar opening of the dome. Compared with the tangential path, the mean winding thicknesses of the adjacent and interlacing paths within the inner evaluation band were reduced by 43.9% and 50.6%, respectively.

title: An integrated process–failure simulation framework for predicting composite allowables via multi-fidelity stochastic simulation and machine learning
exported_title: An integrated process–failure simulation framework for predicting composite allowables via multi-fidelity stochastic simulation and machine learning

metadata.abstract: For material screening, qualification, and certification of aerospace composites, it is essential to establish statistical design properties that account for both inherent material variability and process-induced uncertainty. Regulatory standards require the determination of A-basis and B-basis statistical values as conservative lower bound design allowables. At present, allowables are determined through extensive experimental campaigns, which are costly and time-consuming, thereby limiting the exploration of new material systems. In this work, we present a multiscale, multi-fidelity process-failure modeling framework that enables the simulation-informed estimation of allowables. The framework integrates thermo-chemical-mechanical process simulations with stochastic multi-fidelity failure simulations to capture the effects of curing-induced properties, residual stresses, and microstructural variability on mechanical performance. A transfer-learning-enabled surrogate model accelerate uncertainty propagation across scales, while Bayesian inference leverages limited experimental data to quantify uncertain parameters. High-fidelity macroscale failure simulations then predict tensile strength distributions from which A- and B-basis allowables are estimated. Application to Hexcel AS4/8552 cross-ply laminates demonstrates close agreement with test data, with conservative predictions of statistical allowables. By linking manufacturing process simulation, process-induced residual stresses, stochastic failure analysis, Bayesian calibration, and allowable estimation, the framework provides a pathway toward simulation-informed composite qualification with the potential to reduce experimental effort.

title: Ultra-stretchable, tough, and rapid self-healing MXene-composited hydrogels via dynamic interface-network coupling strategy for reliable wearable sensors and machine learning-assisted gesture recognition
exported_title: Ultra-stretchable, tough, and rapid self-healing MXene-composited hydrogels via dynamic interface-network coupling strategy for reliable wearable sensors and machine learning-assisted gesture recognition

metadata.abstract: Conductive hydrogels with high stretchability, toughness, and rapid self-healing ability have emerged as promising materials for flexible wearable electronics, but face a trade-off between toughness and self-healing, as toughening strategies often suppress the network dynamics required for healing. Here, we report a dynamic interface-network coupling strategy to realize an ultra-stretchable, highly tough, and rapidly self-healing MXene-based conductive hydrogel by incorporating polydopamine-coated MXene nanosheets (PDA@MXene) into a dynamic poly(acrylamide-co-3-acrylamidophenylboronic acid) (P(AM-co-AAPBA)) network. The synergistic coupling between the dynamic interface of PDA@MXene with the polymer matrix and the tough reversible polymer network enables efficient energy dissipation while preserving rapid network reconstruction. The resulting hydrogel exhibits high stretchability (2396 ± 68%), high toughness (3.26 ± 0.37 MJ m−3), and rapid and efficient self-healing (≈83% within 7 min at room temperature). This hydrogel demonstrates good strain sensitivity over a broad range, excellent stability, and rapid recovery of sensing performance after damage, enabling reliable monitoring of diverse human activities. In addition, it can also serve as a skin-conformal bioelectrode for high-quality electrophysiological signal acquisition. Integration with machine learning further enables multiclass gesture recognition with an average accuracy of 96.37%. This work provides a general strategy for constructing highly tough and rapidly self-healing hydrogels for demanding applications.

title: Smart manufacturing in wire arc additive manufacturing: A comprehensive review of FEM-based simulation, machine learning, and digital twin technologies
exported_title: Smart manufacturing in wire arc additive manufacturing: A comprehensive review of FEM-based simulation, machine learning, and digital twin technologies

metadata.abstract: Wire arc additive manufacturing (WAAM) involves complex thermal microstructural mechanical interactions that govern melt pool evolution, heat accumulation, phase transformations, residual stress development, distortion, and final component performance. Accurate prediction of these coupled phenomena remains challenging due to the multi-scale nature of heat transfer, material behavior, and process dynamics. This review critically examines recent advances in smart manufacturing approaches for WAAM, focusing on finite element method (FEM)-based modeling, machine learning (ML), and digital twin technologies. Particular attention is given to heat source modeling, thermal history prediction, constitutive modeling for residual stress analysis, thermal microstructural mechanical coupling, and material data requirements for reliable simulations. Recent developments in accelerated FEM techniques, including adaptive meshing, reduced-order modeling, high-performance computing, and GPU-assisted simulations, are assessed for improving computational efficiency. The review further evaluates ML-driven surrogate models for thermal prediction, process parameter optimization, defect detection, and real-time monitoring, as well as digital twin frameworks that integrate sensor data with physics-based simulations for adaptive process control. Unlike previous reviews that examine these technologies separately, this work establishes a physics data-fused modeling paradigm that links FEM, ML, and digital twins within a unified intelligent manufacturing framework. Current challenges related to computational cost, data availability, model generalization, and real-time implementation are identified, and future directions involving hybrid FEM ML models, physics-informed learning, and autonomous WAAM systems are discussed.

title: Recent progress in machine learning strategies in designing, synthesizing and characterizing new age metal matrix composites
exported_title: Recent progress in machine learning strategies in designing, synthesizing and characterizing new age metal matrix composites

metadata.abstract: Metal Matrix Composites (MMCs) are advanced materials known for their high specific strength, stiffness, wear resistance, and thermal stability, making them vital for aerospace, automotive, defence, and energy sectors. However, traditional trial-and-error approaches for their design and development are inefficient, costly, and inadequate for exploring complex compositional and processing spaces. Recent advancements in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) have enabled a shift toward data-driven and predictive frameworks in MMC development. This review highlights AI/ML applications across the MMCs lifecycle, including materials design, processing, and characterization. It discusses the use of supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning models to optimize matrix–reinforcement combinations, volume fractions, particle morphology, and interfacial properties. The integration of physics-informed and hybrid models for capturing complex strengthening mechanisms and interfacial phenomena is also examined. Further, the review explores ML-driven approaches for real-time process monitoring, defect prediction, microstructure control, and parameter optimization. In characterization, AI techniques are increasingly used for automated microstructure analysis, phase identification, damage detection, and property prediction. Emerging trends such as multimodal data fusion, explainable AI, uncertainty quantification, and the development of open-access materials databases are also discussed. The review concludes by identifying key challenges, including the need for high-quality datasets, standardized methodologies, and better integration of domain knowledge, to enable sustainable and accelerated development of next-generation MMCs.

title: Deep learning-assisted precise segmentation and meso-structure quantitative characterization of 3D7d-BFRP XCT images
exported_title: Deep learning-assisted precise segmentation and meso-structure quantitative characterization of 3D7d-BFRP XCT images

metadata.abstract: Precise segmentation, reconstruction, and quantitative characterization of the meso-structure in 3D7d braided composites are critical for evaluating their mechanical performance under complex loading conditions and varying process parameters. However, the severe yarn adhesion and complex internal topology of cured 3D7d braided composites hinder the accurate segmentation of X-ray computed tomography (XCT) images, posing significant challenges to precise meso-structure characterization. To address this, using XCT digital images of 3D7d-BFRP composites as a case study, this paper proposes a Mask2Former-based 3D7d-BFRP XCT images automatic segmentation framework. The proposed framework enables high-precision segmentation of the meso-structure, achieving accuracies of 93% for the yarn phase and 95% for the pore phase. Subsequently, utilizing the proposed meso-structure model instantiation and reconstruction algorithm based on three-round global optimization, high-fidelity 3D reconstruction and precise quantitative characterization of 3D7d-BFRP samples are achieved. The analysis results indicate that the yarn Fiber Packing Density (FPD) of the 3D7d-BFRP sample is positively correlated with the degree of extrusion and negatively correlated with the cross-sectional area. Overall, the compactness distribution exhibits a characteristic pattern of higher FPD in the central region and looser structure toward the edges. Meanwhile, the pore distribution follows a clear bipolar distribution pattern. This study provides robust data support and key guidance for optimizing braiding and VARTM processes to reduce internal defects.

title: AI-enabled large-format additive manufacturing of thermoplastics: Recent advances and future directions
exported_title: AI-enabled large-format additive manufacturing of thermoplastics: Recent advances and future directions

metadata.abstract: Thermoplastic large-format additive manufacturing (LFAM), as considered in this review, is a large-scale implementation of material extrusion (MEX) for producing meter-scale tooling, molds, fixtures, and structural components with reduced lead time, lower tooling cost, and enhanced design flexibility. Yet high deposition rates, large bead dimensions, long build durations, and large build volumes create persistent challenges in process robustness and part quality, including dimensional error, thermal gradients, heat accumulation, warpage, weak interlayer bonding, voids, and spatially varying properties. These challenges arise from coupled process–structure–property relationships governed by material- and temperature-dependent rheological, thermal, and thermo-mechanical behavior. They are difficult to capture with experiments or physics-based simulations alone, and full-scale simulations remain too costly for real-time deployment. These limitations motivate artificial intelligence (AI) and digital twin approaches that combine in-situ sensing, physics-based understanding, and data-driven learning. This review synthesizes recent AI-enabled and digital twin methods for thermoplastic LFAM. It surveys process and material characteristics, defect mechanisms, sensing modalities, data acquisition and synchronization needs, feature representations, and physics-based modeling strategies. It also examines AI for process monitoring, quality prediction, process optimization, closed-loop control, and physics-informed hybrid modeling, with applications in tooling, aerospace, marine, construction, repair, and hybrid manufacturing. Key gaps include limited standardized datasets, sparse ground-truth validation, insufficient real-time thermo-mechanical twins, and unresolved integration challenges. A research roadmap is proposed for robust and autonomous LFAM systems.

title: Beyond organ-level phenotyping: A cross-scale, AI-assisted framework for decoding the biological determinants of seed vigor
