Results show that this method has high prediction accuracy and can adapt to the randomness and diversity of the service environment.

title: Risk resolution of airport surface based on hybrid Petri nets and inverse reinforcement learning
exported_title: Risk resolution of airport surface based on hybrid Petri nets and inverse reinforcement learning

metadata.abstract: Risk evaluation and conflict risk resolution of airport surface are two correlated challenge problems; however they are rarely studied jointly to reduce operation risk. Moreover, risk resolution performance of current methods also should be improved. Therefore, this paper proposes a novel risk resolution approach based on hybrid Petri nets and inverse reinforcement learning. Firstly, a hybrid Petri nets based on Bayesian fusion is presented to get taxiing risk evaluation of airport surface and its theorem of strict conservation and structure boundedness is proved. Secondly, a new risk model is proposed to minimize total operation cost of flights. Thirdly, a new risk evaluation method based on hybrid Petri nets is studied, and corresponding time complexity analysis is presented. Fourthly, a novel risk resolution algorithm based on inverse reinforcement learning strategy and game model is developed. Finally, datasets from Nanjing Lukou International Airport are used and experimental results show that: 1) our approach reduces delay time in multi-scale samples by 25% on average than state-of-the-arts methods; 2) taxiing conflicts with unacceptable risk are all resolved successfully; 3) it achieves stable convergence results while traditional methods oscillate uniformly, and even fail to reach a state of convergence; 4) sensitivity analysis and statistical result results verify the effectiveness of our method.

title: Recent advances in wind turbine condition monitoring using SCADA data: A state-of-the-art review
exported_title: Recent advances in wind turbine condition monitoring using SCADA data: A state-of-the-art review

metadata.abstract: With the rapid increase worldwide in the number of installed wind turbines, as an increasingly vital role in the global energy landscape, requirements and expenses of maintenance have also increased significantly. This surge in wind turbine installations worldwide has escalated maintenance demands and costs, making condition monitoring an essential focus for research and operational optimization. Built-in supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems could offer a cost-effective approach to condition monitoring in wind turbines, using existing infrastructure to reduce the need for additional sensors and simplifying system complexity. This review critically surveys state-of-the-art SCADA-based condition monitoring techniques for wind turbines. The paper first examines essential data preprocessing strategies tailored for SCADA data challenges. Subsequently, key monitoring methodologies are reviewed, including model-based and data-driven paradigms, analyzing their applications, strengths, and limitations. Finally, the challenges and future trends of SCADA-based wind turbine condition monitoring are discussed. This comprehensive overview serves as a valuable reference for researchers and industry practitioners seeking to enhance wind turbine reliability and operational efficiency through advanced monitoring techniques.

title: Wiener process-assisted online remaining useful life prediction with deep incremental regression transfer learning
exported_title: Wiener process-assisted online remaining useful life prediction with deep incremental regression transfer learning

metadata.abstract: Despite promising developments of remaining useful life (RUL) prediction in predictive maintenance, existing RUL prediction models tend to be incapable of dynamical update using sequentially-collected online data and are then probably with low prognostic accuracy. This study addresses the following challenges of online remaining useful life (RUL) for industrial devices under varying even unknown operating conditions: (1) Degradation data of target machine are unavailable to model training, while data distribution drifts from offline data exist, (2) The degradation tendency of target machine is difficult to be captured because of the varying online operating condition. This paper proposes a Wiener process-assisted deep incremental transfer learning method for online RUL prediction. This method includes a pretraining prognostic model, which captures the essential degradation information from offline machines, and a Wiener process-assisted incremental update mechanism, which dedicates to capture of dynamic tendency information from online data. A Bayesian status feedback strategy is designed to generate pseudo-labels from Wiener process for the online RUL prediction. Numerical experimental results on three run-to-failure rolling element bearing datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method, thus providing a deployable prognosis solution for practical applications.

title: Moving regression artificial neural network framework for reliability evaluation of complex structure/system
exported_title: Moving regression artificial neural network framework for reliability evaluation of complex structure/system

metadata.abstract: For evaluating reliability level of complex structure/system, a moving regression artificial neural network (MRANN) framework is proposed based on artificial neural network (ANN), moving regression technique and intelligent optimization algorithm. Under this framework, four methods of ANN-based moving least squares (MLS) (MLS-ANN), enhanced ANN-based MLS (MLS-EANN), ANN-based improved MLS (IMLS-ANN) and enhanced ANN-based improved MLS (IMLS-EANN) models are developed by introducing the Ivy algorithm and MLS technique into the ANN model. Herein, the Ivy algorithm is used to find the optimal radius of compact support region for selecting effective modeling samples or to search the optimal values of weights and thresholds of ANN model, the MLS technique is applied to assign weights for these effective modeling samples and to resolve unknown coefficients of ANN model, and the ANN model is employed to reflect the relationship of structural response and input parameters. Furthermore, three examples, including multivariate function approximation and probabilistic analyses, aeroengine high-pressure turbine blisk deformation reliability assessment and aircraft flap system deflection angle reliability analysis, are performed to validate and verify the effectiveness of these developed approaches. The analytical results show that MRANN framework holds excellent ability in the modeling and simulation features relative to the existing surrogate models.

title: Reconstruction of existing buildings for evacuation assessment under emergency situations using 3D Gaussian splatting and machine learning
exported_title: Reconstruction of existing buildings for evacuation assessment under emergency situations using 3D Gaussian splatting and machine learning

metadata.abstract: Existing buildings characterized by aging and structurally complex layouts pose significant challenges for emergency evacuation, necessitating advanced and dynamic risk assessment methods that go beyond conventional static evaluations. The primary scientific objective of this study is to develop and validate an integrated computational framework that combines high-fidelity 3D modeling with machine learning to quantitatively assess and predict evacuation risks in such structures. Using laser-scanned structural data, we reconstructed detailed building information models (BIM) via anisotropic 3D Gaussian Splatting, enabling accurate spatial representation. These models were coupled with agent-based Pathfinder simulations to examine evacuation dynamics under diverse crowd densities and movement speeds. Simulated egress capacity informed a risk stratification mechanism. Further, we developed four machine learning models to predict evacuation time, among which the Improved Particle Swarm Optimization-integrated Convolutional Neural Network–Long Short-Term Memory (IPSOCNN-LSTM) model achieved superior predictive accuracy. The results confirm the efficacy of the proposed framework in identifying critical evacuation risks and supporting real-time emergency decision-making. This research contributes a scientifically grounded, data-driven paradigm for dynamic risk assessment in built environments and offers scalable solutions for enhancing safety in aging urban infrastructure under various emergency scenarios.

title: Early warning and prevention of mud cakes in large-diameter slurry shields: Insights from construction parameter data analysis and interpretable machine learning
exported_title: Early warning and prevention of mud cakes in large-diameter slurry shields: Insights from construction parameter data analysis and interpretable machine learning

metadata.abstract: Mud cake blockage in large-diameter slurry shield (LDSS) construction is one of the key factors affecting the high efficiency and quality of tunnel construction. To address the lack of intelligent methods for mud cake detection, an early warning interpretable machine learning approach based on Exponential-Trigonometric Optimization (ETO)-Natural gradient boosting (NGBoost)- Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) for LDSS is proposed. Twenty-four types of construction-related parameter data for LDSSs are selected as input indicators. The knowledge-driven method is used to analyse the construction parameters to obtain the risk level of the mud cake, and the degree of mud cake formation is classified via the ETO-NGBoost intelligent algorithm. The results are as follows: (1) ETO-NGBoost can obtain mud cake supervised classification results with high precision and high generalization performance, and the precision, recall and F1 score values in the test set are all above 0.93. (2) SHAP improves the interpretability and determines the important factors of slurry shields that influence the formation of mud cakes. (3) The supervised classification model driven by knowledge and data can be used to build a mud cake detection and early warning framework to judge the degree of mud cake formation in time. On this basis, effective prevention and control measures can be taken.
keywords: Dual-driven knowledge and construction parameter data

title: Pirate-GPT: A locally deployed large language model framework for reliable offline anti-piracy decision support and knowledge retrieval in maritime operations
exported_title: Pirate-GPT: A locally deployed large language model framework for reliable offline anti-piracy decision support and knowledge retrieval in maritime operations

metadata.abstract: Ensuring the reliability and safety of maritime transportation systems is critically impeded by the fragmentation, complexity, and redundancy of piracy-related information. This study introduces Pirate-GPT, a domain-specific question answering framework built upon large language models(LLMs), designed to advance anti-piracy decision support and maritime knowledge management. Pirate-GPT integrates a semantic sliding-window segmentation algorithm to construct a semantically complete and robust vector database, facilitating precise information retrieval. The framework further employs an Agent collaboration mechanism and a “two-stage retrieval” process, significantly improving answer relevance and explainability while reducing hallucination rates. Centered on the Qwen2.5 LLM and optimized through Generative Pre-trained Transformer Quantization (GPTQ), Pirate-GPT supports efficient, stable, and privacy-preserving local deployment in offline and resource-constrained maritime environments. The system was evaluated using 7399 piracy reports and 230 related documents, and it consistently outperformed baseline models, with LooseMatch scores exceeding 90% and marked reductions in hallucinations across various query types. Ablation studies confirmed the essential contributions of each module to the system’s overall performance. Consequently, Pirate-GPT offers a scalable, reliable, and practical solution, providing a systematic approach to integrating complex domain knowledge and supporting robust risk assessment and decision-making in real-world maritime operations.

title: An anomaly detection method for gas turbines in power plants using conditional variational autoencoder optimized with self-attention
exported_title: An anomaly detection method for gas turbines in power plants using conditional variational autoencoder optimized with self-attention

metadata.abstract: An innovative anomaly detection (AD) framework designed for gas turbines (GTs) in power plants working under variable operating conditions (OCs) was proposed based on conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) optimized with self-attention (SA) in this paper. Three key factors contribute to the model's superior performance in AD. First, the marginal distributions (MDs) of parameters were transformed into conditional probability distributions (CPDs) by incorporating OC variables as conditional inputs in the variational autoencoder (VAE) model, and decoupled modeling of equipment states and external OCs is achieved. Second, by embedding SA modules, the method dynamically adjusts weight allocation of the parameters to capture complex dependencies among them, which can enhance the capability of the model to represent intricate coupling relationships in multi-dimensional parameters. Third, the logarithmic reconstruction probability (LRP), derived from the probabilistic output of SA-CVAE, serves as a unified health indicator (HI) to evaluate the health condition of the GT. The indicator not only accounts for the discrepancy between the reconstructed and original inputs but also incorporates the influence of latent variable (LV) variance on the reconstruction results. Experiments were carried out on one synthetic, one public, and two real-world datasets, with SA-CVAE compared against six leading AD methods. The results demonstrate that under varying OCs, SA-CVAE exhibits superior performance in AD tasks, achieving leading or competitive results across key evaluation metrics.

title: Confidence interval-based robust topology optimization with active learning
exported_title: Confidence interval-based robust topology optimization with active learning

metadata.abstract: Robust topology optimization (RTO) designs material distribution to improve structural performance while reducing its sensitivity to uncertainties. However, for classical probabilistic RTO, it remains challenging to achieve a trade-off between efficiency and applicability to problems involving complex multi-source uncertainties. To address this difficulty, a confidence interval-based RTO (CI-RTO) method is proposed in this paper, which simultaneously improves the structural response and its robustness through minimizing a weighted sum of the median and the width of the confidence interval. The method integrates Monte Carlo simulation (MCS) and the Kriging model to estimate the objective function. Inheriting non-intrusiveness from MCS and imposing no restrictions on input uncertainties, CI-RTO is capable of addressing complex multi-source uncertainties and non-linear relationships between response and random variables. Meanwhile, the Kriging model alleviates the computational burden arising from large-scale sampling, and a confidence interval active learning (CIAL) strategy is developed for its efficient construction. By adaptively improving modeling accuracy around the median and confidence bounds, CIAL significantly reduces the training cost of the Kriging model, thereby further accelerating CI-RTO. In addition, regarding sensitivity analysis, CI-RTO holds a natural advantage over classical RTO methods that minimize mean and standard deviation, since its computational cost is merely three times that of deterministic topology optimization (DTO). The performance of the proposed method is evaluated using four numerical examples, including macro, micro, and 3D design problems, where multiple uncertainties and non-linear responses to uncertain parameters are incorporated. Comparisons with other methods confirm the effectiveness and efficiency of CI-RTO.

title: Estimating node importance in transportation networks: A scalable machine learning approach
exported_title: Estimating node importance in transportation networks: A scalable machine learning approach

metadata.abstract: Urban transportation networks are vulnerable to performance degradation from node-level congestion, such as accidents or capacity overloads. Traditional vulnerability analyses employ iterative traffic assignment to quantify the impact of each congested node on total travel time (TTT). Although accurate, this process results in substantial computational costs and becomes prohibitively slow for large or dynamic networks. To address these limitations, we develop a scalable machine learning framework that predicts the TTT impact of individual node failures. Our model uses features drawn from origin–destination demand data, link attributes, network centrality measures, and socio-economic contexts. We construct an ensemble of four base learners — Random Forests, XGBoost, LightGBM, and Support Vector Classifier — combined via Logistic Regression as a meta-learner to classify nodes into high, medium, and low importance categories, and include a Multi-Layer Perceptron model for comparison. Evaluation across six real-world transportation networks demonstrates that our approach consistently achieves up to 85% classification accuracy while reducing computation time by up to 94%. We enhance interpretability through SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), which identify initial link flow estimates as the most influential predictor. Furthermore, we verify model transferability by training on small variants of the Berlin and Birmingham networks and successfully applying the same models to their full-scale networks and two additional transportation networks. Our results confirm that the proposed framework offers rapid and reliable identification of critical intersections, facilitating more efficient network planning and resilience assessment.

title: A reinforcement learning approach to network-level maintenance planning of co-located road and water infrastructures with interdependencies
exported_title: A reinforcement learning approach to network-level maintenance planning of co-located road and water infrastructures with interdependencies

metadata.abstract: Due to co-location and spatial proximity, deteriorating transportation infrastructure (TI) and water infrastructure (WI) are geographically interdependent, exhibiting complex interactions both within and across systems. Failures from degradation or maintenance disruptions in one system can impair its own performance and cascade into the other. However, many existing studies address long-term maintenance only at the component, subsystem, or single-system level, without fully accounting for interdependencies both within and across co-located infrastructures. This paper proposes a network-wide joint long-term maintenance planning framework that integrates traffic and hydraulic simulations to capture interdependencies within and across multiple infrastructure systems. A reinforcement learning-based optimization model is formulated to minimize the expected cumulative costs of co-located TI and WI systems over a long-term planning horizon while accounting for future uncertainties in the deterioration of roads and pipes. The model jointly quantifies both short-term and long-term economic impacts of joint maintenance decisions at network level by comprehensively investigating diverse topological relationships and interactions between co-located roads and pipes. The framework is further validated through a realistic case study in Ybor City, Tampa, and benchmarked against alternative maintenance strategies, demonstrating cost savings achieved through proactive, coordinated decision-making across interdependent TI and WI systems.

title: Multi-modal graph convolutional network for vessel trajectory prediction based on cooperative intention enhance using conditional variational autoencoder
exported_title: Multi-modal graph convolutional network for vessel trajectory prediction based on cooperative intention enhance using conditional variational autoencoder

metadata.abstract: Advances in maritime instrumentation and measurement (I&M), particularly through the widespread adoption of automatic identification system (AIS), have significantly accelerated the development of intelligent situational awareness systems (ISAS). As a critical component of ISAS, cooperative navigation demands greater accuracy and reliability in vessel trajectory prediction. Nevertheless, challenges arising from complex inter-vessel interactions and implicit intention inference expose limitations in modeling explicit and implicit relationships and ensuring the robustness of trajectory prediction. To address these challenges, we propose a cooperative intention enhance multi-modal graph convolutional network (CIE-MGCN) to learn and predict the future vessel trajectories. The CIE-MGCN is composed of three primary components: Interaction Extractor, Intention Constructor, and Trajectory Generator. In Interaction Extractor, we designed the social-community extractor (SCE) to construct diverse interaction graphs that capture both cooperative and adversarial relationships among vessel trajectories, and the multi-modal transformer (MMT) to fuse explicit interaction features across various modalities. In Intention Constructor, we introduce a conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE)-based approach to infer implicit relationships and capture potential future behavioral variations and multi-modal probability distributions of future trajectories are produced by Trajectory Generator. Extensive experiments on real-world navigation data show that CIE-MGCN outperforms state-of-the-art models in accuracy and robustness, owing to its strong reasoning and learning capabilities. These reliable predictions further support cooperative navigation within ISAS by enhancing coordination and decision-making among multi-vessel.

title: Contrastive decoupling graph neural network with deviation-diffusivity cooperative node selector for equipment remaining useful life prediction
exported_title: Contrastive decoupling graph neural network with deviation-diffusivity cooperative node selector for equipment remaining useful life prediction

metadata.abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have been widely applied to remaining useful life (RUL) prediction driven by multi-source information fusion. However, the conventional GNN-based approaches use the shared node features for both RUL prediction and spatial dependency modeling, which may induce implicit information conflicts. Moreover, they have no effective mechanisms for identifying the weakly correlated nodes, which causes the prediction accuracy to be easily disturbed by noise. To resolve potential information conflicts, we propose a novel node feature contrastive decoupling module (NFCDM). The NFCDM employs a cross-fusion-contrastive decoupling strategy to explicitly decompose node features into global degradation features for RUL prediction and local relational features for spatial dependency modeling. Task-specific contrastive decoupling constraints are further designed to ensure the task relevance and information independence of the decoupled features. In addition, to achieve the effective node screening, a deviation-diffusivity cooperative node selector (DDCS) is proposed. This novel selector is capable of constructing joint evaluation metrics based on the deviation of global degradation features and the information diffusion capability of nodes to adaptively discard redundant nodes. Built upon these two novel modules, the contrastive decoupling graph neural network with deviation-diffusivity cooperative node selector (CDGNN-DDCS) is proposed for RUL prediction. Comparative experiments on public datasets confirm the superiority of the proposed method. Lastly, its engineering practicality is successfully verified via an RUL prediction experiment on actual wind turbines.

title: An efficient graph neural networks surrogate model for slope reliability analysis considering soil spatial variability
exported_title: An efficient graph neural networks surrogate model for slope reliability analysis considering soil spatial variability

metadata.abstract: Soil spatial variability significantly affects slope stability and landslide behaviors, particularly under complex geological conditions where traditional finite element analysis (FEA), while precise, incurs prohibitive computational costs. This study introduces a new surrogate model leveraging graph attention networks (GAT) equipped with sample and aggregate (SAGE) sampling, designed to efficiently handle large-scale data while predicting slope safety factors and identifying potential slip surfaces. The GAT model utilizes a spatial graph construction based on k-dimensional trees (KD-Trees), enabling the effective representation of complex mechanical interactions within the soil. The results indicate the superior performance of this model over traditional machine learning methods such as random forest, feedforward neural networks, support vector regression, and convolutional neural networks, achieving a mean squared error of 0.000218 and an R2 of 0.995. The application of GAT with SAGE sampling highlights the potential of graph neural networks to significantly enhance real-time slope stability monitoring and risk assessment in the geotechnical engineering field, demonstrating a promising direction for computationally efficient surrogate modeling.

title: Reverse Variational Autoencoder: A probabilistic inference framework for structural health monitoring and inverse analysis in engineering
exported_title: Reverse Variational Autoencoder: A probabilistic inference framework for structural health monitoring and inverse analysis in engineering

metadata.abstract: Inverse analysis in structural engineering involves inferring uncertain parameters from limited external observations, which is crucial for structural health monitoring and maintenance. However, real-world applications often face under-constrained problems with multiple possible solutions due to sparse measurements. This study proposes a Bayesian deep learning-based framework, termed Reverse Variational Auto-Encoder (RVAE), to fulfill efficient probabilistic structural inverse analysis. The RVAE framework modifies the original VAE structure to consider the causality relationship underlying inverse problems, enabling a semi-supervised learning paradigm for label-agnostic scenarios. The effectiveness of the RVAE framework is validated through a grid structure experiment. The implemented model successfully reveals all possible solutions for bending amplitudes, strains, and node displacements, with root-mean-squared reconstruction errors of 1.21 %, 2.77 %, and 1.36 %, respectively. A comparative analysis is conducted between mainstream inversion algorithms and RVAE. The results demonstrate that while all the other inversion algorithms achieve low reconstruction errors, they provide single-solution estimation, thus highlighting RVAE's capability to provide the most comprehensive information. RVAE's capability for real-time probabilistic estimation of structural parameters is further discussed and demonstrated in a full-scale bridge tower experiment, where it utilizes multi-sensor data to infer critical structural parameters, showing strong adaptability to noisy, incomplete, and heterogeneous monitoring inputs. In summary, RVAE tackles the challenges of large-scale parameter inversion in engineering structures by enabling efficient probabilistic inference under sparse observations. It supports semi-supervised learning in label-agnostic scenarios and real-time prediction of multiple plausible solutions, thereby fulfilling the synchronous updating requirements of digital twin systems.

title: Explainable artificial intelligence based intelligent fault diagnosis: A systematic review from applications to insights
exported_title: Explainable artificial intelligence based intelligent fault diagnosis: A systematic review from applications to insights

metadata.abstract: Deep learning (DL)-based intelligent fault diagnosis (IFD) has become a key enabler for condition-based maintenance, yet its “black-box” nature limits explainability and reliability. Explainability concerns understanding the model’s decision process, including the physical meaning and contribution of extracted features, while reliability addresses the rationality and stability of diagnostic results under varying conditions. As explainability analysis reveals potential biases and irrational dependencies, it serves as the foundation for improving reliability, spurring extensive research on explainable intelligent fault diagnosis (XIFD). This survey first reviews the core components of IFD to clarify how XIFD enhances model transparency, and then categorizes existing approaches into ante-hoc and post-hoc methods. Ante-hoc methods focus on building inherently interpretable models, whereas post-hoc methods explain results through external analysis. Then, we provide the usage and disadvantages of existing post-hoc XIFD methods and emphasize the significance of ante-hoc XIFD by giving insights into the most popular signal processing-informed IFD methods. Finally, we consolidate the pressing challenges that necessitate immediate attention within the realm of XIFD research, and offer insights into promising prospects for future research endeavors. The library is available at: https://github.com/HazeDT/Awesome-Explainable-IFD-Library.

title: Evacuation under terrorist attacks: A crowd congestion control method based on deep reinforcement learning
exported_title: Evacuation under terrorist attacks: A crowd congestion control method based on deep reinforcement learning

metadata.abstract: Terrorist attacks pose severe security challenges for crowd evacuation, especially in high-density scenarios where panic-induced congestion significantly increases the number of casualties. Although existing research mainly focuses on the direct impact of attacks, the critical issue of low evacuation efficiency and increased mortality rates caused by congestion is often overlooked. Therefore, effectively regulating crowd congestion during terrorist attacks to enhance evacuation efficiency and reduce the number of casualties is a major challenge. To address this, this paper proposes a crowd congestion control method based on deep reinforcement learning under terrorist attack scenarios to enhance evacuation efficiency and safety. First, a congestion–threat coupled cellular automaton (CTCA) is constructed to simulate individual risk-avoidance behavior in a threatening environment. Second, by introducing the attack-aware Dueling Double Deep Q Network (D3QN), a congestion control method based on attack-aware D3QN and CTCA is proposed to learn optimal evacuation strategies that avoid high-risk and high-density areas. Finally, a crowd evacuation navigation system integrating CTCA and D3QN is developed. The experimental results show that the proposed method demonstrates outstanding performance in reducing congestion levels, shortening evacuation times, and lowering mortality rates. It provides theoretical support and technical tools for public safety emergency response systems.

title: A cascaded machine learning model for identification of ship breach characteristics during flooding using sensor data fusion
exported_title: A cascaded machine learning model for identification of ship breach characteristics during flooding using sensor data fusion

metadata.abstract: Water ingress in damaged ships can severely impair navigation and cause sinking. Accurate breach identification is vital for effective incident response. Due to multi-characteristic interaction of breach parameters, minor identification errors can cumulatively lead to significant inaccuracies in subsequent flooding assessment. This study proposes a cascaded machine learning model for breach identification of damaged ship using sensor data. First, the model employs temporal convolutional network to estimate floodwater volume by integrating data from internal water level and floating state sensors. Then, the model combines support vector regression and artificial neural network to identify and fine-tune breach parameters using the floodwater volume data. The hyperparameters of the models are automatically tuned based on particle swarm optimization. Strategies for training data generation and sensor fusion are explored. The model effectiveness is validated through tests on a barge under transient and progressive flooding, demonstrating consistent results with benchmark data for breach parameters and flooding consequences.

title: Human-machine interaction for maritime transport using a data-driven approach
exported_title: Human-machine interaction for maritime transport using a data-driven approach

metadata.abstract: Increasing digitalization in maritime transportation has introduced new challenges for the industry to redefine seafarer competencies linked with autonomous systems. Effective interaction between human operators and machine subsystems is becoming essential for both conventional ships and Maritime Autonomous Surface Ships (MASS). This study aims to quantify human-machine interaction in maritime transport through a comprehensive analytical framework. It employs a Tree Augmented Naive Bayesian Network (TAN-BN) to reveal the network structure, mutual information analysis to quantify interactions, True Risk Influence analysis to identify dominant interaction factors, and graph theory to assess system-level interaction effects. The novelties of this study are as follows: 1) propose a risk-based model to identify critical risk influencing factors (RIFs) in human-machine systems for maritime transport; 2) analyze the interdependencies among RIFs and ship machinery malfunctions using BN; 3) quantify human-machine interaction efficiency using graph theory, providing new implications for the design and deployment of automation in maritime operations. The results show an increase of 2.7% in system efficiency if the seafarers' knowledge competency issue is resolved, i.e., automation simplifies operational processes and reduces human workload. These findings highlight the relationship between seafarer competencies and machinery deficiencies, providing guidelines for maritime authorities to redefine seafarer competencies and for stakeholders to prioritize the autonomy of onboard subsystems. In particular, the more negative the effects of competencies (i.e., knowledge) on systematic performance, the more priority should be given to replacing them with the autonomy sub-machine.

title: Dynamic ensemble model incorporating deep reinforcement learning for earthquake casualty prediction
exported_title: Dynamic ensemble model incorporating deep reinforcement learning for earthquake casualty prediction

metadata.abstract: Accurate prediction of earthquake casualties is crucial to inform decision-making for efficient government rescue operations. This paper proposes a Stacking Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II Double Deep Q-Network Dynamic Ensemble (SND-DE), a unified prediction framework that integrates a two-layer Stacking architecture, Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II) for multi-objective parameter optimization and a Double Deep Q-Network (DDQN) decision agent for dynamic parameter selection. Within SND-DE, the ensemble prediction model utilizes a two-layer stacking structure, selecting high-performance base models and meta-models through experiments and employs a five-fold cross-validation method for prediction. A multi-objective optimization algorithm optimizes the key parameters of the prediction model, aiming to minimize both bias and variance of the prediction. Embedding the non-dominated solutions of the key parameters of the prediction model into the DDQN environment enables the model to adapt to the characteristics of different disaster scenarios and dynamically parameterize the model to reduce prediction errors. The effectiveness of the proposed model is comprehensively evaluated through a series of experiments, whose results indicate that: (1) the SND-DE model is well-trained, exhibits high predictive accuracy and achieves a coefficient of determination (R2) of 0.95279; (2) the performance of the ensemble model surpasses that of all individual base models; (3) the NSGA-II optimization algorithm effectively reduces the model's bias and variance; (4) the DDQN model exhibits strong convergence and achieves high reward values.

title: BMTR-former: Accelerating RUL prediction on scarce and censored data via bayesian-based multi-task reconstruction transformer
exported_title: BMTR-former: Accelerating RUL prediction on scarce and censored data via bayesian-based multi-task reconstruction transformer

metadata.abstract: To overcome the limitations of data censoring in Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction, we introduce BMTR-Former, a Bayesian Multi-Task Reconstruction Transformer. Our framework uniquely treats censored data not as a limitation but as a resource, integrating a supervised RUL prediction task with a self-supervised signal reconstruction task. This multi-task paradigm leverages all available trajectories to learn robust degradation patterns. The self-supervised component uses both censored and uncensored data to learn degradation patterns, enhancing RUL prediction. A hierarchical Bayesian model first denoises sensor signals to provide clean inputs for the Transformer core. Experiments show BMTR-Former excels on highly censored datasets, not only achieving state-of-the-art accuracy but also demonstrating remarkable training efficiency and rapid convergence, decisively outperforming competing models. By transforming censored data into a key asset for generalization, our work offers a new, data-efficient paradigm for industrial prognostics.

title: Degradation process modeling and data-driven lifetime prediction for BGA specimen during small sample electromigration test
exported_title: Degradation process modeling and data-driven lifetime prediction for BGA specimen during small sample electromigration test

metadata.abstract: Electromigration (EM) poses a critical threat to Ball Grid Array (BGA) reliability, yet its lifetime prediction is challenged by limited and heterogeneous data. To address the limitation, this study develops a hybrid physics-informed uncertainty modeling framework for predicting BGA lifetime under small sample conditions. Electromigration experiments at three temperature-current stress levels confirmed copper redistribution layer (Cu RDL) narrowing as the dominant degradation mechanism. Based on this insight, the proposed model couples a simplified degradation formulation derived from relative resistance change with an uncertain differential equation (UDE) to quantify epistemic uncertainty, enabling belief reliable life estimation for individual specimens. Furthermore, a data analysis method for lifetime prediction integrating the Weibull uncertainty distribution, uncertain measure consistency, and Black equation extends lifetime prediction across operating conditions and ensures robustness under sparse data. Comparative analyses with other process-based degradation models and traditional lifetime prediction method based on regression-Weibull-Black equation show that the proposed method achieves superior fitting accuracy, improved stability of current and thermal sensitivities, and more conservative MTBF estimates. These findings highlight the method’s potential to support reliability-oriented design and preventive maintenance planning for high performance electronic packaging.

title: Data-driven transformer-based explainable deep learning model for real-time TBM performance prediction
exported_title: Data-driven transformer-based explainable deep learning model for real-time TBM performance prediction

metadata.abstract: Aiming to effectively and efficiently predict tunnel boring machine (TBM) penetration rates to assist in guiding the operation management, this research proposes TransXTBMNet, a Transformer-based explainable network designed for predicting TBM penetration rates in real-time, which integrates ensemble bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) and improved Transformer to capture the complex interative relationship between operational parameters of TBM and penetration rates, enabling real-time precise predictions. Furthermore, the method encompasses various components: the data preparation process, the SHAP-based model explainability, a loss function, and performance metrics to collectively enhance robust data quality and ensure accurate predictions in dynamic excavation environments. Validation on the real TBM operation dataset demonstrates TransXTBMNet’s exceptional performance, with metrics like Mean Squared Error (MSE) = 0.2529, Root MSE (RMSE) = 0.5029, Mean Absolute Error (MAE) = 0.2991, Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) = 1.4984 %, and R2 = 0.9770. Comparative analysis shows superior results over other state-of-the-art methods such as conventional recurrent architectures (simple RNN (SRNN), GRU, LSTM) and their bidirectional variants (BiSRNN, BiGRU). SHAP analysis reveals that penetration rate at the previous time step, long with thrust groups A and F play crucial roles in predicting penetration rates. Additionally, the proposed method exhibits improved performance when considering the recorded penetration rate data, highlighting its capability to provide a better performance. Overall, the proposed method TransXTBMNet proves to be an effective and efficient solution in predicting TBM performance, providing valuable real-time guidance for optimizing TBM operations.

title: An uncertainty-guided contrastive learning method for OOD detection in trustworthy fault diagnosis
exported_title: An uncertainty-guided contrastive learning method for OOD detection in trustworthy fault diagnosis

metadata.abstract: In the field of Prognostics Health Management (PHM), the “black-box” nature of deep learning-based intelligent fault diagnosis raises concerns about reliability in safety-critical applications. Traditional deterministic networks provide point estimates only, making them inadequate for quantifying prediction uncertainty and detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) samples. To address these limitations, this paper explicitly models feature representations as Gaussian distributions, thereby preserving both predictive information and data-inherent uncertainty. Building on this foundation, we introduce a distribution-level contrastive learning strategy that enhances the separability between in-distribution and OOD samples while avoiding the challenge of negative pair selection in conventional contrastive learning. This joint design establishes a more reliable decision boundary and improves model trustworthiness. Experiments on two representative testbeds — the planetary gearbox and the main gearbox (MGB) — demonstrate that the proposed method not only achieves superior OOD detection but also maintains high in-distribution diagnostic accuracy under noisy conditions. These results highlight the method’s potential for trustworthy deployment in real-world industrial fault diagnosis.

title: A novel AI-driven framework of collaborative intelligent operation and maintenance in cloud-edge computing power networks
exported_title: A novel AI-driven framework of collaborative intelligent operation and maintenance in cloud-edge computing power networks

metadata.abstract: With the global proliferation of computing power networks driven by rapid IoT and artificial intelligence advancement, cloud-edge computing power networks (CECPN) have become critical foundations for modern digital infrastructure. However, their distributed and heterogeneous nature introduces significant cybersecurity vulnerabilities threatening data transmission reliability, thereby posing substantial challenges to operation and maintenance (O&M) management. Current research lacks comprehensive modeling across CECPN's entire data transmission lifecycle and rarely addresses heterogeneous resource allocation strategies under cyberattack scenarios. This paper proposes an AI-driven collaborative O&M framework for CECPN that optimizes multi-phase data transmission reliability recovery and costs through heterogeneous allocation of communication, computing, and operational resources under cyberattack. A case study is conducted on a 20-unit CECPN simulated environment. This study demonstrates three distinct O&M approaches: cost-oriented, reliability-oriented, and balanced strategies. The results validate the framework's capability to generate diverse solutions across various attack scenarios and recovery time windows.

title: Lightweight multimodal LLM-empowered dual-agent collaboration for reliable defect detection and maintenance recommendation in tunnel infrastructure
exported_title: Lightweight multimodal LLM-empowered dual-agent collaboration for reliable defect detection and maintenance recommendation in tunnel infrastructure

metadata.abstract: Accurate identification of tunnel defects and maintenance recommendations are crucial for resilient tunnel operations and sustainable urban underground development. Although numerous automated systems have been developed for tunnel defect detection, existing approaches struggle with limited semantic understanding, poor interpretability, and difficulty generating standard-compliant decisions. To address these challenges, this study proposes a lightweight multimodal LLM-empowered dual-agent collaboration framework for tunnel infrastructure maintenance, with three core innovations that advance existing research: (1) Modular Decoupling of Detection and Reasoning: We explicitly separate visual defect recognition (via a fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL-7B vision-language model) from regulatory-compliant maintenance reasoning (via a LightRAG-enhanced agent), solving the interpretability and traceability limitations of end-to-end tunnel AI systems. (2) Cost-Efficient Training & Lightweight Deployment: Using 4-bit quantization (Unsloth framework) and LoRA, we fine-tune the 7B-parameter model at ∼USD $5 per session (Google Colab Pro+) and enable real-time operation on consumer-grade GPUs (e.g., NVIDIA RTX 4050), eliminating reliance on high-end proprietary hardware. (3) LightRAG-Powered Standards-Compliant Reasoning: The LightRAG module integrates clause-level knowledge graphs and hybrid vector-graph retrieval, ensuring maintenance recommendations strictly adhere to national/regional standards (e.g., JT/T 790–2023) and mitigating LLM hallucination risks. This dual-agent design enhances tunnel resilience by enabling interpretable, scalable, and compliance-driven maintenance, with experimental validation on 8928 Shanghai tunnel images confirming superior performance over baseline models by ROUGE-1 (0.8342), ROUGE-2 (0.7389), BLEU (0.68), and semantic similarity (0.9830) scores.

title: A remaining useful life estimation method based on meta contrastive learning
exported_title: A remaining useful life estimation method based on meta contrastive learning

metadata.abstract: Precise remaining useful life (RUL) estimation can effectively enhance the reliability and safety of industrial machinery. While deep learning methods have demonstrated strong potential in this area, their effectiveness is often limited by the scarcity of labeled data, which is both costly and time-consuming to obtain in industrial applications. Therefore, a novel RUL estimation method based on meta contrastive learning is proposed to construct an efficient semi-supervised learning process, which specifically targets the challenges of limited labeled data by deeply mining the underlying degradation information within the vast amounts of unlabeled data. First, a meta contrastive learning algorithm is proposed to ensure that the contrastive information derived from unlabeled data positively influence the model’s performance on labeled data. Meanwhile, a meta-update strategy is designed to mitigate overfitting and catastrophic forgetting, effectively improving the feature extraction potential and generalization ability of deep learning structures. Additionally, a weight optimization strategy is proposed to adaptively adjust the weight factor of the semi-supervised learning process based on the performance of the supervised task, thus enhancing the flexibility and effectiveness of semi-supervised learning. The proposed method is validated on the turbofan engine and wind turbine gearbox datasets, demonstrating its effectiveness and superiority.

title: Risk source identification and prevention for metro driven by large language models: A new approach to enhancing system reliability and safety
exported_title: Risk source identification and prevention for metro driven by large language models: A new approach to enhancing system reliability and safety

metadata.abstract: Hazard source identification in metro operation and maintenance faces challenges like high data dimensionality, data heterogeneity and difficult data structuring. Existing general knowledge graphs fail to fully consider domain - specific business logic, leading to low identification accuracy and frequent catastrophic incidents. To solve this, this paper develops a new identification method based on the dual knowledge self -verification large language model, which boosts accuracy and enables efficient targeted control. It establishes a three - dimensional “root cause – hazard source - hazardous event” framework, integrates In - Context Learning with Chain of Thought for reasoning, uses Transformer multi - head self - attention to extract knowledge triplets, applies dual verification to build hierarchical causal knowledge graphs, and creates a risk quantification model. Validation with metro data shows domain knowledge extraction has an 86.6% F1 score (18.1% higher than UIE model). Targeting the critical “inadequate management and maintenance” node (78.4% of cumulative disaster severity weight) cuts accident rate by 16.66%. This research enables a shift from passive to proactive metro disaster risk control.

title: Enhancing safety management: A data-driven approach for accident mitigation in a steel industry
exported_title: Enhancing safety management: A data-driven approach for accident mitigation in a steel industry

metadata.abstract: Efficient analysis of accident data is necessary for managing industrial safety. Since this data is frequently categorical, the main analysis factors that we need to use are frequency and causality. We can develop risk assessments and mitigation strategies from these analyses to prevent future accidents. Heterogeneous data might conceal important correlations between variables, making traditional methods of causality analysis difficult to use. To address this, we have used Latent Class Clustering (LCC) to transform such data into a more homogeneous form, minimizing the reliance on expert opinions. Correspondence Analysis (CA) is then employed to visualize latent classes in a 2D space, aiding in categorization for causal analysis. We have found the direction and strength of cause-effect links by using Bayesian Networks (BN), although it necessitates a balance between algorithmic learning and expert knowledge. Finally, we have extracted safety rules from the homogeneous categorical safety data from a steel factory using CA and t-Distributed Stochastic Neighbor Embedding (t-SNE) in this work, which offers important insights for safety management.

title: A sample-efficient transfer learning framework for industrial remaining useful life prediction leveraging large language models
exported_title: A sample-efficient transfer learning framework for industrial remaining useful life prediction leveraging large language models

metadata.abstract: Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction is fundamental to industrial Prognostics and Health Management (PHM). However, existing models struggle to process high-dimensional, multi-condition sensor data, generalize across varying operating conditions, and perform well with limited labeled data. To address these challenges, we propose a sample-efficient RUL prediction framework based on a transferable Large Language Model (LLM), which captures complex temporal dependencies in sensor data while reducing pre-processing requirements. The framework integrates two core innovations: a transferable LLM backbone that automates feature extraction from complex sensor data, and a dual-score sample selection strategy that significantly improves learning efficiency by identifying the most informative samples for transfer learning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the framework achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance across diverse operating conditions using a single hyperparameter configuration, significantly reducing the computational overhead and domain expertise requirements that limit the scalability of existing methods. Beyond predictive accuracy, this study offers insights into its internal mechanisms, showing how it dynamically prioritizes sensor data to capture critical degradation patterns across varying conditions. These findings enhance model interpretability by linking data-driven predictions to physical processes. By addressing key challenges such as data efficiency, feature extraction, and transferability, the framework offers a reliable solution for industrial signal processing, improving the cost-effectiveness and robustness of PHM strategies across diverse operational domains.

title: An aero-engine remaining useful life prediction method based on deformable convolutional residual attention enhanced Kolmogorov-Arnold networks with prediction advance and shape constraints
exported_title: An aero-engine remaining useful life prediction method based on deformable convolutional residual attention enhanced Kolmogorov-Arnold networks with prediction advance and shape constraints

metadata.abstract: Improving the practicality and reliability of remaining useful life (RUL) prediction requires achieving more accurate, earlier, and more relevant forecasts. However, existing methods are limited by the weak feature extraction ability of fully connected layers and the inability of conventional loss functions to balance early prediction and trend consistency. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a prediction model base on deformable convolutional residual attention (DCRA) modules with Kolmogorov–Arnold networks (KAN). An early prediction and shape constraint loss function (ESLF) is further designed to enhance model reliability. Specifically, the DCRA module adaptively extracts multi-scale degradation features through deformable convolution kernels, while KAN serves as a regressor to improve feature mapping. Moreover, the main spline function of KAN reflects the occurrence of degradation, thereby improving model interpretability. The proposed ESLF is asymmetric and improves the similarity between predicted and actual RUL sequences. Comparative and ablation experiments conducted on the CMAPSS and NCMAPSS datasets verify the superior prediction performance of the proposed method. The average RMSE and Score are reduced by 5.19 % and 9.28 % on CMAPSS, and by 4.63 % and 9.47 % on NCMAPSS, respectively. These results demonstrate the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed approach in practical health management scenarios.

title: Self-data-driven remaining useful life prediction of rotating machinery under time-varying operating conditions based on a two-stage hybrid state-space model
exported_title: Self-data-driven remaining useful life prediction of rotating machinery under time-varying operating conditions based on a two-stage hybrid state-space model

metadata.abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is the foundation of predictive maintenance and provides an effective way to reduce operational and maintenance costs. However, time-varying operating conditions (TVOCs) and limited run-to-failure data at industrial sites significantly hinder the performance of traditional RUL prediction methods. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposes a novel self-data-driven RUL prediction method for rotating machinery (RM) under TVOCs. First, inspired by time-varying response systems in control theory, a two-stage hybrid state-space model (HSSM) is developed by combining the dynamic modeling capabilities of state-space models with the nonlinear fitting ability of neural networks. This model innovatively integrates TVOCs into the mathematical formulation of the dynamic degradation process of RM. It aims to describe the functional relationship among operating conditions, system states, and response signals during the entire life cycle of RM under TVOCs, thereby avoiding the impact on RUL prediction caused by the coupling of operating conditions and system states. Then, based on the extended Kalman filter algorithm and the monitoring data generated by the system itself, an alternating parameter update strategy is introduced to solve the system state within the HSSM, enabling real-time tracking of RM degradation. Furthermore, an adaptive model selection strategy is proposed to dynamically identify the optimal state degradation model. This method effectively overcomes the problem of insufficient historical run-to-failure data for offline model training. In addition, the design characteristics of the HSSM at different stages provide an integrated solution for both anomaly detection and RUL prediction in RM. The effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method are validated through both simulation and experimental studies.

title: A prediction strategy for embankment piping occurrence based on comprehensive feature selection and machine learning
exported_title: A prediction strategy for embankment piping occurrence based on comprehensive feature selection and machine learning

metadata.abstract: Piping is a critical hazard in embankment structures, posing risks to public safety. Traditional piping prediction models are often computationally complex and time-consuming. This study proposed a piping occurrence prediction strategy that integrates feature selection and machine learning (ML) to monitor embankment conditions. Taking the Yangtze River embankment as the dataset, comprehensive feature selection techniques (including Pearson analysis, random forest feature importance, and SHAP values) were employed to analyze the importance and correlation of factors influencing piping. The influential factors were ranked as follows: overburden thickness H (0.32), void ratio e (0.24), water level difference ∆h (0.17), compressibility coefficient av (0.12), dry density ρd (0.07), and effective cohesion c'(0.03). To address the impact of an imbalance dataset on the ML prediction model, variational autoencoder (VAE) technology was used to process the original piping data, ensuring a balance dataset. To develop an accurate prediction model, the parameters of backpropagation (BP), support vector machines (SVM), and EXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) were optimized using genetic algorithms (GA), particle swarm optimization (PSO), and grey wolf optimization (GWO). The research results showed that the GA-XGBoost model achieved the best performance, with an R2 of 0.96, RMSE of 0.10, and MAE of 0.06 on the Yangxin validation set. And the proposed model outperformed existing methods on prediction accuracy. Additionally, a piping prediction platform was developed, providing an intuitive interface that facilitates quick retrieval of predictions, enabling engineers to make informed decisions with ease.

title: AK-TSYS: An enhanced active learning Kriging model for time-dependent system reliability analysis
exported_title: AK-TSYS: An enhanced active learning Kriging model for time-dependent system reliability analysis

metadata.abstract: Complex engineering systems involve multiple failure modes, components, and temporal parameters, all of which pose significant challenges for time-dependent system reliability analysis (TDSRA). In this study, a novel framework named AK-TSYS, an active learning Kriging-based method for TDSRA, is proposed to enhance the conventional AK-MCS (active learning combining Kriging and Monte Carlo simulation) framework. Within the proposed method, initial training samples are selected to construct Kriging models for all failure modes. A two-stage active learning strategy is then adopted: in the global exploration stage, a hybrid learning function integrates composite expected least global (ELG) and expected improvement (EI) functions to identify optimal random variables, time instances, and failure mode indexes; the subsequent local exploitation defines a localized region around the candidate global optimal point to find a higher-quality learning point, thereby iteratively refining the surrogate model. The training process terminates when an error-based system stopping criterion is satisfied, ensuring convergence with improved computational efficiency and accuracy. The system failure probability is finally estimated using the system structure functions, which are applicable to series, parallel, and mixed systems. The AK-TSYS is demonstrated through three numerical examples and four practical applications, including a parallel Daniels system, a remote vector reducer, mixed systems, and a series system analyzed by finite element simulation. Furthermore, a sensitivity analysis systematically evaluates the influence of key parameters, including the stopping criterion threshold, initial training points, and local exploitation radius. Based on the findings, practical implementation guidelines of AK-TSYS are provided.

title: A self-calibrating digital twin for space thermionic nuclear reactors under fault conditions
exported_title: A self-calibrating digital twin for space thermionic nuclear reactors under fault conditions

metadata.abstract: Space nuclear power systems operate unattended for extended periods, making them susceptible to failures. Furthermore, spatial constraints necessitate sparse sensor deployment, which makes comprehensive operational status monitoring difficult. Therefore, a Digital Twin (DT) model capable of characterizing the system's unmeasurable states is crucial for ensuring its reliability and operational safety. Faults or performance degradation can introduce parameter uncertainties that severely compromise DT accuracy. To address this, a DT model for a space thermionic nuclear reactor (STNR) has been developed. This model is underpinned by a physics-based mechanism model and incorporates Transformer and eXtreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) to achieve initial state synchronization. Furthermore, an online calibration mechanism is implemented using Model Predictive Control (MPC) and the Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy (CMA-ES). Following sensitivity analysis to identify adjustable parameters, CMA-ES then finds the optimal parameters that minimize deviation, thereby correcting the transient evolution behavior of the STNR. The root mean squared error (RMSE) for state synchronization on the test set was under 0.0878, and the relative errors of online calibration under fault conditions were below 0.6 %. Furthermore, noise tests and fault sensitivity analyses were conducted, confirming the method meets engineering requirements. Therefore, the method shows promising potential in deep space exploration.

title: A generative modeling method to quantify the long-term benefit of neural-network-based RUL predictions to maintenance
exported_title: A generative modeling method to quantify the long-term benefit of neural-network-based RUL predictions to maintenance

metadata.abstract: Many remaining useful life (RUL) prediction models rely on neural networks. These models focus on predictive accuracy at the component level, but their impact on system-level maintenance remains underexplored. Quantifying this effect is difficult because maintenance decisions are often optimized from long-term simulations. These simulations do not provide real-time measurements for RUL prediction, making direct use of specific prognostic models challenging. To address this gap, we propose a maintenance optimization framework that uses generative modeling with a generative adversarial network (GAN) to create realistic prognostic trajectories for system-level cost assessment. Feature adaptation is added to the GAN to ensure that generated trajectories retain key statistical properties, such as accuracy, timeliness, and credibility, seen in actual model evaluations. This framework allows the benefits of prognostic models to be assessed probabilistically and offers guidance on whether to include prognostics in maintenance planning. A case study on wind farm maintenance demonstrates the effectiveness of the method. Although the wind farm example considers only limited subsystem dependencies, the framework is not restricted to this configuration. The approach is flexible and can be extended to systems with more complex dependencies by adjusting maintenance policies.

title: EnergyMatch: A long-tailed semi-supervised learning framework for cross-domain fault diagnosis
exported_title: EnergyMatch: A long-tailed semi-supervised learning framework for cross-domain fault diagnosis

metadata.abstract: Achieving nearly-unbiased fault diagnosis with long-tailed labeled source domain is vital. Semi-supervised learning (SSL) methods, leveraging pseudo-labeling and consistency regularization, offer promising solutions for handling imbalanced data. However, variations in working conditions cause feature distribution shifts and potential class distribution shifts in the unlabeled target domain, where the specific class distribution remains unknown. These challenges significantly diminish the performance of conventional SSL methods. To address these issues, we propose EnergyMatch, a novel long-tailed SSL framework for cross-domain fault diagnosis under unknown target class distributions. EnergyMatch builds upon a classic SSL method FixMatch, which uses pseudo labels of weakly augmented instances to train strongly augmented ones. We introduce a double-classifier architecture: the balanced classifier dynamically estimates the target class distribution to guide logit adjustment for pseudo labels generated by the standard classifier. Additionally, we design two energy-based strategies: a free energy-based alignment loss to mitigate feature distribution shifts and an energy-based instance removal module to discard high-uncertainty instances and select more reliable pseudo-labeled instances with dynamically adjusted confidence thresholds. Extensive experiments on bearing and gearbox datasets validate the proposed EnergyMatch, demonstrating its effectiveness in addressing distribution shifts and improving classification performance in challenging scenarios under varying target class distributions.

title: An unsupervised long-tailed fine-grained few-shot fault diagnosis method based on feature space adjustment strategy
exported_title: An unsupervised long-tailed fine-grained few-shot fault diagnosis method based on feature space adjustment strategy

metadata.abstract: In the operation of mechanical equipment, fault data often display an implicit long-tailed distribution, making manual labeling labor-intensive. Moreover, traditional fault diagnosis methods struggle to identify fault causes from a fine-grained perspective without labels. Based on those, an unsupervised long-tailed fine-grained few-shot fault diagnosis method, USL-F4SA, is proposed, which dynamically enhances batches through a queue mechanism and applies indicators and auxiliary sets to construct a class balance mechanism in the feature space. Initially, K-means clustering identifies cluster centers of the original training set, the sparsity of clustering features is used to detect tail classes. Samples with high cosine similarity to the original training set are selected from an auxiliary dataset to balance the distribution of tail classes. Then, a dynamic queue is introduced to find the nearest neighbor for each sample, which is added as a positive sample to the batch. The optimal transport algorithm samples the queue, ensuring optimal assignment between current batch embeddings and the queue, allowing dynamic adaptation to new data. Finally, an indicator assigns indexes to all samples, ensuring correct sample pairing and distinguishing samples from different distributions. Validated on public datasets, USL-F4SA outperforms state-of-the-art methods in predicting unseen fine-grained faults (code available at https://github.com/zhiqan/USL-F4SA).

title: Improved AHP and dual-hidden layer adaptive regularized neural network model for the quantitative risk assessment of oil and gas pipelines
exported_title: Improved AHP and dual-hidden layer adaptive regularized neural network model for the quantitative risk assessment of oil and gas pipelines

metadata.abstract: Conventional risk assessment of oil and gas pipelines primarily relies on expert judgment, which suffers from limited generalizability, high uncertainty and subjectivity, frequently leading to imprecise outcomes. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a risk evaluation model (ImAHP-DHARN) for oil and gas pipelines based on an improved analytic hierarchy process (AHP) and a dual-hidden-layer adaptive regularized neural network (DHARN) model. First, a dynamic frequency-consequence matrix is employed to enable dynamic updates of risk values using five significant key factors: corrosion factor, structural defect, third party damage, natural disaster, and physical damage. Second, AHP is integrated with a comprehensive weighting framework to determine indicator weights, offering improved accuracy. Third, the DHARN model is developed, incorporating tansig-Softmax activation, L2 regularization, and early stopping to mitigate overfitting. Finally, Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) module is implemented to interpret model outputs and quantify the relative importance of indicators, providing insights into risk prioritization. The proposed ImAHP-DHARN model was validated using PHMSA pipeline accident data, achieving an accuracy of 98.3 %, outperforming SVM (93.3 %) and LVQ (98.0 %). In Monte Carlo adversarial testing (e.g., earthquake scenarios superimposed with internal corrosion), the model exhibits a misjudgment rate of only 1.3 %, underscoring its robustness. The SHAP analysis further highlights corrosion prevention T3 as the highest-priority risk factor, providing valuable reference for pipeline risk management. In summary, the ImAHP-DHARN model significantly enhances the objectivity, generalization capability, robustness of pipeline risk assessment. Beyond this domain, this methodology can be extended to other complex industrial systems, providing a robust framework for risk assessment.

title: Prediction of navigation aid malfunction based on hash chain-optimized FP-growth and gradient boosting random forest
exported_title: Prediction of navigation aid malfunction based on hash chain-optimized FP-growth and gradient boosting random forest

metadata.abstract: Causal analysis and prediction of navigation aid malfunctions are essential for waterway safety and maritime traffic efficiency. Existing research has largely been confined to shallow analyses of navigation aid status perception and factors influencing malfunctions, lacking in-depth exploration of the complex nonlinear causal mechanism, which limits the capability for high-precision prediction of navigation aid malfunctions. To address this issue, this study first developed a hash chain-optimized directional constraint FP-growth algorithm to mine association rules between the causes and the malfunctions. Then, the extracted rules were integrated as features into the original dataset for data augmentation. Finally, this study employed a hyperparameter-optimized gradient boosting random forest algorithm to predict navigation aid malfunctions. The results indicate that ship collision is the primary cause of navigation aid malfunctions, and river discharge is the key environmental factor. Moreover, through improvements in data augmentation and algorithm optimization, the proposed method outperforms the baseline model, achieving improvements of 8.6 %, 7.4 %, 6.3 %, 8.2 %, 4.7 %, and 7.6 % in Precision, Recall, F1-Score, Accuracy, AUC, and AUPR, respectively. This research methodology effectively identifies the key causes of navigation aid malfunctions and enhances prediction accuracy, providing robust decision support for the intelligent maintenance of navigation aids and waterway safety management.

title: Long-term resilience assessment of bridge networks using data-driven seismic analysis method for deteriorating bridges
exported_title: Long-term resilience assessment of bridge networks using data-driven seismic analysis method for deteriorating bridges

metadata.abstract: Understanding the long-term seismic resilience of bridge networks is essential to disaster management of transportation infrastructures. For that purpose, a long-term seismic resilience assessment methodology for bridge networks is proposed. It encompasses seismic hazards, structural vulnerabilities, post-earthquake functionality losses, etc., as well as their inherent uncertainties. During that process, two major challenges warrant attention, (1) rapidly capture the time-variant performance of regional bridges under both sudden earthquakes and continuous deterioration effects, and (2) comprehensively evaluate the post-disaster functionality and resilience of bridge networks. To address them, a data-driven method is developed for rapid seismic analysis of regional highway bridges, based on which the residual bridge-, edge-, path-, and network-functionalities can be simulated. Further, this study delves into the functionalities of bridge networks, pioneering a novel set of multi-dimensional seismic resilience metrics. Finally, the long-term seismic resilience of a bridge network in China is investigated as a case study. The results indicate the effects of damage accumulation of the bridge network can result in about 35% resilience decrease, highlighting the necessity of considering deterioration effects in resilience assessment.

title: Causal modeling and risk assessment of runway excursion events via interpretable machine learning
exported_title: Causal modeling and risk assessment of runway excursion events via interpretable machine learning

metadata.abstract: Runway excursions remain a persistent threat to flight safety and operational reliability. The causal chains behind these events are often unclear under complex weather and workload conditions. This study identifies and quantifies the triggers and pathways that lead to runway excursion risk. We analyze 1345 Boeing 737-700 flights using Quick Access Recorder data. An XGBoost model with SHAP values screens nonlinear drivers. We then apply the Independent Component Analysis Linear Non-Gaussian Acyclic model to infer directed and weighted links among sequential exceedances. A Bayesian network estimates trigger probabilities, average treatment effects, and joint risks. Our main contribution is the integration of interpretable learning and causal discovery in a single, queryable graph. Results confirm key triggers: angle of attack asymmetry, elevated radio altitude near touchdown, and delayed thrust reverser deployment. The network shows path dependence, convergence from multiple sources, and escalation along high-impact chains. In a counterfactual policy test, we increase the share of landings with normal bank and a normal 50 ft to touchdown distance by 1.5 percent and reduce the share with small bank and long float by 1 percent. This lowers the estimated probability of severe excessive total landing distance from 11.7 percent to 10.0 percent. A 1 percent increase in the favorable scenario lowers this probability by 0.14 percentage points. Findings remain stable in robust bootstrap tests and noise sensitivity checks. These insights support targeted training and procedures that prioritize touchdown precision and timely deceleration. The framework provides quantitative and reproducible guidance for reliability-centered runway safety management.

title: Fragility analysis of dam-reservoir systems under seismic loading using LSTM-integrated model order reduction
exported_title: Fragility analysis of dam-reservoir systems under seismic loading using LSTM-integrated model order reduction

metadata.abstract: Seismic analysis of dam-reservoir systems considering fluid-structure interactions and nonlinear material behavior is crucial for safety assessment. It requires a three-dimensional full-scale model capable of capturing various failure modes, considering various uncertainties. Fragility analysis, routinely used in a probabilistic framework, is computationally very expensive because of the size and need for repeated simulations. This issue is addressed here using a combination of reduced order modeling (ROM), machine learning, and high-performance computing using CPU and GPU. Accordingly, a proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) based non-intrusive ROM is integrated with LSTM for high dimensional regression. Two new modifications to an existing framework are proposed here. First, force-feeding system parameter information in the LSTM, and second, adopting two-step singular value decomposition for large systems. A model of the Koyna dam of varying complexities — from 2D linear to 3D nonlinear models with more than 105 degrees of freedom — under non-stationary excitations is considered for numerical studies. The nonlinearity is modeled using a continuum plasticity-based damage model. The proposed methodology is scalable, and achieves a computational speed-up of three orders of magnitude compared to the full-scale analysis. The non-intrusive nature of the method allows usage of any black box or commercial code.

title: When agents learn to think: Large language model-enhanced agent-based modeling for crowd evacuation in disaster scenarios
exported_title: When agents learn to think: Large language model-enhanced agent-based modeling for crowd evacuation in disaster scenarios

metadata.abstract: Reliable and realistic modeling of crowd evacuation is critical for improving the safety and resilience of complex transportation and infrastructure systems under disaster emergencies. Traditional agent-based modeling has been widely used to simulate individual behaviors and interactions during evacuations, but often struggles to represent interpersonal communication, context-aware reasoning, and adaptive decision-making under rapidly evolving conditions. To address these limitations, this study introduces a dynamic evacuation simulation framework that integrates large language models as decision-making cores for individual agents.
