However, the current understanding of the evolutionary patterns and correlation mechanisms of bus traffic safety with operation-related factors remains limited.​ Thus, this study proposes an Adaptive Three-Stage Temporal Feature Forecasting(ATS-TFF) framework. Taking a mountainous Chinese city as an example, it forecasts the trend of urban bus traffic safety situation (BTSS) and analyzes the relationships between BTSS and multiple influencing factors.​ The results reveal at the feature level, factors such as the mean number of downstream bus stops in the road sections, the mean number of tunnels allowing lane changes along the routes, and the maximum temperature all have substantial effects on BTSS. Temporally, BTSS most significantly affects itself five days later. At the interaction level, the mean number of downstream bus stops in the passed road sections four days prior has the most important impacts on BTSS. ​Overall, the proposed ATS-TFF framework and findings provide data-driven support for proactive bus system safety management, advancing the shift from reactive control to forward-looking, targeted intervention strategies.

title: InSight-R: A structured interface data-driven framework for dynamic human reliability analysis of interface-induced errors
exported_title: InSight-R: A structured interface data-driven framework for dynamic human reliability analysis of interface-induced errors

metadata.abstract: Human-machine interface (HMI) failures remain a major contributor to human errors in safety-critical systems, yet conventional human reliability analysis (HRA) largely relies on qualitative judgment. Although recent cognitive modeling approaches introduce quantitative mechanisms, they rarely link objective interface design attributes directly to human error probabilities in dynamic operational contexts. To address this gap, we propose InSight-R, a structured interface data-driven probabilistic framework that quantitatively models the association between interface design attributes and interface-induced human errors. By integrating objective interface analytics, empirical behavioral data, and hierarchical probabilistic inference, the framework enables path-level diagnosis of interface-induced risks. The model captures theoretically motivated directional relationships between interface metrics and operator cognitive-behavioral states, where target salience, semantic interference, and interaction span jointly predict execution-related and time-deviation errors. The framework was evaluated on a high-fidelity nuclear simulator using representative panel-inspection tasks with licensed operators and student participants. Results show that increased visual and semantic complexity is associated with higher probabilities of execution errors and temporal deviations. By establishing a quantitative link between interface design attributes and human error probabilities, InSight-R provides a data-driven refinement of HMI-related performance shaping factors and supports dynamically interpretable human reliability analysis.

title: Active learning Kriging with spherical low-discrepancy sampling and gradient refinement for efficient reliability analysis of geotechnical systems
exported_title: Active learning Kriging with spherical low-discrepancy sampling and gradient refinement for efficient reliability analysis of geotechnical systems

metadata.abstract: Reliability analysis of geotechnical systems often requires numerous high-fidelity simulations to evaluate complex limit state functions (LSFs), resulting in prohibitive computational cost. Traditional surrogate-based approaches, such as active learning Kriging with Monte Carlo simulation (AK-MCS), often suffer from local clustering of background samples and inefficient exploration of the failure domain, especially in high-dimensional problems. To address these limitations, an enhanced active learning Kriging framework, termed AK-SLDS, is developed. The method integrates a spherical low-discrepancy sampling (SLDS) scheme with a gradient-refined learning strategy to improve the global representativeness of background samples and the local accuracy of surrogate updates. The performance of AK-SLDS is verified through five numerical examples, including two benchmark problems and three engineering applications. The two benchmark problems demonstrate the method’s accuracy and efficiency for low- to medium-dimensional reliability analyses. The engineering examples, involving the bearing capacity of a shallow footing and two slope stability problems, confirm its robustness for strongly nonlinear and high-dimensional geotechnical systems. Results show that AK-SLDS produces failure probability estimates in close agreement with MCS while requiring substantially fewer true LSF evaluations compared with conventional active learning approaches. The method thus provides an efficient and reliable framework for conducting reliability analysis in geotechnical systems.

title: Active learning with dynamic exploitation-exploration balance for aircraft engine remaining useful life prediction
exported_title: Active learning with dynamic exploitation-exploration balance for aircraft engine remaining useful life prediction

metadata.abstract: Accurate remaining useful life (RUL) prediction for aircraft engines using deep learning is often hindered by the scarcity of labeled run-to-failure data. Active learning (AL) addresses this by selecting the most informative samples for labeling, but traditional methods often use fixed criteria and fail to properly balance the exploitation-exploration trade-off. This paper proposes a novel AL framework that dynamically manages this balance. We utilize a Bayesian hybrid deep learning model to quantify prognostic uncertainty. Based on this, we develop a dual-criteria acquisition function, which integrates uncertainty and diversity by using a feedback mechanism to dynamically adjust their balance. To mitigate redundancy in batch queries, we also introduce a greedy selection algorithm to promote intra-batch diversity. Validation on the C-MAPSS and PHM08 benchmark datasets demonstrates that our framework achieves high RUL prediction accuracy with significantly fewer labeled samples than the compared AL strategies.

title: A data-driven framework for failure probability prediction of water supply pipelines: Integrating feature selection and homogeneous grouping
exported_title: A data-driven framework for failure probability prediction of water supply pipelines: Integrating feature selection and homogeneous grouping

metadata.abstract: Accurate prediction of water supply pipeline failure probability over a future period is vital for risk prevention. Within the prediction period, pipeline failures are typically modeled as a Poisson process. Nonetheless, the scarcity and poor quality of historical failure data necessitate homogeneous grouping to estimate average failure rates. A key challenge in this process is determining how to select appropriate features for grouping, as it directly affects prediction accuracy. This study proposes a data-driven framework integrating feature selection and homogeneous grouping to improve failure probability prediction. First, failure observation samples for a specific time period are generated based on the pipeline’s failure records. A layered feature selection strategy combining filter and wrapper methods is designed to balance selection efficiency with model performance. Filter methods are used to identify candidate feature subsets based on correlation with failure rates. These subsets are then used for grouping, resulting in multiple failure probability labeled datasets. For each, prediction models are developed using Artificial Neural Network and Support Vector Regression. The optimal feature subset and corresponding model are determined by comparing predictive performance. The framework’s effectiveness is validated using a case study of water supply pipelines in the central area of Shanghai, China.

title: A Bayesian uncertainty-guided transfer learning method for trustworthy fault diagnosis of rotating components
exported_title: A Bayesian uncertainty-guided transfer learning method for trustworthy fault diagnosis of rotating components

metadata.abstract: The overall reliability and safety of mission-critical equipment, such as aero-engines, largely depend on the health of their rotating parts. Therefore, trustworthy fault diagnosis is essential for achieving reliability-centered health management. Existing methods face several challenges under cross-working conditions, including computational redundancy, a high risk of negative transfer, and a lack of awareness of uncertainty. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel trustworthy fault diagnosis method based on transfer learning. More specifically, first, a domain-shared feature encoder that fuses sparse self-attention and a deep CNN is designed to extract local and global features. Second, a Bayesian classifier based on variational inference is constructed and combined with Monte Carlo sampling to quantify epistemic uncertainty. Then, a domain alignment mechanism combining explicit and implicit discrepancy measures is introduced. Meanwhile, the uncertainty is mapped via an exponential decay function into adaptive weights that guide domain alignment, thereby prioritizing the transfer of high-confidence samples and suppressing unreliable ones. Finally, the experimental results on the gear dataset show that the proposed method achieved the highest accuracy rate of 99.11% in three transfer tasks. Moreover, among the correct predictions, 91.84% fall within the low-uncertainty region, while all misclassifications are flagged as high-uncertainty. These results demonstrate that the proposed method can provide trustworthy, uncertainty-aware diagnostics to enhance the reliability and safety of complex mechanical systems.

title: A correlation-aligned proxy-learning framework for few-shot prediction of battery remaining useful life
exported_title: A correlation-aligned proxy-learning framework for few-shot prediction of battery remaining useful life

metadata.abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is critical for quantifying battery operational safety and longevity, yet the deployment of machine learning techniques is often constrained by a widespread deficiency of high-quality labelled degradation data. To address this challenge, we propose a correlation-aligned proxy-learning framework that establishes a principled bridge between scarce RUL labels and opportunistic ageing cues. The framework employs a bilateral-branch neural network to explicitly disentangle initial manufacturing variability from in-use degradation dynamics, ensuring robust feature extraction across heterogeneous cells. By recasting a class of differential incremental capacity (ΔIC)-based descriptors as proxy labels, the method leverages their strong intra-cell and through-life correlation with RUL to transform the under-determined few-shot regression problem into a consistency-matching task. This strategy effectively constrains the model’s learning manifold, enabling the exploitation of non-ideal indicators from routine charging events while mitigating the risk of overfitting. Validated across diverse battery chemistries and cycling temperatures, the framework significantly outperforms conventional semi-supervised baselines, delivering more than a 50% improvement in prediction accuracy under extreme few-shot regimes.

title: Development of urban fire risk index based on fire damage weighting methodologies and AI analysis of meteorological factors
exported_title: Development of urban fire risk index based on fire damage weighting methodologies and AI analysis of meteorological factors

metadata.abstract: As urban density increases, the development of reliable quantitative indicators for fire risk assessment becomes essential for disaster management. However, existing studies have tended to rely on single weighting methods without validating their suitability for predictive modeling based on meteorological conditions. This study constructed fire risk indices using three distinct methodologies: principal component analysis (PCA) for statistical objectivity, analytic hierarchy process (AHP) for expert judgment, and value of statistical life (VSL) for economic valuation. Using ten years of fire and meteorological data from Busan, risk grades were classified using K-Means clustering, and predictive models were developed via a Random Forest (RF) classifier based on four key meteorological variables (average temperature, maximum wind speed, effective humidity, and sea-level pressure). Comparative analysis revealed that the AHP and VSL models, which placed excessive weight on fatalities, showed low correlation with meteorological conditions and poor predictive performance for high-risk events (recall < 0.20). In contrast, the PCA-based index effectively captured the physical mechanisms of fire spread under low temperature, dry, and high-pressure conditions. The PCA model achieved a precision and recall of 0.99 in classifying high-risk grades. While AHP and VSL are useful for post-event impact assessment, this study demonstrated that the PCA-based index is the most scientifically valid and reliable measure for a meteorology-based predictive early warning system.

title: Optimizing fault tree traversal order for efficient minimal cut set generation: A lightweight graph neural network approach
exported_title: Optimizing fault tree traversal order for efficient minimal cut set generation: A lightweight graph neural network approach

metadata.abstract: Although the downward method is widely used in fault tree analysis, the critical impact of sibling node traversal order on computational efficiency has received insufficient attention. Current approaches rely on either fixed heuristic rules or random selection, resulting in unstable computational performance. To address this challenge, we introduce graph neural networks to intelligently optimize node traversal order. We construct a comprehensive dataset that maps graph structures and node orderings to computational costs, and propose a novel two-stage training framework: a cost prediction network that evaluates ordering quality, followed by a ranking generator guided by predicted costs. Experimental evaluation on industrial fault trees demonstrates that our GNN-based approach consistently identifies efficient traversal strategies, achieving 1.5–40 × speedups over conventional methods and competitive performance against established solvers. By transforming the discrete combinatorial optimization problem into a learnable task, this work provides a new perspective for optimizing topological traversal in minimal cut set analysis.

title: Energy-saving optimization of train speed Profile based on online Policy deep reinforcement learning algorithm under emergency conditions
exported_title: Energy-saving optimization of train speed Profile based on online Policy deep reinforcement learning algorithm under emergency conditions

metadata.abstract: In the domain of energy-efficient train-speed-profile optimization, off-policy reinforcement-learning (RL) algorithms and their variants have long dominated the academic landscape. Such approaches typically rely on an experience-replay buffer to reuse historical samples, yet they suffer from low training efficiency, poor numerical stability, and insufficient real-time responsiveness—limitations that become critical in complex metro systems or under emergency conditions. To overcome these drawbacks, we propose an on-policy RL framework termed the Energy-Saving Maximization Advantage Distribution (ES-MAD) algorithm. ES-MAD abandons the replay buffer and instead employs dual policy networks (new vs. old): data collected by the newly explored policy are immediately leveraged to update the old policy, thereby markedly improving sample efficiency. In addition, a normalized-and-scaled advantage function is introduced to reduce variance, which significantly enhances model stability in highly dynamic or emergency scenarios. Finally, a multi-objective, self-adaptive reward mechanism is designed that seamlessly integrates energy efficiency, punctuality, ride comfort, and stopping accuracy; this reward structure requires no re-tuning when the system switches between normal and emergency operating modes. Experimental validation on the Yizhuang metro line demonstrates that ES-MAD exhibits strong robustness and generalization capability under regular service, sudden schedule changes, and multi-interval comprehensive tests. Compared with state-of-the-art off-policy deep RL baselines, ES-MAD achieves 24 % and 26 % additional energy-saving under normal and emergency conditions, respectively.

title: Batch active learning for reliability-based model validation
exported_title: Batch active learning for reliability-based model validation

metadata.abstract: In engineering, quantifying the deviation between model prediction and reality is crucial, particularly when simulation or empirical models are used in safety-critical applications or for product release. Model validation aims to quantify this discrepancy by comparing model predictions to experimental results. However, conducting physical experiments for validation is often costly and time-consuming. Active learning strategies can mitigate this problem by reducing the data needed to assess model accuracy. In practice, these strategies must account for experimental uncertainties, such as material variability. This work proposes an active learning framework for model validation focused on efficiently identifying the limit state between valid and invalid model regions under such conditions. Therefore, we introduce a decision-theoretical basis from which we derive two novel misclassification-based acquisition functions for mean-based and quantile-based validation. Furthermore, the framework is extended to the batch setting, allowing multiple points to be proposed for evaluation while considering nonlinear constraints of the input space. The proposed method is compared to alternative approaches for several analytical and engineering problems. Finally, the validation of a temperature model for an electric motor demonstrates the efficiency of the method in a complex scenario.

title: A k-GNN Wiener process interactive RUL prognosis method for stochastic degrading devices monitored by related multiple sensors
exported_title: A k-GNN Wiener process interactive RUL prognosis method for stochastic degrading devices monitored by related multiple sensors

metadata.abstract: Remaining useful life (RUL) prediction is critical for making proactive decisions regarding the health management activities of degrading devices, thereby effectively ensuring safe, reliable, and economic operations. For degrading devices monitored by multiple sensors, hybrid prognosis methods combining statistical-model-based and deep-learning-based approaches, have become popular in the field of prognostics and health management. However, existing studies based on open-loop model architectures, tend to overlook the correlations and complementary relationships among multiple sensors, leading to a reduction in prediction accuracy. Therefore, this paper presents a novel data-model integrative prognosis framework incorporating high-order graph neural networks (GNNs) and Wiener process (WP). Specifically, a k-order GNN (k-GNN) capturing the high-order interaction information among different sensors is utilized to construct a composite health index (CHI). Subsequently, the time-varying stochastics within the CHI is depicted through a WP. By joint learning parameters of the k-GNN with those of the WP, a closed-loop framework is established to improve the matching degree between the constructed CHI and the WP-based degradation models. Both experimental results on simulated datasets including C-MAPSS and N-CMAPSS and real-world case study results on milling cutter dataset demonstrate that the proposed k-GNN-WP model achieves a substantial improvement in RUL prediction accuracy.

title: Towards AI-Driven smart maintenance of computed tomography equipment: From health indicator design to transferable remaining useful life prediction
exported_title: Towards AI-Driven smart maintenance of computed tomography equipment: From health indicator design to transferable remaining useful life prediction

metadata.abstract: Failures of Computed Tomography (CT) equipment can disrupt hospital operations and compromise patient safety. However, research on Predictive Maintenance (PdM) for such systems remains limited. The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) provides a practical foundation by enabling real-time acquisition of high-dimensional operational data. This study proposes a deep learning framework for predicting the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of CT equipment. First, a physics-guided Health Indicator (HI) is defined as the deviation between the observed current and the predicted nominal current of the X-ray tube filament. Second, a CT-specific degradation path identification module that combines operational state filtering with adaptive signal fusion to extract smooth, physically consistent trends is proposed. Third, a bidirectional LSTM sequence-to-sequence model, combined with cross-equipment transfer learning and uncertainty quantification, is developed for RUL prediction under heterogeneous work states and across different equipment. The framework is validated on real-world IoMT-collected X-ray tube filament datasets from multiple hospitals and CT equipment. The proposed framework achieves prediction errors of 0.3, 3.0, and 2.3 days with error rates of 0.23%, 2.33%, and 1.78%, respectively, outperforming classic and recent strong baselines in temporal alignment and generalization. These results demonstrate the potential of IoMT-enabled PdM to support maintenance decision-making, clinical workflow optimization, and downtime minimization.

title: EPAL: An exponential-penalty based active-learning function for adaptive Kriging models in structural reliability analysis
exported_title: EPAL: An exponential-penalty based active-learning function for adaptive Kriging models in structural reliability analysis

metadata.abstract: Accurate estimation of structural failure probability in engineering systems is frequently limited by the high computational cost of evaluating complex performance functions. This paper introduces an exponential-penalty based active-learning (EPAL) function for adaptive refinement of Kriging models in reliability analysis. The EPAL formulation integrates the Kriging predictive variance with a normalized distance measure relative to the predicted limit-state surface through an exponential decay term. This functional form dynamically suppresses the selection of new samples in regions of low predictive uncertainty or those far from the failure boundary. The inherent resistance to sample clustering ensures a balanced sampling strategy that simultaneously explores regions of high uncertainty and refines the vicinity of the failure boundary. A key feature of this design is that the EPAL function is mathematically simple, parameter-free, and continuously differentiable. By removing the need for empirical tuning parameters or auxiliary distance thresholds, the method reduces subjective bias and computational redundancy. Numerical results from multiple benchmark problems confirm that the proposed method provides accurate failure probability with high computational efficiency. Its effective performance in both engineering applications and problems with small failure events further demonstrates its suitability for reliability analysis involving expensive simulations.

title: A data-efficient surrogate-based structural reliability approach using a firefly-optimized deep neural network: Application to hang-off drilling riser evacuations
exported_title: A data-efficient surrogate-based structural reliability approach using a firefly-optimized deep neural network: Application to hang-off drilling riser evacuations

metadata.abstract: Reliability assessment of offshore structures subjected to nonlinear hydrodynamic-structural interactions requires uncertainty propagation that is statistically consistent with the full response space. However, fully coupled finite-element (FE) simulations are too computationally expensive for Monte Carlo (MC) analysis, limiting their applicability in nonlinear structural reliability. This study develops a data-efficient structural reliability methodology that integrates nonlinear FE simulations, a firefly-optimized deep neural network (FA-DNN) surrogate model, and MC uncertainty propagation into a unified framework. The methodological innovation lies in the FA-DNN model, where a multi-objective firefly optimization strategy adaptively tunes hyperparameters to improve learning stability, prevent overfitting under limited FE data, and accurately reproduce nonlinear response behavior required for reliability evaluation. Trained on a small FE-generated dataset, the FA-DNN achieves R² values above 0.996 and reduces prediction errors by over 90% compared with ANN and baseline DNN models, enabling fast and statistically consistent MC-based estimation of failure probability. Application to a deepwater riser system in hang-off evacuation serves as a verification example, demonstrating that the methodology yields reliability-informed operational limits with negligible computational cost. The framework is general and transferable, offering an efficient surrogate-enhanced pathway for nonlinear reliability assessment of offshore and other complex structures under stochastic loading.

title: The prediction of limit wheel profile using geometric-constrained residual Bayesian neural networks
exported_title: The prediction of limit wheel profile using geometric-constrained residual Bayesian neural networks

metadata.abstract: Wheel profile prediction is critical to the maintenance of high-speed electric multiple units. This study proposes a geometric-constrained residual Bayesian neural network for high-accuracy prediction of worn wheel profiles. A vehicle–track dynamic simulation model is further employed to determine whether predicted worn profiles exceed the limit and to estimate the time-dependent reliability associated with profile degradation. The proposed approach is evaluated via quantitative and qualitative comparisons with a conventional wheelset wear prediction method. Results indicate that the geometric-constrained residual Bayesian neural network improves wheel wear prediction accuracy. In addition, the simulation-based prediction is more conservative, and the wear range observed in service is wider than that obtained from simulation. Wear patterns of wheels within the same wheelset also show strong correlations. Moreover, wheel diameter affects wear behaviour, including the wear degradation rate, equivalent conicity, the vehicle critical speed, and the Sperling index. Hence, Maintenance scheduling should therefore account for wheel diameter effects to ensure robust performance and durability.

title: Bayesian deep learning framework for pesticide transport modeling with uncertainty quantification
exported_title: Bayesian deep learning framework for pesticide transport modeling with uncertainty quantification

metadata.abstract: Pesticide transport and transformation in soil pose potential threats to ecological environments and human health, while traditional numerical simulation methods exhibit high computational costs and difficulty in accurately quantifying prediction uncertainty. A Bayesian deep learning framework is developed for pesticide transport modeling, integrating uncertainty quantification, interpretability analysis, and risk assessment. Surrogate models including deterministic, MC Dropout, and Deep Ensemble architectures are constructed based on 447,300 COMSOL simulation data points. The Deep Ensemble model achieves the optimal balance between prediction accuracy (R2>0.96) and uncertainty quantification, with calibration errors of 0.0350–0.0467. SHAP analysis reveals the dominant role of second-layer soil hydraulic parameters, which simultaneously constitute the primary sources of model uncertainty. Spatiotemporal uncertainty analysis shows that the mean prediction uncertainty decreases from 0.21 to 0.05 within 14 days and remains stable at 0.04–0.08 over the full 365-day period.The risk assessment framework reveals that contamination risk escalates from a mean probability of 0.476 (t=2 days) to 0.837 (t=28 days) with 72.1% of the domain classified as very high risk, and the early warning system indicates that the alert and emergency thresholds are triggered at 2.0 and 4.0 days, respectively. Climate change impacts are quantified through 10 scenario analyses: warming reduces the near-surface mean concentration by 18.8% via the Q10 effect, while precipitation changes affect transport through the source concentration (c0) and infiltration forcing (Hp0) pathways, with the c0 pathway dominating most exposure metrics. Under extreme drought conditions, the high-concentration area of aldicarb sulfoxide reaches 20.0–57.2%, far exceeding baseline levels. The framework provides a comprehensive approach to uncertainty-aware pesticide transport prediction, with future extensions needed for three-dimensional heterogeneous systems and multi-pesticide synergistic effects.

title: Adaptive parameter estimation-based neural sliding mode control for uncertain singular Markovian jump systems against actuator attacks
exported_title: Adaptive parameter estimation-based neural sliding mode control for uncertain singular Markovian jump systems against actuator attacks

metadata.abstract: This article primarily focuses on tackling the challenge of adaptive parameter estimation-based neural sliding mode control for singular Markovian jump systems under actuator attacks The singular Markovian jump system exhibits adaptive uncertain parameters and inaccessible states. Furthermore, due to vulnerable control signals during transmission, the actuator may receive compromised commands from malicious attacks. To mitigate the effects stemming from actuator attacks, neural network (NN)-based strategy is employed to approximate and evaluate the fraudulent information introduced by adversaries. Subsequently, the online estimation of uncertain system parameters is conducted by leveraging the derived adaptive law. Meanwhile, a newly designed sliding mode observer is integrated into the system to evaluate the unobservable states, thereby significantly enhancing the comprehensiveness of system state monitoring. An innovative adaptive neural sliding mode control strategy is presented, which is designed to ensure that both the estimated states and their corresponding errors are capable of converging to the sliding manifolds. Simultaneously, this strategy guarantees the stochastic admissibility of the uncertain singular Markovian jump systems. Ultimately, the effectiveness and applicability of the proposed method are demonstrated through empirical research on the direct-current (DC) motor and the Quarter-Car active suspension (QCAS) model.

title: Graph-based deep reinforcement learning for adaptive and scalable post-earthquake bridge network restoration
exported_title: Graph-based deep reinforcement learning for adaptive and scalable post-earthquake bridge network restoration

metadata.abstract: Rapid restoration of bridge networks following earthquake events is crucial to ensuring transportation continuity, reducing economic disruption, and supporting emergency response. This study proposes a novel graph-based deep reinforcement learning framework (GNN-DRL) that synergistically integrates Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL), and a Top-k action filtering mechanism, to enable adaptive and scalable post-earthquake bridge network repair scheduling under resource constraints. The proposed approach captures network topology and dynamic bridge states to prioritize sequential bridge repair decisions across a restoration planning horizon. The GNN-DRL decision policy is evaluated on several case-study bridge networks with varying sizes and is compared to other restoration policies including ranking-based, mixed-integer linear programming, and DRL-only policies. Sensitivity analyses are carried out to examine the effect of the Top-k filtering mechanism on balancing bridges network resilience and computational complexity, for practical real-time deployment. Results show that the proposed GNN-DRL policy consistently achieves faster and more effective restoration as well as higher final functionality throughout the planning horizon, demonstrating the potential of AI-guided infrastructure restoration to enhance disaster resilience in complex transportation systems. The framework offers a practical balance of resilience, scalability, and computational efficiency suitable for rapid post-earthquake restoration decision support.

title: Efficient time-variant reliability analysis through parallel adaptive Gaussian process modeling based on look-ahead sampling strategy
exported_title: Efficient time-variant reliability analysis through parallel adaptive Gaussian process modeling based on look-ahead sampling strategy

metadata.abstract: During the full life cycle of engineering products, structural performance inevitably degrades over time and is affected by uncertainties. Time-variant reliability analysis (TRA) plays a crucial role in ensuring safety and evaluating service life. However, accurately characterizing the time-variant failure probability within limited computational resources remains a challenging task. To address this issue, this study proposes a novel method termed parallel time-variant stepwise error reduction (PTSER) for efficient TRA within the single-loop Gaussian process framework. The core lies in constructing a look-ahead learning function to explicitly account for the impact of current sampling decisions on the future model accuracy. Subsequently, parallel sampling is achieved by combining probability-weighted importance and correlation-based diversity control. In addition, to accelerate the training process, a pruning mechanism is introduced to construct a truncated objective integration set and a compact candidate pool, thereby reducing computational complex while preserving reliability-critical information. Meanwhile, a hybrid stopping criterion combining uncertainty reduction and estimate stabilization is developed. The performance of the proposed method is illustrated on several examples. Experiment results show that the proposed method can obtain more accurate failure probability estimates with higher efficiency.

title: Dynamic evolution mechanism of mine accident risks: An interpretable machine learning framework for causal analysis
exported_title: Dynamic evolution mechanism of mine accident risks: An interpretable machine learning framework for causal analysis

metadata.abstract: Traditional static risk assessments often fail to capture the nonlinear dynamic evolution mechanisms inherent in mine accidents. To address this gap, this study constructs an analytical framework that integrates interpretable machine learning with causal inference, utilizing a longitudinal dataset of 3.38 million Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) records. The empirical results reveal three core mechanisms driving risk evolution. First, risk exhibits strong path dependence, identifying historical safety performance as the dominant predictor. Second, a statistically robust phase transition threshold is detected at approximately 48 annual violations; surpassing this critical limit triggers a qualitative shift from a responsive linear stage to a saturated state of management failure. Third, risk structure plays a decisive role, where high-entropy risk dispersion patterns are shown to be significantly more catastrophic than simple quantitative accumulation. Building on these findings, the "Threshold-Structure" dynamic risk evolution framework is proposed. By resolving the regulatory "Scale Paradox," this framework provides a scientific foundation for shifting safety management from static monitoring to differentiated, precision regulation.

title: Value-of-information-based optimization of grey-box models for computational risk assessment of cyber-physical systems
exported_title: Value-of-information-based optimization of grey-box models for computational risk assessment of cyber-physical systems

metadata.abstract: The complexity of Cyber-Physical Systems (CPSs) requires that their safety be evaluated by Computational Risk Assessment (CRA). The very large computational challenge can be addressed by Grey-Box Models (GBMs), which integrate first-principles White-Box Models (WBMs) and data-driven Black-Box Models (BBMs): different WBMs or BBMs can be used to model each CPS subsystem, which leads to a combinatorial number of possible GBM alternatives that come with different trade-offs between computational burden and physical fidelity. In this work, we propose a Value-of-Information (VoI)-based procedure to identify the best GBM for CPS CRA. We show the procedure by application to an Integrated Power and Telecommunication (IP&TLC) infrastructure: VoI-driven GBM alternatives are evaluated and those that reduce the computational burden while keeping accurate in computing the risk metrics of interest are identified.

title: An active learning method combining Reliability Analysis Transformer and attention-based sampling for high-dimensional reliability analysis
exported_title: An active learning method combining Reliability Analysis Transformer and attention-based sampling for high-dimensional reliability analysis

metadata.abstract: Reliability analysis faces the challenge of accurately estimating failure probabilities while minimizing the number of time-consuming model evaluations. Surrogate models can significantly alleviate the computational burden. However, the increasing dimensionality of modern engineering systems poses substantial challenges to the performance of traditional surrogate models. To address these issues, this paper introduces a novel cross-domain paradigm for high-dimensional reliability analysis, where the dimensionality of random variables is conceptually mapped to the sequence length in natural language processing (NLP). Building on this mapping, a Reliability Analysis Transformer (RAT) is designed to capture complex dependencies between random variables and system responses. Furthermore, based on the principle that similar samples contribute less new information, an attention-based sampling strategy is proposed to measure sample similarity and iteratively select the least similar samples to existing ones from the candidate dataset, thereby improving the accuracy of the RAT. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated through four high-dimensional numerical examples and a liquid rocket engine case study. Results show that the proposed method achieves high accuracy and efficiency in handling high-dimensional and large-scale engineering problems.

title: Likelihood-driven reinforcement learning synergizing knowledge graph embedding and supervised pre-training for system-level fault localization
exported_title: Likelihood-driven reinforcement learning synergizing knowledge graph embedding and supervised pre-training for system-level fault localization

metadata.abstract: System-level fault localization remains a critical challenge in vehicle powertrain health management, hindered by complex fault propagation, data scarcity, and the "one/multiple-phenomenon, one/multiple-cause" problem. While data-driven methods excel at component-level diagnosis, their reliance on large annotated datasets and inability to model system topology limit their effectiveness for system-level applications. This paper proposes SPKL-RL, a likelihood-driven reinforcement learning framework that synergizes supervised pre-training with knowledge graph embedding to address these limitations. The framework formulates fault localization as a likelihood optimization within a Partially Observable Markov Decision Process (POMDP). A supervised pre-training module provides a warm-start policy using historical data, mitigating RL's cold-start issue. A knowledge graph embedding module encodes system topology and fault propagation into interpretable vectors. A likelihood-driven mechanism then guides exploration by integrating information gain and knowledge consistency into the reward function. Experimental results on a real powertrain dataset show SPKL-RL achieves 89.3% diagnostic accuracy across 15 fault types, reduces average diagnostic steps from 38 to 16 (58% efficiency gain), and significantly outperforms baselines, particularly in complex cascading (86.9% accuracy) and coupled fault (80.7% accuracy) scenarios. The framework demonstrates substantial advantages in reducing data dependency, improving generalization, and enhancing interpretability for complex system diagnostics.

title: Machine learning-assisted reliability assessment of main girder deflection in suspension bridges
exported_title: Machine learning-assisted reliability assessment of main girder deflection in suspension bridges

metadata.abstract: This study presents a probabilistic reliability assessment method for vertical deflection in long-span suspension bridges, addressing uncertainties and multifactor coupling in deflection prediction. A hybrid model integrating temporal convolutional network (TCN), bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU), and Gaussian mixture model (GMM) is developed within a unified probabilistic framework. Trained on field data from Nanxi Suspension Bridge using temperature, vehicle load, and historical deflection inputs, the model estimates both the mean and standard deviation of deflections. It achieves a 38.4%–54.4% improvement in point-prediction accuracy and a 3.5%–15.6% increase in interval coverage compared to conventional methods. An extreme-value framework combining the peaks-over-threshold method with a filtered Poisson process is used to fit a generalized Pareto distribution (GPD), with threshold selection guided by diagnostic plots and statistical tests. Convergence toward the generalized extreme value distribution (GEVD) is confirmed. Extrapolation over a 100-year service life and multi-section integration yields a full-span reliability model, identifying critical sections at 2/8l and 6/8l of the main span. The approach offers a theoretically sound and practical tool for life-cycle performance evaluation of bridges under complex environmental and loading conditions.

title: Extrapolating optimal selective maintenance strategy in new environments: A meta-reinforcement learning approach
exported_title: Extrapolating optimal selective maintenance strategy in new environments: A meta-reinforcement learning approach

metadata.abstract: Selective maintenance, a widely adopted strategy in industry and military fields, has attracted increasing attention over the past decades. It involves selecting a subset of feasible maintenance actions to maximize the success probability of subsequent missions under limited resources. Most existing studies on selective maintenance optimization assume that the system degradation process is known. In many real-world applications, however, when a system is deployed in a new environment, the environmental effects on its degradation process are typically unknown, rendering these methods ineffective. To address this challenge, this study proposes a novel meta-reinforcement learning (meta-RL) approach for extrapolating optimal selective maintenance strategies from known environments to unseen ones. Within the proposed framework, a meta-agent is trained across multiple known environments to acquire generalized decision-making knowledge. When encountering a new environment, the trained meta-agent infers environmental characteristics from collected observations and adapts its strategy accordingly. Furthermore, a data augmentation method is introduced to mitigate performance loss during the initial explorations in new environments. Results from a two-component system and a coal transportation system demonstrate that the optimal selective maintenance strategies vary substantially across environments and highlight the importance of extrapolating adaptive maintenance strategies under unknown environments.

title: Data-Driven break size detection model for small modular reactors based on convolutional neural network-long short-term memory model and SHapley Additive exPlanations
exported_title: Data-Driven break size detection model for small modular reactors based on convolutional neural network-long short-term memory model and SHapley Additive exPlanations

metadata.abstract: During a loss of coolant accident (LOCA), timely and accurate detection of the break size is crucial for nuclear power plant safety. However, current methods rely on the personal judgment of operators, which fail to meet the requirements of both speed and accuracy in high-risk situations. In this study, a CNN-LSTM model is proposed to detect the break size of LOCA, with six optimization algorithms used to tune the model hyperparameters. The GWO-WOA optimized model achieves the lowest validation loss (0.1563) and standard deviation (0.01462), outperforming the unoptimized model. To enhance model interpretability, SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis was conducted. Its results align with actual accident analysis, indicating that the model effectively captured the key features of the accident and enhanced the operators' trust in the AI model. Furthermore, three SHAP-based feature selection strategies were analyzed to reduce the number of required features and improve model performance. The results show that the selection strategy based on the mean SHAP value, which reduces the test set MSE from 0.196 (original feature combination) to 0.0396, is closest to the optimal feature combination. These findings offer practical guidance for developing LOCA break size detection systems, enhancing accident response timeliness and effectiveness.

title: Zero-shot cross-domain transfer for remaining useful life prediction of aero-engines via iterative diffusion refinement
exported_title: Zero-shot cross-domain transfer for remaining useful life prediction of aero-engines via iterative diffusion refinement

metadata.abstract: Accurate prediction of the Remaining Useful Life (RUL) of turbofan engines is critical for effective predictive maintenance. However, conventional models often struggle to generalize when sensor data distributions shift due to variations in operating profiles, environmental conditions, or system configurations. Existing unsupervised domain adaptation methods alleviate this issue by exploiting unlabeled target-domain data, but they still require additional data sampling. In this paper, we present RUL-DiT, a Diffusion Transformer architecture that combines Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models with a Transformer backbone and a novel LSTM-based conditioning network to iteratively refine RUL predictions via diffusion-based posterior denoising. At each reverse-diffusion step, RUL-DiT refines a Gaussian latent posterior whose mean and schedule-defined variance progressively concentrate the RUL estimate, enabling more faithful modeling of gradual degradation processes than conventional models. Crucially, when trained on a single subset of CMAPSS and NCMAPSS, two established benchmark datasets for aircraft engine prognostics, RUL-DiT achieves strong performance relative to previously reported baselines on both datasets. Moreover, RUL-DiT enables zero-shot cross-domain transfer and achieves competitive performance across transfer tasks on several source-target pairs, without requiring any target-domain labels or fine-tuning. This source-only capability enables direct deployment on unseen subsets and engine operating conditions, substantially reducing data collection overhead for RUL prognostics.

title: Data-driven modeling and application of general aviation system safety theory: From topics to factor analysis and application processes
exported_title: Data-driven modeling and application of general aviation system safety theory: From topics to factor analysis and application processes

metadata.abstract: The safety barriers in general aviation (GA) are significantly weaker than those in commercial transport aviation, especially under multifactor coupling in complex operational conditions. To address the limitations of traditional small-sample analyses and the “pre-dependencies” of emerging technologies, this study proposes a data-driven dual-task modeling framework for GA system safety theory (GA-SST). The framework integrates an improved bidirectional encoder representations for topic modeling (BERTopic) model with the human factors analysis and classification system (HFACS), significantly enhancing the interpretability of large-scale data analysis. Thematic analysis revealed five critical themes: loss of control, human‒machine interaction failures, adverse weather, training deficiencies, and pilot characteristics. Causal mapping further reveals some key risk factors: intentional procedural violations, deficient safety awareness and culture, inadequate safety supervision, human‒machine interaction failures under complex conditions, component failures, poor management of pilot qualifications and training, and deficient spatial perception. Furthermore, a BERT-Convolutional Neural Network-Gated Recurrent Unit (BERT-CG) model is developed to support practical application of these causal factors. The results demonstrate that the GA-SST framework effectively bridges theoretical analysis and data-driven approaches, providing valuable and actionable safety insights from large data.

title: A machine learning-enhanced real-time reliability assessment framework for maritime autonomous surface ships propulsion systems
exported_title: A machine learning-enhanced real-time reliability assessment framework for maritime autonomous surface ships propulsion systems

metadata.abstract: Driven by industry-wide digitalization and the pursuit of autonomy, maritime autonomous surface ships (MASS) are transitioning from conceptual design to real-world operation, emerging as a vital future maritime transportation. Among the challenges confronting MASS, the reliability of propulsion systems stands out as a paramount concern due to its direct impact on safety and mission continuity. This study proposes a real-time reliability assessment framework for MASS propulsion systems based on a diagnosis-informed dynamic Bayesian Network (DBN). The framework integrates Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD), Transformer, and Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (BiGRU) models to diagnose faults and update the DBN with real-time evidence, allowing dynamic and adaptive reliability assessment. This approach incorporates real-time fault diagnosis at the component level to refine system-level reliability predictions. The feasibility of the approach was validated using a case study on a diesel-electric hybrid propulsion system using failure rate data and operational data from simulated fault scenarios. The results indicated that the reliability of related subsystems declined significantly, and the hybrid propulsion system dropped to 0.986 on Day 30, after the navigation mission was completed. This framework introduces a causal inference mechanism that bridges the gap between component-level diagnostics and overall reliability assessment, providing a promising approach for intelligent health monitoring and proactive maintenance planning in MASS operations. The results can provide valuable support for decision-making in scheduling, degradation management, and maintenance planning for the MASS propulsion system with actual operation data.

title: Real-time crash risk level prediction of freeways based on a hybrid spatiotemporal deep learning framework with channel redistribution
exported_title: Real-time crash risk level prediction of freeways based on a hybrid spatiotemporal deep learning framework with channel redistribution

metadata.abstract: The accurate prediction of crash risk from massive traffic data has become a critical challenge for enhancing road safety. To improve real-time crash risk prediction capabilities, a novel hybrid deep learning framework combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), Transformers, and STar Aggregate-Redistribute (STAR) Module is proposed (i.e., CNN-Transformer-STAR). Using high-resolution vehicle trajectory data from the NGSIM dataset, the model extracts complex spatiotemporal interaction features to classify the crash risks into three categories: low level, medium level, and high level. Specifically, the CNN branch is employed to capture local spatiotemporal dynamics and cross-feature coupling relationships, while the Transformer models global temporal and spatial dependencies. Additionally, the STAR module implements a centralized scheme to extract a global latent representation, which is then redistributed across feature channels to optimize inter-channel interactions. Comparative experiments demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves a superior AUC of 0.90, outperforming baselines. The transferability of the predictive framework is validated using an external dataset, which shows a good robustness (AUC = 0.86) in different freeway scenarios. The results provide policy guidance for freeway traffic safety management.

title: Hierarchical domain-physical topology enhanced Fully-Connected Spatial-Temporal Graph Neural Network for remaining useful life prediction
exported_title: Hierarchical domain-physical topology enhanced Fully-Connected Spatial-Temporal Graph Neural Network for remaining useful life prediction

metadata.abstract: Accurate and reliable Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction is paramount for ensuring the operational reliability and safety of complex industrial systems. However, existing deep learning paradigms often fail to incorporate explicit structural biases derived from physical dependencies, neglecting inherent physical mechanisms and failing to provide rigorous uncertainty quantification. To surmount these challenges, this paper proposes a Hierarchical Domain-Physical Topology Enhanced Fully-Connected Spatial-Temporal Graph Neural Network (HDPT-FC-STGNN). First, to bridge the heterogeneity between symbolic domain knowledge and continuous sensor streams, a Hierarchical Domain-Physical Topology (HDPT) is constructed leveraging high-dimensional semantic embeddings. A hierarchical message-passing mechanism is subsequently devised to explicitly encode topological dependencies, thereby fusing static physical priors with dynamic sensor streams. Second, to mitigate spurious correlations in noise-intensive environments, a Structure-Aware Probabilistic Graph Sampling strategy is introduced. By selectively injecting stochasticity into unreliable data-driven edges, this mechanism treats the graph topology as a latent variable, bolstering the model robustness against epistemic ambiguity. Finally, a Bayesian uncertainty quantification module, governed by a risk-sensitive hybrid loss function, is implemented to yield high-fidelity RUL estimates alongside well-calibrated confidence intervals. Extensive experiments on the C-MAPSS benchmark demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in both deterministic precision and probabilistic reliability, notably reducing the RMSE by approximately 6.9% on the FD001 subset while ensuring high probabilistic reliability.

title: Knowledge graph-enhanced large language models for explainable causal analysis of crane accidents
exported_title: Knowledge graph-enhanced large language models for explainable causal analysis of crane accidents

metadata.abstract: Crane accidents are characterized by high suddenness, chain-like evolution, and strongly coupled causal factors. Traditional experience-driven approaches are insufficient for reliable causal analysis and evidence-grounded interpretation. This study proposes a knowledge graph-enhanced large language model framework for explainable causal analysis and question answering in crane accident scenarios. A domain-specific ontology for crane accident causation is established based on the human-machine-environment-management (HMEM) framework, and a multi-stage automated knowledge extraction pipeline is developed. Using few-shot prompting, relation enrichment, and self-discrimination filtering, the method achieves high-consistency extraction of accident entities and relationships, resulting in a high-quality crane accident knowledge graph. A Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (GraphRAG) mechanism is further introduced to integrate BAAI General Embedding (BGE)-based semantic vector retrieval with multi-hop causal path expansion, enabling the retrieval of structurally constrained causal evidence. An evidence-constrained generation strategy ensures that the produced responses are logically coherent, consistent with retrieved causal evidence, and traceable. The CraneSafe QA prototype system supports knowledge extraction, graph visualization, causal chain analysis, and interactive reasoning. Experiments demonstrate improvements in retrieval accuracy, evidence consistency, and noise robustness, with stable performance across queries of varying semantic depth. The results indicate that knowledge graph-enhanced large language models substantially improve the reliability and interpretability of causal analysis in crane accident scenarios.

title: Pump fault diagnosis for vanadium redox flow batteries using an optimized smoothing-based graph convolutional network
exported_title: Pump fault diagnosis for vanadium redox flow batteries using an optimized smoothing-based graph convolutional network

metadata.abstract: Vanadium redox flow batteries (VRBs) are promising for large-scale energy storage, yet reliable pump fault diagnosis remains challenging due to complex multivariate coupling and limited labeled data. Graph convolutional networks (GCNs) provide an effective way to model variable relationships, but their performance is fundamentally limited by the oversmoothing problem, which leads to loss of feature discriminability in deep architectures. To address this issue, an optimized smoothing-based GCN (OS-GCN) framework is proposed. A smoothing factor (SF) is introduced to regulate feature propagation, and particle swarm optimization is employed to determine its optimal value, enabling a balance between information aggregation and feature preservation. Data association graphs for the GCN are constructed based on Euclidean distance (ED) relationships to capture system dynamics. Pump fault data are collected under both controlled and real-world conditions, providing the basis for an in-depth analysis of operating temperature effects, robustness to noise, and the applicability of the proposed model. Experimental results show that OS-GCN significantly outperforms existing fault diagnosis methods under controlled and real-world conditions. These findings confirm that the proposed framework effectively mitigates oversmoothing and improves the accuracy and robustness of VRB pump fault diagnosis.

title: Human reliability design method for human-machine interface based on an optimized back propagation neural network under visual cognitive interference
exported_title: Human reliability design method for human-machine interface based on an optimized back propagation neural network under visual cognitive interference

metadata.abstract: In the operation of medical equipment, laboratory personnel often fall into visual blurring when facing highly pathogenic dangerous viruses due to wearing goggles for a long time. Under such circumstances, human reliability level is subject to mixed uncertainties due to factors such as human cognition disturbed and so on. Moreover, there is a lack of relevant research. Constructing an appropriate human reliability design method model for Human-Machine Interface (HMI) is crucial for enhancing cognitive interaction level. Firstly, this research adopted the Human Error Assessment and Reduction Technique (HEART) combined with Grey Relational Algorithm (GRA) to measure Human Error Probability (HEP), which can solve that problem about the universality of its quantitative values leading to the uncertainty of matching in actual scenario. By comparing with two similar algorithms, to reduce the uncertainty of high-dimensional data modeling, Levenberg-Marquardt Backpropagation Neural Network (LM-BPNN) optimized by Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) was finally selected to construct the design model, fitting the correlation between the operation state and interface elements. Meanwhile, HEP analyzed by improved HEART was taken as one of input features of BPNN. Ultimately, statistical experiment verification shows that this method is effective and can promote the reliable development of medical laboratory systems.

title: An explicit surrogate model for real-time reliability assessment of face stability in underwater slurry shield tunneling
exported_title: An explicit surrogate model for real-time reliability assessment of face stability in underwater slurry shield tunneling

metadata.abstract: Ensuring tunnel face stability in underwater slurry shield tunneling is challenging due to the inherent stochasticity of geotechnical parameters. Despite their advantages, current frameworks face practical limitations: RFM rigorously captures spatial variability, but its computational cost hinders real-time deployment. Conversely, machine learning based RVMs rely on opaque models lacking explicit expressions, restricting their engineering portability. Importantly, groundwater effects are frequently not properly incorporated into existing frameworks. This study proposes a transparent, efficient reliability assessment framework that incorporates groundwater via the effective stress principle and the upper-bound theorem of limit analysis. A high-fidelity dataset of 4000 samples, accounting for parameter cross-correlations, is used to train a Back-Propagation Neural Network (BPNN). By extracting an explicit algebraic expression from the network, the framework eliminates model opacity and platform dependency. Combined with Sobol sensitivity analysis and Monte Carlo simulations, this surrogate model facilitates real-time determination of reliability-based face support pressure. Results indicate that the reliability-based surrogate model achieves an instantaneous execution time of 0.3 s, marking a substantial acceleration from the 55 h required by the traditional RFM. Moreover, it yields more conservative design values, thereby providing an additional safety buffer for engineering applications. Field validation at the Jiangyin-Jingjiang Yangtze River Tunnel confirms the framework's practical utility for real-time safety assessment in sandy strata.

title: Deep reinforcement learning-driven resilience optimization for infrastructure systems: A socio-technical perspective integrating functional resonance analysis method
exported_title: Deep reinforcement learning-driven resilience optimization for infrastructure systems: A socio-technical perspective integrating functional resonance analysis method

metadata.abstract: Escalating natural disasters and growing infrastructure complexity render resilience optimization indispensable for sustaining operations and mitigating losses. While deep reinforcement learning (DRL) offers powerful optimization potential, current models often overlook the interactions and variability inherent in socio-technical systems. Integrating DRL with the functional resonance analysis method (FRAM) shows promise, yet remains impractical without a dedicated focus on resilience-oriented controls. Accordingly, this paper proposes a FRAM-DRL framework tailored for infrastructure resilience optimization. Its key advancements are threefold: (1) extending FRAM into a multi-stage structure to capture socio-technical features throughout the resilience lifecycle; (2) establishing variability analysis rules to transform qualitative FRAM into an interactive environment; and (3) defining FRAM-based state, action, and reward representations to facilitate DRL training. The framework was applied to urban metro system (UMS) resilience under extreme rainfall, leveraging the Nanjing Metro case. Results demonstrate that the Dueling DQN performed best among the tested value-based architectures, with action constraint (κ=4) providing the optimal balance between optimization gain and cost efficiency. The learned policies prioritize high-leverage domains and early-stage controls, achieving a favorable reward-efficiency advantage over heuristic strategies via global policy search. Overall, this work methodologically advances Safety-II-oriented proactive management, offering a transferable basis for broader resilience research.

title: AL-IDNN: Active learning method based on incremental updating of deep neural networks for structural reliability analysis
exported_title: AL-IDNN: Active learning method based on incremental updating of deep neural networks for structural reliability analysis

metadata.abstract: Reliability analysis is essential for ensuring the safety of engineering systems under uncertainty. In reliability analysis, surrogate models are widely used to reduce computational cost. However, improving the accuracy of reliability analysis typically requires the continuous introduction of critical samples and repeated reconstruction of the surrogate model. To improve model accuracy while maintaining computational efficiency, this paper proposes an active learning method for structural reliability analysis based on incremental updating of deep neural networks (AL-IDNN). The proposed method preserves the knowledge learned by the existing model through parameter inheritance, thereby eliminating the need to retrain the model from scratch. Meanwhile, an adaptive sampling strategy is employed to enrich the design of experiments (DOEs). By combining model predictions with the distribution characteristics of the sample space, critical samples near the limit state surface (LSS) are identified. Furthermore, the DOEs updating strategy is introduced to control sample quality and improve the fitting accuracy to the LSS. Comparative studies with similar methods are conducted to evaluate the proposed AL-IDNN method. Results from benchmark examples and a prestressed hollow slab girder bridge case demonstrate its effectiveness in terms of both accuracy and efficiency in reliability analysis.

title: Decision reliability analysis framework for intelligent unmanned system-of-systems using the cooperative multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient
exported_title: Decision reliability analysis framework for intelligent unmanned system-of-systems using the cooperative multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient

metadata.abstract: The decision reliability is the capability of the intelligent unmanned system-of-systems (IUSoS) to make and execute decisions under a disturbed environment. However, the inherent uncertainty of individual autonomy may render decisions unreliable, leading to task failures and resource wastage. To address this issue, we propose a novel decision reliability analysis framework for the IUSoS using the cooperative multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (C-MADDPG). Firstly, considering individual autonomy and functional diversity, a multilayer operation network based on graph coloring theory is established to provide a foundation for decision analysis. Secondly, a distributed decision model based on the enhanced actor-critic (AC) architecture is presented to maintain the individual stable decision-making ability. Thirdly, considering the impact of individual decisions on reliability, an operation-loop-oriented decision reliability assessment model is proposed to quantify decision reliability. Then, the decision reliability is optimized by the C-MADDPG algorithm, which updates the enhanced AC network with the cooperative reward. Finally, a case study on a multi-agent collaborative scenario demonstrates the feasibility of the methodology. The proposed method receives the most rewards compared with variant algorithms and consistently outperforms them in task completion degree, providing a technical approach for improving system-of-systems reliability under distributed architectures and demonstrating that the cooperative reward mechanism balances individual autonomy with system reliability.

title: Cascading failure analysis of critical infrastructure in conflict zones: a large language model-driven knowledge graph framework
exported_title: Cascading failure analysis of critical infrastructure in conflict zones: a large language model-driven knowledge graph framework

metadata.abstract: Modern geopolitical conflicts increasingly target interdependent critical infrastructures, where localized damage can trigger cascading failures, leading to widespread disruption of essential public services. Traditional intelligence safety assessment frameworks struggle to process the dynamic, unstructured data streams from conflict environments. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces a novel probabilistic framework for dynamic cascading failure analysis of Critical Infrastructure (CI) under attacks by integrating Large Language Model (LLM) and Knowledge Graph (KG). Our novel dual-graph architecture first employs an LLM to automatically construct a Dynamic Battlefield Event Knowledge Graph (BEKG) from real-time Open-Source Intelligence (OSINT), capturing tactical events as they unfold. This dynamic event layer then serves as evidence for a probabilistic inference process on a static Infrastructure Service Dependency Knowledge Graph (ISDKG), which is modeled as a Bayesian Network (BN). This integration enables the simulation of the propagation of cascading failures, translating initial physical damage into a quantifiable risk assessment of widespread service disruptions. Validated through a case study on Ukraine's infrastructure, our system demonstrates high fidelity in automated knowledge construction, provides novel insights into cascading impact analysis, and offers a powerful decision-support tool for assessing the systemic vulnerability and resilience of complex infrastructure networks in conflict zones.

title: Mitigation action-dependent prediction of nuclear plant parameters for severe accident management via conditional generative model
exported_title: Mitigation action-dependent prediction of nuclear plant parameters for severe accident management via conditional generative model

metadata.abstract: Effective severe accident management in nuclear power plants requires situational awareness to anticipate multivariate plant responses under time pressure and uncertainty. While artificial intelligence–based surrogate models can support real-time decisions, many studies use recursive multistep forecasting, which tends to accumulate errors over long horizons and often does not reflect operator mitigation actions explicitly. This study proposes an action-conditioned, multivariate multistep prediction model for severe accident decision support. By integrating a transformer, Autoformer, temporal convolutional network, and conditional variational autoencoder, the model produces direct multi-horizon forecasts with uncertainty estimates and represents mitigation actuation states as conditional inputs. For model training and testing, a database was generated using the MAAP 5.06 code with optimized discretization intervals used for data generation and Latin hypercube sampling applied to obtain representative severe accident scenarios with reduced computational cost. The resulting action-conditioned predictions support technical support center staff and plant operators in comparing mitigation options against a no-action baseline and also in assessing key safety-related trends during severe accident progression.

title: Robust reinforcement learning with graph neural networks for stochastic urban rail daily maintenance scheduling
exported_title: Robust reinforcement learning with graph neural networks for stochastic urban rail daily maintenance scheduling

metadata.abstract: Urban rail daily maintenance scheduling is challenged by urgent task insertions, limited time windows, and multi-resource requirements. This paper formulates the problem as a stochastic resource-constrained project scheduling problem on dynamic directed acyclic graphs and proposes a preference-conditioned graph neural network (GNN) and deep reinforcement learning framework for real-time rescheduling. The GNN combines precedence-aware propagation and change-decaying message passing to encode topology shifts after interruptions and insertions, while deterministic action masking guarantees precedence- and resource-feasible decisions. The policy is conditioned on a dispatcher-specified preference vector and trained with an Augmented Tchebycheff objective, enabling online adaptation among makespan, overtime penalty, financial cost, maintenance quality, and resource fairness without retraining. Experiments on PSPLIB show near-optimal static performance, including a 0.29% optimality gap on J120 with linear inference complexity. In stochastic insertion environments, the method achieves strong Pareto-front quality in hypervolume, IGD, and non-dominated solutions, while obtaining the best fixed-preference composite cost with sub-second inference latency. It also demonstrates robust cross-scale and zero-shot transfer to the Shenzhen Metro network. On real-world metro data, the framework achieves an average makespan of 625.03 min in 1.17 s, while additional stress tests verify its robustness, interpretability, and industrial applicability.

title: Dynamic vulnerability assessment of urban rail transit systems using spatiotemporal deep learning
exported_title: Dynamic vulnerability assessment of urban rail transit systems using spatiotemporal deep learning

metadata.abstract: A dynamic vulnerability assessment framework that integrates deep learning and complex networks is proposed to better understand the responses of urban rail transit (URT) systems to various disruptions. Specifically, a spatiotemporal deep learning model is developed to forecast network passenger flows over different time periods. A node importance evaluation method considering dynamic travel demands and static network structural characteristics is presented. A comprehensive metric is designed to assess both structural and functional vulnerabilities of the network. The proposed method is validated using Shanghai's URT system as a case study. The results reveal that: (1) The proposed graph convolutional network-temporal kolmogorov-arnold network (GCN-TKAN) model accurately predicts passenger flows across different time periods, achieving an average R² of 0.865 on the testing data, an improvement of 0.056 compared to the second-best model (TKAN); (2) When a sequential single-node attack, guided by the proposed node-importance metric, removes the top 5% of stations, overall network performance drops by 45.00%, which is 4.92% higher than the average decline caused by other basic attack strategies. The innovation of this study lies in the joint modeling of time-varying passenger flows and spatial topological properties, which accurately quantifies the network's vulnerability under different disturbance scenarios, providing a theoretical basis for enhancing system resilience.

title: An adaptive multi-dimensional protection framework for 5G cloud-native networks using collaborative multi-agent systems
exported_title: An adaptive multi-dimensional protection framework for 5G cloud-native networks using collaborative multi-agent systems

metadata.abstract: With the deep integration of cloud infrastructure and 5G, microservices have become the mainstream architecture for operators to deliver core network services to 5G users. However, the fine-grained nature of such services also expands the attack surface, introducing new security risks. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a dynamic security policy configuration framework for microservices. Based on the Multi-Agent Proximal Policy Optimization (MAPPO) algorithm, the framework resolves high-dimensional collaborative decision-making problems in microservice scenarios through cooperative gaming and state sharing among intelligent agents. Compared with existing static or single-agent solutions, our framework enables more efficient security collaboration in multi-agent environments. Simulation experiments demonstrate that the framework can dynamically formulate security protection and quality of service (QoS) assurance strategies according to the current system state, thereby effectively resisting continuous adversarial attacks while minimizing the impact on service quality.

title: Active Bayesian support vector regression with importance sampling for rare event reliability analysis
exported_title: Active Bayesian support vector regression with importance sampling for rare event reliability analysis

metadata.abstract: Importance sampling achieves variance reduction by introducing an importance sampling density function, and it is one of the most promising methods for reliability analysis. This paper aims to further improve the efficiency and accuracy of importance sampling by integrating the Bayesian support vector regression model with an active learning strategy, thereby enabling its application to a broad spectrum of engineering problems involving rare event analysis. To achieve this, we propose a novel learning function and a new candidate samples construction method that allow the model to actively select training points near the failure surface, characterized by the highest prediction error and greatest spatial diversity. Additionally, we introduce a stopping criterion based on the global prediction error across unclassified points, ensuring that the algorithm terminates with sufficient accuracy. Through both academic case studies and practical engineering examples, we demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms traditional importance sampling methods as well as other active learning surrogate modeling techniques in terms of efficiency and accuracy.

title: A novel data-driven quantitative resilience evaluation method for large-scale systems
exported_title: A novel data-driven quantitative resilience evaluation method for large-scale systems

metadata.abstract: To address disaster-induced damages to systems, resilience theory offers a broader and more practical alternative to traditional risk theory. However, resilience evaluation for large-scale systems faces challenges such as massive data and complex disaster scenarios. This paper proposes a data-driven framework for large-scale system resilience evaluation. First, a standardized dataset structure is defined, and a disaster process recognition method based on metric learning is developed. Second, probabilistic functions linking disaster processes to system performance are established as resilience indicators.
