title: Multi Objective Inverse Design of Cement-Based Pseudocapacitive Electrodes Using Interpretable Machine Learning
exported_title: Multi Objective Inverse Design of Cement-Based Pseudocapacitive Electrodes Using Interpretable Machine Learning

metadata.abstract: Integrating electrochemical energy storage into cement-based materials provides a route to multifunctional building components. Multicomponent formulations simultaneously regulate the pseudocapacitive active phase, cement hydration phases, conductive carbon phases and pore structure, leading to coupled electrochemical and mechanical requirements for cement-based pseudocapacitive electrode design. Therefore, an interpretable machine learning workflow was developed to establish predictive relationships between multicomponent formulations and the device level areal energy density and compressive strength of cement-based positive electrodes. The optimized gradient boosting decision tree models achieved testing R2 values of 0.881 and 0.853 for device level areal energy density and compressive strength. SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis identified current density as the most influential feature for energy density. Features related to conductive networks and water-to-solid ratio also contributed to the predictions, with microstructural characterization supporting the proposed material interpretation. A candidate design window with a water-to-solid ratio of 0.80 to 0.83, the carbon black and carbon nanotube contents of 2.00 to 2.13 wt.% and 1.86 to 2.24 wt.%, the carbon fiber and MnO2 contents of 1.97 to 2.20 wt.% and 10.28 to 12.65 wt.% was identified using strength constrained multi objective particle swarm optimization. The selected formulation achieved 0.57 ± 0.01 mWh/cm2 and 3.13 ± 0.08 MPa, with prediction deviations of 5.26% and 3.51%. This work provides a data supported approach for formulation screening under coupled electrochemical and mechanical requirements.

title: Physics-Informed Topological Graph Neural Networks for micromechanical insights and uncertainty quantification in void-containing composites
exported_title: Physics-Informed Topological Graph Neural Networks for micromechanical insights and uncertainty quantification in void-containing composites

metadata.abstract: Predicting the performance uncertainty of porous composites necessitates capturing the highly non-linear damage mechanisms governed by authentic defect morphologies. This study proposes an integrated experimental-computational framework to unravel these complex micromechanisms. First, high-resolution in-situ micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) is utilized to extract stochastic, process-induced void topologies, directly informing the reconstruction of experimentally validated, elastoplastic Representative Volume Elements (RVEs). To decisively overcome the prohibitive computational cost of finite element analysis (FEA) for large-scale stochastic evaluation, we develop the Physics-Informed Topological Graph Attention Network (PIT-GAT). By abstracting microstructures into a primal–dual graph and integrating label-free physical soft constraints with weakest-link statistical pooling, PIT-GAT achieves an O(104) speedup over traditional non-linear solvers. Leveraging Explainable AI (XAI), the model autonomously reveals that void coalescence is fundamentally driven by diagonal plastic shear bands (30°–45°) rather than perpendicular Mode-I tearing. Furthermore, it naturally captures the classical size effect of void clusters. Finally, predictive uncertainty is reframed as a physically meaningful proxy for material instability, probabilistically mapping this variance to potential micro-damage bifurcation loci to establish robust, risk-aware design guidelines.

title: Causal Contrastive Learning for Reliability-oriented Fault Detection in Wastewater Treatment under Process Uncertainty
exported_title: Causal Contrastive Learning for Reliability-oriented Fault Detection in Wastewater Treatment under Process Uncertainty

metadata.abstract: To ensure reliable operations and quality control in wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs), data-driven fault detection has received wide attention recently, but reliable detection of faults or failures with respect to process variables or quality-related variables remains challenging due to significant process uncertainty. In WWTPs, fault detection is usually affected by data uncertainty, operating-condition uncertainty, and inter-variable relationship uncertainty. These uncertainties are essentially caused by delayed water-quality measurements, wastewater influent loads, or other environmental factors, such as temperature and humidity. In response to these issues, this study proposes causal structure contrastive learning (CSCL) for reliable WWTPs fault detection. In this method, CSCL addresses observation uncertainty by learning window-level representations rather than relying on isolated delayed measurements. Also, it can handle operating-condition uncertainty through causality-preserving augmentation, which retains normal causal structures under admissible influent and process variations. Furthermore, inter-variable relationship uncertainty, by constructing causality-disrupted negative samples that break internal causal dependencies or perturb exogenous-disturbance-driven causal patterns, can be addressed efficiently. By comparing causality-consistent with causality-disrupted samples, CSCL can separate normal process variability from fault-induced causal changes, thereby strengthening the reliability of fault detection. Experiments on BSM2 fault scenarios and full-scale WWTP data demonstrate that CSCL can outperform other fault detection baselines.

title: Neural Scheduling for Carrier Aircraft Recovery with Bolter and Aerial Refueling
exported_title: Neural Scheduling for Carrier Aircraft Recovery with Bolter and Aerial Refueling

metadata.abstract: Existing carrier aircraft recovery scheduling studies commonly assume a predetermined aircraft set, limiting their applicability to safety-critical operations involving bolter events, fuel-endurance risk, and online insertion of new-wave tasks. This study formulates dynamic carrier aircraft recovery scheduling as an event-driven sequential decision-making problem that jointly considers bolter recovery, aerial refueling, remaining-fuel evolution, and online task insertion. A Long-Range Dependency-Aware Proximal Policy Optimization algorithm, termed LDA-PPO, is developed by integrating a dynamic recovery pool with a multi-layer masking mechanism. The pool maps time-varying aircraft sets to a stable neural decision interface. The dynamic-recovery-pool and attention masks exclude empty slots from representation learning, while the action-feasibility mask excludes unavailable aircraft from action selection. Each aircraft is encoded as an aircraft token, and multi-head self-attention captures global dependencies in fuel safety, mechanical integrity, mission priority, bolter risk, and new-wave arrivals. In 128 single-wave scenarios with 32 aircraft, LDA-PPO combined higher mean composite objectives and low online computational cost with fewer touchdown fuel-reserve violations and better fuel reliability than most baselines. It handled different task sizes within the dynamic recovery pool capacity and multi-wave missions without parameter updates. The proposed method provides a reliability-oriented online decision-support framework for dynamic carrier aircraft recovery.

title: Pseudo-Anomaly Data Driven Robust and Confidence Information Redundancy Approach in Aircraft Components
exported_title: Pseudo-Anomaly Data Driven Robust and Confidence Information Redundancy Approach in Aircraft Components

metadata.abstract: Information redundancy (IR) for flight parameters requires robustness to corrupted auxiliary measurements and confidence assessment of the resulting estimates. This paper proposes a Pseudo-Anomaly data-driven Robust and Confidence IR (PA-RCIR) framework. A Random Anomaly Scenario Generator (RASG) generates pseudo-anomalous auxiliary inputs through complementary signal-level perturbations while preserving their target references. A Dual-phase Robust Variational Inference Network (DRVIN) jointly learns from original and perturbed inputs using a probabilistic latent representation. An Empirical Cumulative Distribution function of prediction Statistical Features (ECDSF) constructs empirical confidence scores from repeated prediction samples and a normal-validation reference distribution. Experiments use real flight records from the Thor and Ibis UAV datasets, with angle-of-attack (AoA) redundancy as a representative task and separate training and evaluation on each dataset. Over ten runs, the mean absolute error (MAE) under normal inputs is 0.0120 on Thor and 0.0007 on Ibis. Under controlled bias and noise corruptions affecting five auxiliary-input channels, the corresponding values are 0.0200 and 0.0012. In both evaluated multichannel mixed-anomaly scenarios, PA-RCIR achieves statistically significant improvements over all six baselines for the three prediction-error metrics after Holm correction. Representative cases and expected calibration error analysis characterize the relationship between confidence scores and prediction quality, with calibration behavior varying across input conditions and prediction-sample statistics. These results support robust information redundancy with empirical confidence assessment under the evaluated input conditions.

title: Human–AI Teaming Reliability in Diagnostic Tasks: Performance-Shaping Factors and Quantitative Modeling
exported_title: Human–AI Teaming Reliability in Diagnostic Tasks: Performance-Shaping Factors and Quantitative Modeling

metadata.abstract: Humans and AI systems are increasingly forming human–AI teaming configurations for operating complex safety-critical systems. Understanding and quantifying human–AI teaming reliability is therefore essential for system safety, yet it remains overlooked despite extensive research on human–AI teaming. Here we investigate certain key performance-shaping factors (PSFs) influencing teaming reliability and develop data-driven quantitative models. We focus on an important workflow in which humans make final decisions while AI provides advice in simulated medical diagnosis. In a preregistered behavioral experiment (N = 420), we measure human reliability and human–AI teaming reliability at two time points separated by one week. We manipulate AI reliability, task difficulty, and teaming mode (simultaneous vs. sequential), while exploring the roles of human baseline ability (lower vs. higher performers) and decision-making style (conservative vs. aggressive decision-makers). Results show that AI reliability and teaming mode affect human reliability gains from AI assistance. Sequential mode (humans access AI advice after forming initial judgments) yields greater reliability gains than simultaneous mode (humans access diagnostic cases and AI advice concurrently), with exploratory analyses suggesting that this advantage may be limited to aggressive decision-makers. We finally build two linear and nonlinear models of teaming reliability. Our findings advance the understanding of PSFs and quantitative modeling for human–AI teaming reliability.

title: Context-Aware Prompt Encoding Compression and Sentence-Level Pooling based LLMs for Industrial Equipment Health Status Prediction
exported_title: Context-Aware Prompt Encoding Compression and Sentence-Level Pooling based LLMs for Industrial Equipment Health Status Prediction

metadata.abstract: Accurate forecasting of industrial equipment health states is crucial for improving system reliability, enabling predictive maintenance, and supporting intelligent manufacturing. Conventional forecasting methods primarily rely on structured sensor data and often fail to leverage reliability-related knowledge contained in unstructured sources such as maintenance reports and failure logs. Although large language models (LLMs) show strong capabilities in textual understanding, their application to industrial prognostics and health management remains limited due to weak integration with quantitative signals and sensitivity to irrelevant textual information. To address these issues, this study proposes a cross-modal forecasting framework, Context-Aware Prompt Encoding Compression and Sentence-Level Pooling–Large Language Model (CASP-LLM). The framework integrates maintenance text with sensor time-series data to improve equipment health-state prediction. Prompts derived from statistical characteristics of sensor signals guide context-aware encoding and sentence-level pooling to extract reliability-relevant semantic features, while a parallel pathway captures temporal degradation patterns from sensor observations. The resulting representations are fused for prediction. Experiments are conducted on public fuel cell datasets and two real industrial heat exchanger datasets. The results demonstrate that CASP-LLM consistently outperforms LSTM, Transformer, TimeLLM, and other comparative models across multiple forecasting horizons.

title: Uncertainty-aware dynamic-static knowledge injection for few-shot electromagnetic interference failure assessment via large language models
exported_title: Uncertainty-aware dynamic-static knowledge injection for few-shot electromagnetic interference failure assessment via large language models

metadata.abstract: Electromagnetic interference (EMI) can reduce the reliability of electronic systems and lead to functional failures, making EMI immunity assessment essential for reliable system operation. However, such assessment usually requires many experiments, and the resulting data are often costly or unavailable. This makes few-shot EMI failure assessment difficult, especially when model uncertainty must be controlled and physical constraints must be respected. To address the above issues, we propose the Dynamic-Static Knowledge Injection Large Language Model (DSKI-LLM) for few-shot EMI failure assessment. The framework contains a static knowledge injection module and an uncertainty-aware dynamic module. The static module combines Domain-Corrective Alignment Loss with gated low-rank adaptation (LoRA) to encourage representations consistent with electromagnetic knowledge. The dynamic module uses predictive entropy to estimate confidence and adjusts retrieval depth during inference. Low-confidence queries retrieve more historical EMI cases, while high-confidence queries avoid unnecessary context expansion. We evaluate DSKI-LLM on PhyEMI, a benchmark dataset built from a controlled EMI experimental platform. Results show that DSKI-LLM improves few-shot prediction over the evaluated baselines and produces more reliable probability estimates. By combining prediction with uncertainty estimation and adaptive evidence retrieval, the proposed method supports more trustworthy EMI failure assessment under limited data.

title: Quality-aware LLM root-cause analysis of offshore incident reports: report quality as an upstream uncertainty in safety analytics
exported_title: Quality-aware LLM root-cause analysis of offshore incident reports: report quality as an upstream uncertainty in safety analytics

metadata.abstract: Incident reports are increasingly analyzed with large language models (LLMs), yet most studies treat report text as a fixed input. This study examines report quality as an upstream uncertainty in automated root cause analysis (RCA): whether the available record conditions what causal evidence can be recovered, how LLM-RCA models behave, and what safety narrative becomes visible. Using 1,000 public offshore incident records from BSEE, we develop an auditable LLM-assisted ranking pipeline that harmonizes heterogeneous reports, constructs an interpretable weak prior, aggregates listwise judgments with a regularized Bradley–Terry (BT) model, and incorporates targeted human pairwise calibration. The resulting quality prior is stable, with 99.985% of reports remaining within ±1 stratum under bootstrap perturbation. We then evaluate 250 Q-stratified incidents using a human-reviewed reference set and five GPT-5-mini runs. Mean top-level reference labels increase from 1.10 in Q1 to 3.38 in Q5, indicating richer recoverable RCA evidence. GPT-5-mini precision and F1 generally improve with quality; the model also under-abstains on sparse low-quality records. Report quality further conditions the recoverable safety narrative: low-quality reports emphasize personnel performance and external triggers, whereas high-quality reports reveal organizational and systemic contributors. These findings suggest that report quality is a first-order variable in LLM-based safety analytics.

title: AI-Enabled construction safety management: A paradigm shift from passive compliance to proactive empowerment
exported_title: AI-Enabled construction safety management: A paradigm shift from passive compliance to proactive empowerment

metadata.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly applied to construction safety through hazard recognition, risk assessment, monitoring, and decision support. Despite rapid advances, existing systems differ substantially in their ability to interpret risk, generate safety-related outputs, and assume intervention authority. This study develops a reliability-oriented maturity framework to classify AI-enabled construction-safety functions. A PRISMA-guided review identified 171 eligible publications, including 153 technical studies and 18 reviews. The technical studies were characterized using two complementary dimensions: Objective Scanning Response (OSR), describing risk-information processing, and Safety State Output (SSO), describing safety-related output. Building on these functional profiles, an L0-L5 maturity framework is developed to characterize functional position, intervention authority, Operational Design Domain, and fallback capability. A Perception-Cognition-Decision-Execution (P-C-D-E) architecture is further developed to represent the functional structure of closed-loop safety intervention, including fast-slow functional separation, state verification, and fallback. Representative scenarios illustrate the framework’s application. The coded evidence indicates a marked asymmetry between risk understanding and physical intervention. The framework remains theoretically derived and has not undergone independent maturity-classification validation. Its contribution is nonetheless substantive: it provides a reproducible classification procedure, an authority-allocation model, and a reliability-oriented evaluation pathway specifying the evidence required before higher levels of autonomous intervention can be justified.

title: Sparse stage path graph Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) for bearing remaining useful life prediction
exported_title: Sparse stage path graph Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) for bearing remaining useful life prediction

metadata.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have been utilized to analyze monitoring data for predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of bearings. Conventional methods typically aggregate degradation features through GNNs after converting the monitoring data into graphs. However, traditional GNNs face two primary challenges: (1) a single stage of graph data construction is insufficient to capture the complexity of bearing degradation, and (2) the effectiveness of these methods heavily depends on the selection of initial weights, making them susceptible to noise interference. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a novel sparse stage path graph Kolmogorov-Arnold network (SSPGKAN) model to enhance bearing RUL prediction. First, a siamese KAN model is developed to classify bearing degradation stages, and stage path graphs (SPGs) are constructed to aggregate the degradation features. Subsequently, the SSPGKAN model replaces traditional edges in the graph structure with learnable functions, overcoming the limitations of initial linear weight selection in GNNs and enabling dynamic transmission of graph data. Additionally, a sparse graph optimization method is used to reduce the impact of noise and accurately predict bearing RUL. Verification results from two test bench datasets demonstrate that the SSPGKAN model improves the prediction efficiency and accuracy of bearing RUL.

title: Resilience enhancement study of renewable energy power networks by integrating subnet division and priority enhanced Q-Learning
exported_title: Resilience enhancement study of renewable energy power networks by integrating subnet division and priority enhanced Q-Learning

metadata.abstract: With the acceleration of global energy transition and escalating climate challenges, the large-scale integration of renewable energy into power systems has become inevitable. However, the intermittency of renewable energy output significantly exacerbates the risk of cascading failures in power grids. Traditional critical node protection and post-fault restoration methods struggle to adapt to renewable energy uncertainties, bottlenecking grid resilience assessment and enhancement. This study proposes a dual-phase resilience enhancement framework for renewable energy power systems, addressing pre-failure protection and post-failure restoration challenges. The methodology integrates a Subnet Division-Based Strategy and a Priority Enhanced Q-Learning-Based Restoration to mitigate cascading failures. Subnet Division-Based Strategy partitions networks into functional subnets using breadth-first search and maximum flow algorithms, identifying critical nodes through betweenness centrality optimization. Priority Enhanced Q-Learning-Based Restoration incorporates subnet priority rankings into Q-learning to create a guided exploration mechanism for repair sequence optimization. Experimental validations on IEEE test cases with renewable energy show that: 1) The Subnetwork Division-Based Strategy enables critical node protection, reducing resilience loss by 10%–30% across four attack scenarios; 2) Priority Enhanced Q-Learning-Based Restoration achieves 10% lower resilience loss and a 0.5–1 unit resilience improvement compared to conventional methods; 3) Subnet division prioritization combined with Q-Learning yields a 26.3% performance gain. This dual-phase approach provides grid operators with preventive protection strategies and real-time restoration optimization capabilities, establishes a replicable framework for enhancing network resilience.

title: A GCN-based availability analysis method for mobile network with spatial–temporal effect awareness
exported_title: A GCN-based availability analysis method for mobile network with spatial–temporal effect awareness

metadata.abstract: The spatial–temporal effect induces complex dynamic changes in the states of network, increasing the risk of mobile network unavailability. Current availability analysis methods are difficult to establish the network spatial–temporal dynamic variation pattern. Machine learning methods avoid the weakness of explicitly modeling effect patterns. However, these methods usually neglect spatial topology changes and abrupt temporal dynamics. To address the above problem, we propose a GCN-Based Availability Analysis Method for Networks with Spatial–Temporal Effect Awareness (Gstea). In the spatial domain, the spatial variation is captured by graph adaptation and graph convolution. In the temporal domain, the Ek (ERP-based time-aligned with k-shape integration to preserve shape similarity) fully aligns the temporal sequence to identify abrupt network changes and generates enhanced graph signal propagation. Experimental results show that Gstea outperforms the best-performing baseline methods in various complex network scenarios (average improvement range from 7% to 26%). This demonstrates that Gstea can provide a more accurate evaluation in networks with spatial–temporal effect.

title: An interpretable fault diagnosis framework for nuclear power plant via graph representation and multi-task learning
exported_title: An interpretable fault diagnosis framework for nuclear power plant via graph representation and multi-task learning

metadata.abstract: Neural networks have great potential for enhancing fault diagnosis in nuclear power plants (NPPs). However, current approaches often face challenges such as limited interpretability, data scarcity, and insufficient handling of open-set fault conditions. To address these issues, this article proposes a novel interpretable fault diagnosis framework that integrates graph-based representation with multi-task learning. The framework uses a graph structure to encode the physical and functional relationships within NPPs and integrates it with a hybrid network architecture for spatiotemporal feature extraction. Multi-task learning is then employed to simultaneously perform signal reconstruction, node-level anomaly detection, graph-level fault classification, and prototype learning. Experiments on two reactor systems show that the proposed framework achieves 100% accuracy in closed-set fault classification, even with limited samples, and outperforms baseline models. It also successfully identifies unknown and compound faults in open-set scenarios, providing interpretable insights into fault propagation and affected regions. These results illustrate the framework’s practical potential for improving diagnostic reliability and supporting operators in NPPs.

title: FBSTFnet: A full-band spatiotemporal fusion network for machine remaining useful life prediction
exported_title: FBSTFnet: A full-band spatiotemporal fusion network for machine remaining useful life prediction

metadata.abstract: Remaining Useful Life (RUL) prediction is central to prognostics and health management (PHM) systems, enabling proactive maintenance and preventing major machinery failures. Current deep learning approaches often employ squeeze-and-excitation mechanisms for multi-sensor signal processing, but mainly capture low-frequency features and neglect important information in other frequency bands. In addition, existing spatiotemporal fusion methods rely on computationally heavy architectures that restrict practical deployment. To address these challenges, a Full-Band Spatiotemporal Fusion Network (FBSTFnet) is proposed, featuring four main innovations: a Full-Band Local Interaction Feature (FBLIF) mechanism that enhances multi-frequency representation through discrete cosine transform (DCT)-based spectral transformation; a hybrid architecture integrating gated recurrent units (GRU) with one-dimensional convolutions for efficient temporal–spatial feature extraction; an Easy-ProbSparse self-attention (EPSA) block that improves spatiotemporal fusion while reducing computational cost; and a Memory-Enhanced Local Feature Compensation (MELFC) block that restores long-term temporal continuity by reinforcing memory and compensating local features. The effectiveness of FBSTFnet is demonstrated on two benchmark datasets. Results show that FBSTFnet achieves a lightweight structure with accurate RUL prediction, providing a promising direction for advancing PHM in mechanical systems.

title: Bayesian adaptive elastic net for early prediction of battery cycle life
exported_title: Bayesian adaptive elastic net for early prediction of battery cycle life

metadata.abstract: Accurate prognosis of battery remaining useful life is essential for evaluating reliability and optimizing the utilization of energy storage systems. To address the challenge of multicollinearity among degradation features, we propose a Bayesian adaptive elastic net method that improves prediction accuracy while providing comprehensive uncertainty quantification. The proposed approach implements adaptive shrinkage, applying separate penalty parameters to each regression coefficient to shrink the non-significant variables while preserving the effects of important predictors. By representing Laplace priors as Gaussian-exponential mixtures through data augmentation techniques and approximating the normalizing constant numerically, we develop an efficient Metropolis-Hastings-within-Gibbs sampling framework for posterior inference. Validation using numerical simulations and battery cycle life data demonstrates that the proposed method delivers superior prediction accuracy and robust uncertainty quantification, even under severe multicollinearity, providing an effective solution for battery lifetime prediction.

title: CSIR-Net: a continuous spatio-temporal information redundancy network based on structural priors for satellite telemetry data reliability enhancement
exported_title: CSIR-Net: a continuous spatio-temporal information redundancy network based on structural priors for satellite telemetry data reliability enhancement

metadata.abstract: Enhancing satellite telemetry reliability is essential for status assessment and operational management. However, telemetry data have complex spatio-temporal dependencies and diverse missing patterns, making it challenging for traditional methods with discrete modeling, fixed parameters, and static prediction steps to recover. To address these, this paper proposes a continuous spatio-temporal information redundancy network that transforms degraded discrete data recovery into timestamp-aware continuous-trajectory inference with uncertainty-calibrated selection. Specifically, a long short-term memory network is reconstructed using neural stochastic differential equations to model hidden-state evolution in continuous time, and Ito integrals are incorporated to characterize uneven observation gaps, thereby enabling recovery at arbitrary timestamps. Additionally, time-varying signals and Brownian perturbations are integrated into the model to allow dynamic adjustment of parameters with the input, thereby improving the ability to recover multiple evolving features. Finally, a structure-prior-guided hierarchical graph is constructed to fuse multi-scale dependencies while suppressing redundant error propagation, and multi-head graph attention is used to derive adaptive confidence intervals for selective recovery, thereby improving telemetry reliability without obscuring novel patterns. Experiments on five datasets show the proposed method improves recovery accuracy by 27.7% over the best baseline, achieves 15.2–78.5 ms batch latency, and has strong potential for real-time large-scale telemetry reliability.

title: Lifetime Early Prediction for Second-Life Lithium-Ion Battery: A Hierarchical Bayesian Learning Method
exported_title: Lifetime Early Prediction for Second-Life Lithium-Ion Battery: A Hierarchical Bayesian Learning Method

metadata.abstract: With the rapid growth of electric vehicle (EV) adoption, the widespread use of lithium-ion batteries has brought increasing attention to the echelon utilization of second-life batteries (SLBs). These SLBs, typically retired from EVs upon reaching 80% of their rated capacity, possess considerable potential for deployment in stationary energy storage systems. To fully exploit their remaining capacity, accurate lifetime prediction during second-life applications is essential. This study addresses the early lifetime prediction of SLBs by proposing a hierarchical Bayesian model (HBM). Considering the heterogeneity in degradation behavior under varying working conditions, the method initially performs clustering based on operating conditions. Subsequently, a two-level hierarchical Bayesian framework is constructed to model the relationships between battery groups and individual units, enabling more accurate lifetime estimation. Bayesian inference is employed to optimize model parameters using extracted features, thereby reducing predictive uncertainty and enhancing overall accuracy. Validation on a self-collected SLB aging dataset demonstrates that the proposed method outperforms conventional machine learning approaches, especially under data-limited conditions. Quantitatively, the model achieves an average root mean square error (RMSE) of 113.444 cycles (±31.423), mean absolute error (MAE) of 76.616 cycles (±15.516), and mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 17.188% (±4.073%) on the test set.

title: PAKP: Parallelized Adaptive Kriging method with Partial least squares for high-dimensional reliability analysis
exported_title: PAKP: Parallelized Adaptive Kriging method with Partial least squares for high-dimensional reliability analysis

metadata.abstract: In structural reliability analysis, tackling high-dimensional problems with computational efficiency remains a significant challenge. To address this, the paper proposes a novel active learning method, termed Parallelized Adaptive Kriging with Partial least squares (PAKP), which is designed to enhance both accuracy and efficiency in high-dimensional reliability analysis of complex engineering structures. PAKP combines Kriging-based surrogate modeling with Partial Least Squares (PLS) for dimensionality reduction, effectively mitigating the challenges posed by curse of dimensionality. Another key innovation is the learning function allocation scheme, which adaptively selects the most suitable learning function from a portfolio to identify informative samples for refining the surrogate model. Additionally, a parallelization strategy is introduced to select multiple samples in each iteration, significantly enhancing the computational efficiency. An importance sampling scheme is also incorporated to handle small failure probabilities in high-dimensional settings. The effectiveness of PAKP is validated through five numerical examples, demonstrating its superior performance in balancing accuracy and efficiency. This highlights its potential as a promising solution for high-dimensional reliability analysis.

title: Cavitation reliability assessment of aviation fuel centrifugal pumps combining kriging and subset simulation important sampling
exported_title: Cavitation reliability assessment of aviation fuel centrifugal pumps combining kriging and subset simulation important sampling

metadata.abstract: Cavitation in aviation fuel centrifugal pumps can lead to impeller erosion and performance degradation, posing significant reliability risks. To efficiently assess low-probability cavitation failures under multidimensional uncertainty, this study proposes a surrogate-based reliability analysis framework named AK-IEI-SSIS, which integrates Kriging modeling, an Improved Expected Improvement (IEI) learning function, and Subset Simulation Importance Sampling (SSIS). The framework adaptively refines sampling near failure boundaries to enhance accuracy and computational efficiency. Its performance is validated through multiple benchmark cases involving nonlinear and high-dimensional systems. A Python-based parametric platform is also developed to orchestrate parametric modeling, meshing, CFD simulation, and reliability analysis. Applied to an aviation fuel centrifugal pump, the framework accurately quantifies cavitation-induced failure probabilities as low as 5.63 × 10⁻⁴ using only 202 CFD evaluations, achieving a 99 % reduction in computational cost compared to Monte Carlo methods. Although demonstrated on a specific pump, the framework is applicable to reliability assessment of rotating fluid machinery under uncertainty, supporting reliability analysis and maintenance planning for next-generation aerospace propulsion systems.

title: Multi-fidelity Kriging structural reliability analysis with the fusion of non-hierarchical low-fidelity models
exported_title: Multi-fidelity Kriging structural reliability analysis with the fusion of non-hierarchical low-fidelity models

metadata.abstract: Adaptive Kriging is a common Bayesian statistical method and has founded wide application in structural reliability analysis. Multi-fidelity (MF) Kriging model can significantly reduce computational cost compared to single-fidelity Kriging model. However, research on MF Kriging reliability analysis remains relatively limited in the literature. Most existing MF Kriging approaches assume that reliability performance functions of varying fidelity levels follow a hierarchical nature, which is not applicable when the performance functions exhibit non-hierarchical fidelity levels across the input space. To handle this challenge, we develop a novel Bayesian adaptive MF Kriging method to integrate high-fidelity (HF) data with non-hierarchical low-fidelity (LF) Kriging models for reliability analysis. We first use the local correlation and variance-weighted fusion approach to fuse all the non-hierarchical LF models. Then, the hierarchical Kriging is employed for the construction of MF model based on HF data and the fused LF model. A new adaptive hierarchical refinement strategy is proposed. This strategy mainly involves a new hierarchical expected feasibility function (HEFF) for identifying the location and fidelity of the optimal sample simultaneously, and a low-fidelity-selection (LFS) algorithm based on Kriging-Believer approach to allocate simulations among non-hierarchical LF models. One numerical example and two engineering examples involving an aircraft tubing and an airfoil stiffener rib, are used to validate the performance of our method.

title: Auto-learning process risk optimization considering uncertain degradation pathways: A bayesian-learning-informed termination approach
exported_title: Auto-learning process risk optimization considering uncertain degradation pathways: A bayesian-learning-informed termination approach

metadata.abstract: Safety-critical task systems operating under uncertain degradation pathways demand precise decision paradigm to balance operational continuity against catastrophic failure risks. This study addresses a risk control problem arising in mission-critical systems under degradation evolution uncertainties. To tackle potential failure risks stemming from process uncertainties, we develop a tractable risk control model that incorporates parameter learning into the adaptive termination decision process, constituting an auto-learning control-limit policy. The integrated optimization problem is representable as a finite-horizon MDP framework, which strives to mitigate the aggregate losses originating from (a) task termination and (b) operational anomalies. Theoretical analysis confirms the presence of termination thresholds along with its monotonic characteristic relative to inspection counts and degradation severities, revealing an age-state-dependent threshold structure that adapts to non-steady conditions. We further account for the implication of core degradation/cost parameters on risk alleviation, which facilitates efficient decision-making. Comparative evaluations demonstrate that the optimal policy outperforms alternative strategies over risk loss control.

title: Causal graph inference with adaptive dynamic structure learning for mechanism-oriented fault diagnosis in dynamic industrial systems
exported_title: Causal graph inference with adaptive dynamic structure learning for mechanism-oriented fault diagnosis in dynamic industrial systems

metadata.abstract: Complex rotating machinery is essential to safety-critical industrial systems, where undetected faults may trigger cascading failures and pose serious safety risks. Inherent dynamic couplings, multi-source interferences, and time-varying feedback loops lead to complex fault propagation, presenting major challenges for reliable and interpretable diagnostics. Traditional data-driven methods, primarily relying on correlation-based models, often fail to generalize under non-stationary conditions and provide limited understanding of underlying failure mechanisms. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes the Dynamic Causal Mechanism Learning Diagnostics Framework (DCMLDF), designed to enhance system reliability and mitigate fault risks. The framework incorporates a multi-scale temporal encoder, semantics-aware causal graph inference, a causality-guided predictive decoder, and a unified optimization strategy to enable end-to-end modeling of dynamic fault evolution from high-dimensional sensor data. Evaluated on four benchmark datasets, DCMLDF consistently outperforms five representative baselines in both accuracy and stability. More importantly, it reveals system-level causal dependencies that characterize evolving failure pathways, thereby enabling early warning, root-cause identification, and risk-informed decision-making. These findings highlight the framework’s effectiveness in improving predictive reliability and operational safety, offering a scalable solution for prognostics and health management in complex mechanical systems.

title: Sparse Bayesian learning for joint load-parameter-response identification
exported_title: Sparse Bayesian learning for joint load-parameter-response identification

metadata.abstract: The joint identification of the structural loads, parameters, and responses from the sparse measurements is crucial but challenging for assessing the operational conditions of civil infrastructures. Existing joint identification methods typically require the prior information, such as the loading locations and the covariance matrices of the process and observation noise, which are unavailable in practice. To address this limitation, a sparse Bayesian learning technique based on the transmissibility matrix is proposed for the joint load-parameter-response identification. The spatial sparsity of damage indices (defined as the structural parameter change) and loads is adopted as priors in the Bayesian framework. The Expectation-Maximum (EM) algorithm is used to iteratively estimate the most probable values of the damage indices, unknown force time history, measurement noise, and other variance parameters. A modified Metropolis-Hastings (MH) algorithm is developed to jointly generate posterior samples of structural parameters and loads for the expectation calculation in the EM algorithm. Upon convergence, some hyperparameters approach infinity and the associated damage indices and forces become zero, resulting in the sparsity of the identified damage indices and loads. Consequently, the damage indices and input forces are located and quantified simultaneously, and the full-field structural responses are sequentially reconstructed with suppressed uncertainties. The proposed method is verified by a numerical simply-supported beam, a laboratory-tested three-story frame model, and a three-span continuous bridge model. Results demonstrate that the proposed sparse Bayesian technique can accurately identify the damage indices, loads, and responses simultaneously, even when the load position is unknown.

title: A double-loop adaptive Kriging-based robust design optimization method with aleatory and epistemic uncertainty
exported_title: A double-loop adaptive Kriging-based robust design optimization method with aleatory and epistemic uncertainty

metadata.abstract: Robust design optimization under aleatory and epistemic uncertainty still remains several key issues, such as lack of a unified quantitative robustness measure, suffering from huge computational burden and in need for proper searching strategy, etc. To remedy these, a novel adaptive Kriging-based robust design optimization method with aleatory and epistemic uncertainty is proposed. Based on the unified MC-based simulation technique for both aleatory and epistemic uncertainty, a decision model for robustness measure is built to comprehensively characterize the nominal expectation, the variation due to epistemic uncertainty alone, and the mixed variation due to both epistemic and aleatory uncertainty. To solve the decision model, a double-loop adaptive Kriging-based method is proposed, which can ensure a balance of optimality and robustness with limited calculations of the real deterministic objective. The inner-loop Kriging is locally updated at each training sample of the outer-loop one to ensure accuracy of the minimization and maximization at each focal element of the deterministic objective, while the outer-loop Kriging is deeply coupled into each simulation level of the subset simulation optimization to quickly converge to the optimum without much loss of accuracy. A toy example is used to illustrate the performance of the proposed methodology, engineering applicability of which is further tested by three real engineering examples.

title: Adaptive Kriging‑assisted enhanced sparrow search with augmented‑Lagrangian first-order reliability method for highly efficient structural reliability analysis
exported_title: Adaptive Kriging‑assisted enhanced sparrow search with augmented‑Lagrangian first-order reliability method for highly efficient structural reliability analysis

metadata.abstract: Uncertainty information exists widely throughout the life cycle of engineering products. Efficient reliability analysis methods are essential to solve complex reliability problems considering multi-source uncertain information. In this study, a hybrid method combining the Active Kriging (AK) model with Enhanced Sparrow Search Optimization (AK-ESSO) is proposed to enhance the performance of classical First-Order Reliability Method (FORM). In the first stage, ESSO’s ability to search for reliability indicators is enhanced through adaptive global search and random local search strategies. In the second stage, the augmented Lagrangian penalty function in FORM is used to enhance the accuracy of the optimization model used to approximate reliability indicators in ESSO. In the third stage, the novel hybrid AK strategy considering global and local accuracy is proposed to enhance the computational efficiency in the limit state assessment process. By combining these three strategies, AK-ESSO enhances the robustness and global performance of FORM in searching for reliability indicators. Using eight numerical and three applicable engineering problems, the AK-ESSO frameworks applied in FORM are compared to the classical FORM algorithm, popular FORM-based metaheuristic algorithms, and hybrid Kriging-based metaheuristic algorithms. The results indicate that AK - ESSO offers significant advantages in efficiency, and in terms of computational accuracy, the augmented Lagrangian optimization probabilistic model provides significant advantages for AK - ESSO, as well as global convergence in terms of robustness.

title: Variational inference for hierarchical Bayesian learning framework for model updating with non-stationary prediction errors
exported_title: Variational inference for hierarchical Bayesian learning framework for model updating with non-stationary prediction errors

metadata.abstract: Quantification of model uncertainties are essential for ensuring the credibility of numerical models in robust structural response prediction and reliability assessment. Probabilistic model updating provides an effective way to achieve this purpose. Among these methods, the hierarchical Bayesian modeling (HBM) framework has been widely recognized as a powerful tool for jointly estimating the uncertainty of model parameters and prediction errors, thereby enabling a comprehensive quantification of model uncertainties. Typically, Gaussian white noise (GWN) is used as the probabilistic model for prediction errors, but this assumption fails to capture their non-stationary characteristics. To overcome this limitation, a new HBM framework is developed, which replaces GWN with a Gaussian process (GP) model. An orthogonal expansion is utilized to approximate the GP model as the summation of orthogonal functions with independent Gaussian coefficients for efficient error representation. The use of GP introduces a coupling relationship between the model parameters and the Gaussian coefficients, which makes it impossible to directly infer their joint posterior distribution. To resolve this issue, variational inference is employed. Specifically, the mean field assumption is utilized to decouple the parameters into independent sets, and the variational distributions of each set are sequentially inferred. To ensure consistency across these distributions, an iterative procedure is designed, where the evidence lower bound serves as the convergence index. Through iterative sequential inference, the optimal variational distributions for each parameter set are obtained, and their product approximates the joint posterior distribution. Additionally, the model class selection approach is utilized to determine the optimal number of orthogonal terms for simulating prediction errors, striking a balance of simulation accuracy and complexity. With the estimated uncertainties of model parameters and the GP model of prediction errors, the uncertainty of the output quantity of interest can be predicted. The effectiveness of the proposed framework is validated using two examples in structural dynamics.

title: Incomplete cost-sensitive collaborative learning-based manufacturing quality predictive modeling method under heterogeneous sensing
exported_title: Incomplete cost-sensitive collaborative learning-based manufacturing quality predictive modeling method under heterogeneous sensing

metadata.abstract: The manufacturing quality of the product plays a vital role in the reliability of the complex equipment and the overall system safety. Accurately predicting manufacturing quality helps promptly detect abnormal products and shorten production time. Nevertheless, the multi-source heterogeneous sensor data on the manufacturing systems will unavoidably result in incomplete data, thereby affecting the accuracy of the predictive model. In addition, the imbalanced data in quality labels can deceive conventional models to obtain inexact predictive boundaries, leading to missed detection of abnormal manufacturing products. In this study, an new incomplete cost-sensitive collaborative learning-based model is proposed for manufacturing quality prediction. Specifically, an improved probabilistic principal component analysis-based incomplete learning module is first designed to supplement heterogeneous data information. After that, an elaborated cost-sensitive quality predictive model is developed to handle the imbalanced quality labels. Finally, an evolutionary collaborative learning strategy is appended to enhance predictive performance via collaboratively optimizing the incomplete and cost-sensitive learning modules. Application case studies of actual wheel bearing component and valve manufacturing plants demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves higher accuracy in manufacturing quality abnormal prediction.

title: Ensemble multimodal fusing learning for geological identification in tunnel construction
exported_title: Ensemble multimodal fusing learning for geological identification in tunnel construction

metadata.abstract: This paper proposes an ensemble multimodal deep learning approach to identify the geological conditions in shield tunnel engineering. The proposed approach improves the Swin Transformer architecture, building a multimodal model with soil images and tunnel boring machine (TBM) parameters as input. The Dempster Shafer theory is used for information fusion to develop the Ensemble Swin-Transformer-MLP (ESwin-T-M), which accurately identifies geological conditions for tunnel shield projects. In addition, the Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-Cam) and the Model-Agnostic Permutation Feature Importance (MAPFI) are used to perform model interpretation analysis. The Circle Line Phase 6 C885 Tunnel Project in Singapore is used to validate the effectiveness of the proposed approach. The results indicate that: (1) The proposed ensemble multimodal fusing network identifies geological conditions with a high F1-Score of 0.9746 in 5-fold cross-validation. (2) The recognition accuracy of the ensemble multimodal fusion network is superior to that of the single modality models and the basic models. (3) The ensemble fusing approach outperforms the approaches utilizing soil images or TBM parameters separately in terms of robustness and anti-interference ability. The novelty of this research lies in the development of an integrated detection method for multimodal information, which overcomes the trustworthy limitations of traditional single-data method and provides technical support for the precise and reliable identification of geological conditions in tunnel engineering.

title: An online prediction method for airplane landing risk in extremely windy conditions based on stream learning
exported_title: An online prediction method for airplane landing risk in extremely windy conditions based on stream learning

metadata.abstract: Accurate prediction of landing risk during extremely windy conditions is vital to ensuring flight safety. However, most existing methods rely on pre-trained single-risk models, which often have poor prediction accuracy under extremely windy conditions such as strong winds. This study proposes an online multi-risk prediction method for airplane landing during extremely windy conditions, leveraging a streaming Bi-LSTM-Transformer (BLT) architecture. First, data preprocessing is performed to ensure the high-quality input for analysis. A comprehensive multi-risk assessment framework is then developed to evaluate the potential landing risks, utilizing the processed data. Subsequently, time-series modeling is conducted using a Bi-LSTM network. To improve the models’ global time-series modeling ability, a Transformer component is integrated into the Bi-LSTM output, forming the BLT model. Finally, stream learning is introduced to maintain predictive performance under extremely windy conditions. Using real-time flight data streams, the Stream BLT model applies eligibility traces and a dynamic learning rate to enable continuous, adaptive learning. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method accurately predicts airplane landing risks under extremely windy conditions, particularly when wind speeds exceed 33knots. The model achieves an average relative error of approximately 0.01–0.07 and a prediction latency of under 30 ms, offering efficient, reliable real-time airplane landing risk assessment.

title: Multi-level adaptive risk control: synergistic maintenance-termination optimization with online parameter learning
exported_title: Multi-level adaptive risk control: synergistic maintenance-termination optimization with online parameter learning

metadata.abstract: Catastrophic functional disruptions of degrading systems during task executions usually incur severe safety repercussions and substantial losses, necessitating prompt risk mitigation strategies. It is therefore of paramount significance to develop distinct risk intervention levels following refined degradation evaluations. This study establishes a collaborative self-adaptive optimization problem of routine maintenance and task termination decisions for heterogeneous degrading systems. A Bayesian learning methodology is employed to continuously update the unknown degradation rate utilizing equidistantly sampled data; leveraging such updates constitutes an adaptive multi-level risk control policy employing age-state-dependent thresholds to select between (a) operational continuation, (b) routine maintenance partially restoring degradation at a severity-dependent cost, or (c) terminate the task instantly for overhaul. In order to minimize the total expense encompassing maintenance expenditures, task failure penalties, and termination losses, we identify several key findings into the optimality of the multi-level control policy, showcasing that the policy is representable as a monotonic threshold policy relative to degradation progression. Implementation on shipboard phased-array radar drivers confirms the framework’s operational viability and demonstrates substantial advantages over conventional strategies in risk loss prevention and task success promotion.

title: Adaptive portfolio optimization-based metamodel method for the multi-armed bandit problem of learning function in slope reliability analysis
exported_title: Adaptive portfolio optimization-based metamodel method for the multi-armed bandit problem of learning function in slope reliability analysis

metadata.abstract: Adaptive metamodels using single learning functions fail to consistently maintain the high accuracy or efficiency in calculating failure probabilities of slopes under all scenarios (e.g., natural vs. reservoir slopes) due to the No Free Lunch theorem. It poses a challenge in the adaptive selection of the optimal function under high-dimensional random field domains. To this end, we consider the selection problem as a multi-armed bandit problem, and thus propose a portfolio optimization-based adaptive polynomial-chaos Kriging (POPCK) method that dynamically balances exploration and exploitation of six distinct learning functions, thereby adaptively selecting better functions based on their historical performance. This adaptive selection could be performed under high-dimensional variables by incorporating Karhunen–Loève expansion and sliced inverse regression techniques into POPCK. The feasibility of the proposed method is demonstrated through four classic examples (involving natural, four soil layers, rainfall infiltration, and water level drawdown conditions). Results show that the proposed method exhibits good robustness for all examples, high accuracy (ranking 1st) and computational efficiency (ranking 2nd), whereas the performance of PCKs using the single learning functions fluctuates greatly. This method effectively mitigates the randomness of learning function selection, which is valuable for engineers who lack prior knowledge of optimal learning functions.

title: An efficient reliability assessment framework for complex mechanism wear degradation based on probabilistic space decomposition kriging model
exported_title: An efficient reliability assessment framework for complex mechanism wear degradation based on probabilistic space decomposition kriging model

metadata.abstract: Operational wear in complex mechanical systems with joint clearances, driven by nonlinear dynamic behavior, leads to functional degradation and accelerated failure. While critical, the influence of vibration on wear progression is often overlooked in existing studies, and efficiently assessing the reliability of high-fidelity simulation models remains a significant challenge. To address these issues, this paper proposes a reliability assessment framework for wear degradation (PSDK-WDR). First, we develop a non-uniform wear prediction model that integrates a nonlinear dynamic model with the Archard wear model. This model innovatively updates the wear coefficient using parameters derived from real-time vibration signal energy dissipation. Furthermore, for efficient reliability analysis, we introduce a Monte Carlo simulation method based on a Probability Space Decomposition Kriging model (PSDK-MCS). This method decomposes high-dimensional random variables into subsets via Probabilistic Space Decomposition (PSD) and constructs parallel Kriging sub-models for each subset to accelerate assessments. The accuracy and efficiency of the proposed wear model and the PSDK-WDR framework are validated through case studies on crank-slider and flapping-wing mechanisms. This work provides a theoretical basis for understanding wear evolution and efficiently evaluating reliability degradation in complex mechanisms.

title: Nested adaptive Kriging-based reliability analysis and computational resource allocation for complex systems
exported_title: Nested adaptive Kriging-based reliability analysis and computational resource allocation for complex systems

metadata.abstract: Efficient reliability analysis of complex engineering systems faces significant challenges due to the integration of multiple subproblems, multidisciplinary coupling, high-dimensional characteristics, and resource incompatibility. These systems are often decomposed into multiple cascading subsystems, which enables concurrent analysis to manage this complexity. Surrogate-based techniques are widely utilized to alleviate the computational burden associated with time-consuming simulations. This study proposes a nested adaptive Kriging-based method for the reliability analysis of complex systems by integrating system decomposition with adaptive surrogate-based methods. The proposed method operates within a multilayer framework and proceeds in two stages, namely, a sequential updating stage and a resource allocation stage. In the first stage, an efficient nested reliability-oriented acquisition function is developed to guide model updating, and its closed-form expression is derived. In the second stage, a cost-effectiveness strategy that accounts for both simulation costs and modeling costs is introduced to determine which model combinations should be updated at each iteration. Finally, the proposed method is validated to be superior to the benchmark method and strategy through two mathematical examples and two practical applications.

title: Domain knowledge-enhanced dual-stream graph joint learning network for aeroengine remaining useful life prediction
exported_title: Domain knowledge-enhanced dual-stream graph joint learning network for aeroengine remaining useful life prediction

metadata.abstract: Prediction methods integrating domain knowledge with deep learning show great promise for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction of aeroengines. Nevertheless, neglecting the decoupling modeling of multi-level domain knowledge such as component-level physical topology and parameter-level essential dependencies has resulted in insufficient and incorrect utilization of valuable degradation information, limiting the further improvement of prediction accuracy and stability. Therefore, a novel domain knowledge-enhanced dual-stream graph joint learning network (DK-DGJLN) is proposed. First, the physical essential dependencies among components and sensor parameters are extracted through in-depth analysis of aeroengine’s overall structure and working characteristics. Then, a component-level static graph is built to capture physical topology with high fidelity, while a parameter-level dynamic graph is constructed to model dynamic dependencies and degradation evolution. Their decoupling modeling enables faithful embedding of multi-level domain knowledge. Finally, a DGJLN is designed to extract rich and complementary spatial-temporal degradation features from both graphs, with a self-attention-based feature alignment module aggregating them for accurate RUL prediction. Extensive comparative experiments on the C-MAPSS dataset against 19 SOTA methods demonstrate that DK-DGJLN significantly improves prediction performance, especially on FD002 and FD004, where the RMSE values of 12.93 and 13.57 are markedly lower than those of the best comparative methods.

title: Multi-granularity learning-based intelligent decision-making method for equipment operation and maintenance on large-scale knowledge graphs
exported_title: Multi-granularity learning-based intelligent decision-making method for equipment operation and maintenance on large-scale knowledge graphs

metadata.abstract: Effective equipment operation and maintenance (O&M) is crucial for productivity and safety; however, traditional manual decision-making methods are hindered by long cycles and inconsistent accuracy. This paper introduces MulKGR, an intelligent decision-making model designed for large-scale O&M knowledge graphs, addressing challenges such as insufficient multi-level fault association and low decision-making efficiency. The model extracts multi-granularity subgraphs from the O&M knowledge graph, incorporating equipment status, failure modes, and environmental factors to construct relational paths that enhance decision-making. MulKGR then employs a graph convolutional network (GCN) to jointly encode problem text and relational paths, generating word embeddings and calculating similarity scores, thereby optimizing computational efficiency through subgraph pruning. Finally, the pruned subgraphs are processed by a reasoning decision module that integrates GCN with long- and short-term memory networks for dynamic learning, enabling accurate reasoning and answer generation. Experimental results from a new energy vehicle production plant show that MulKGR significantly improves decision-making, achieving an F1 score of 65.88 %, a Hits@1 score of 62.5 %, and reducing decision-making time by 5.69 %. These results demonstrate the model's effectiveness in intelligent decision-making for equipment O&M.

title: Graph learning with variational graph structural information bottleneck for multi-sensor machinery remaining useful life prediction
exported_title: Graph learning with variational graph structural information bottleneck for multi-sensor machinery remaining useful life prediction

metadata.abstract: Existing graph learning-based remaining useful life (RUL) prediction approaches typically rely on predefined structural priors or fixed constraints to optimize graph topologies. Such priors are often crafted for specific signal modalities and thus exhibit limited generality, restricting their ability to model the complex and heterogeneous interdependencies inherent in multi-sensor signals. To overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a graph learning framework with a variational graph structural information bottleneck (GL-VGSIB) for multi-sensor machinery RUL prediction. The proposed GL-VGSIB establishes an information-theoretic graph structure learning paradigm that adaptively discovers degradation-relevant graph representations by balancing discriminability and compressibility. In contrast to prior GNN-based RUL frameworks that depend on static structural priors, the variational bottleneck mechanism in GL-VGSIB infers a probabilistic distribution over graph structures, enabling the model to preserve essential task-relevant dependencies while suppressing redundant or spurious connections. The framework integrates a multi-scale convolutional encoder with positional encoding to enhance spatio-temporal feature extraction and employs a reparameterization mechanism to facilitate differentiable stochastic graph sampling. Experimental results on two multi-sensor equipment datasets show that GL-VGSIB achieves a 2.9%-14.8% reduction in prediction error relative to state-of-the-art baselines, thereby demonstrating its effectiveness to multi-sensor machinery RUL prediction.

title: Active Kriging-based uniform importance sampling with rejection control for highly efficient and accurate structural reliability analysis
exported_title: Active Kriging-based uniform importance sampling with rejection control for highly efficient and accurate structural reliability analysis

metadata.abstract: Developing highly efficient and accurate structural reliability analysis for high computational cost and low failure probability problems is critical for engineering application. In this paper, a novel active learning strategy coupling with weight control and adaptive distance control is proposed for Kriging-based uniform importance sampling. The rejection control is introduced to improve the efficiency of reliability analysis. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through numerical cases and three aerospace engineering applications, which showed that the proposed strategy could reduce both the cost of performance function evaluations and surrogate model calls. The repeated results validated that the proposed method is efficient, accurate, and robust, proving its capability to address real-world engineering challenges.

title: Risk predictive deduction and propagation chain mining for URT emergencies based on interpretable ensemble learning: A new approach to in-time safety management
exported_title: Risk predictive deduction and propagation chain mining for URT emergencies based on interpretable ensemble learning: A new approach to in-time safety management

metadata.abstract: To enhance the emergency response capability of Urban Rail Transit (URT), this paper proposes an in-time safety management approach based on explanatory ensemble learning and key risk chain mining. Firstly, an innovative in-time safety management framework is designed. On this basis, historical incident data from Beijing Metro in recent years is used to identify risk causation and impact range. A dynamic risk assessment and predictive deduction method based on explanatory Stacking ensemble learning model is designed. It incorporates Synthetic Minority Over-Sampling Technique (SMOTE) for sample balanced and Optuna for optimal hyperparameter tuning of both base and meta models, achieving superior prediction accuracy for risk impact levels. Then, SHapley Additive exPlanation (SHAP) is employed to identify key risk causes and quantify their influence on prediction results. Finally, an improved W-Apriori algorithm is employed to mine the complex associations within key risk propagation chains, thereby providing targeted emergency response strategies. To demonstrate the approach, this paper presents a simulation case based on real operational emergency data and indicate that the proposed model achieves 95.83% accuracy, outperforming traditional machine learning methods across five performance metrics and exhibit superiority to promote a shift in URT safety management from traditional reactive response to proactive prevention and in-time intervention.

title: Stress-coupled parameter learning in stochastic processes for reliability-oriented accelerated degradation modeling
exported_title: Stress-coupled parameter learning in stochastic processes for reliability-oriented accelerated degradation modeling

metadata.abstract: Accelerated degradation testing is widely used for reliability assessment, yet stochastic processes cannot be directly utilized to model accelerated degradation data because they lack inherent stress covariate. To address this problem, the stress-coupled parameters, whose values vary with stress levels, must first be determined. Then, the stress-coupled parameters are replaced by acceleration models to construct a degradation model incorporating stress covariate. However, the assumed stress-coupled parameters have commonly been adopted, resulting in poor explicability of accelerated degradation modeling and unreliable life extrapolation results, particularly when multiple assumptions on stress-coupled parameters exist for a given degradation model. This study proposes an explicable framework for determining stress-coupled parameters in stochastic processes. The framework consists of two approaches: an analytical derivation method for linear degradation models and a numerical computation method for nonlinear models. These approaches are applied to Wiener, Gamma, and Inverse Gaussian processes to derive stress-coupled parameters, validating the equivalence of them for linear degradation models and revealing that different time functions fundamentally determine the stress-dependency patterns of model parameters. The numerical computation method is applicable to complex degradation models, but it can not discover the potential proportional relationship among multiple stress-coupled parameters. To address this issue, the framework offers a workflow combining the two approaches. A case study on electrical connectors further verifies the practical effectiveness of the proposed framework. The results show that the framework works well in deriving stress-coupled parameters and benefits strengthening the theoretical basis of accelerate degradation modeling.

title: Physics-constrained causal structure learning for root cause analysis in nuclear system monitoring
exported_title: Physics-constrained causal structure learning for root cause analysis in nuclear system monitoring

metadata.abstract: Root cause analysis (RCA) is important for identifying the initiating cause of faults and analyzing fault propagation paths in nuclear systems. However, robust RCA in nuclear accident monitoring remains challenging because it depends on reliable identification of causal relationships among monitoring variables, which is difficult under complex system coupling and limited-sample conditions. To address this issue, this paper proposes a physics-constrained causal structure learning method for RCA in nuclear accident monitoring. First, a simplified physical model of the nuclear system is constructed to extract a priori causal knowledge among key monitoring variables. Second, the causal relationships among different variables are learned by a score-based causal structure learning method under the guidance of the extracted physical constraints. In this process, physically infeasible edges are excluded and the admissible parent sets are restricted before score optimization. Finally, the root cause nodes of faults are identified based on the learned causal graph. The proposed method is validated using two representative accident scenarios generated from a nuclear simulation platform. The results show that the proposed method can improve root-node identification performance, reduce abnormal-edge misidentification, and enhance the robustness of causal structure learning under limited-sample conditions without introducing additional computational burden.

title: Dynamic branch expansion: A hypergraph-augmented adaptive continual learning framework for machine health prognosis under time-varying conditions
exported_title: Dynamic branch expansion: A hypergraph-augmented adaptive continual learning framework for machine health prognosis under time-varying conditions

metadata.abstract: Industrial data streams with dynamic distributions pose more daunting challenges for data-driven machine health monitoring. Continual learning (CL) method has the ability to adapt to newly-collected data and retain partial memory of previous degradation knowledge, while it still sinks into a dilemma of insufficient accumulation for long-term and diverse degradation patterns under complex operating conditions (OCs). This study proposes an adaptive continuous health prognosis framework with dynamic branch expansion (DBE) for absorbing dynamic data streams to predict the remaining useful life of rotating machines under time-varying OCs. Among it, an OC-aware hypergraph topology network is designed to enhance the hypergraph representation, after which hypergraph topology-memorized knowledge buffer is established for optimal replay sampling. On this basis, an adaptive DBE framework is constructed, which self-recognizes the addition of branches with the continuous influx of new data; and it ingeniously integrates multi-branch predictions via branch discriminator logits at inference stage to enhance CL generalization capability. Case studies of multi-stage continuous prognosis are conducted to verify the effectiveness of the proposed framework. The results indicate that it can gradually enhance the prediction performance with incremental data, and maintain the predictions of old data while fully learning degraded knowledge at new stages.

title: Risk-oriented degradation modeling and maintenance decision support for computed tomography X-ray tubes using mechanism-informed learning
exported_title: Risk-oriented degradation modeling and maintenance decision support for computed tomography X-ray tubes using mechanism-informed learning

metadata.abstract: Accurate estimation of the remaining useful life (RUL) of Computed Tomography (CT) X-ray tubes is essential for maintaining medical service continuity, reducing failure risk, and minimizing unplanned downtime. However, intrinsic degradation patterns are often obscured by heterogeneous operating conditions, such as automatic tube current modulation and voltage optimization. To address this challenge, we propose the Hybrid Affine Gated Fusion Network (HAGF-Net), a deep learning framework tailored for Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) environments. HAGF-Net employs a dual-branch parallel architecture that integrates physical priors with data-driven features. One branch processes Mechanism-driven Indicators (MDIs) derived from filament degradation physics, including cathode degradation rate (CDR) and degradation kinetic increment (DKI), using a Conditioned Operating-Gated Transformer (COG-Transformer) that dynamically modulates attention weights based on discrete operational states. Simultaneously, a raw-signal Branch based on CNN-LSTM modules captures local fluctuations and long-term temporal dependencies from multi-dimensional sensor sequences. The framework was validated on a high-resolution IoMT dataset comprising 10 Philips X-ray tubes from multiple clinical sites across China (2017–2024), covering their entire service lives. HAGF-Net demonstrates high global predictive accuracy (RMSE = 0.07) and precise final-stage performance (MAE ≈ 3.85 days) and 95% prediction intervals close to the nominal coverage across sites. Ablation and comparison studies indicate that incorporating physical MDIs and condition-aware gating mechanisms enhances model’s robustness and responsiveness to complex degradation dynamics. Under simulated unreliable monitoring conditions, the proposed method evaluates model robustness under reduced sampling frequencies, demonstrating stable performance across different levels of data sparsity.

title: Reliable virtual sensing of inter-turbine total pressure in degraded aero-engines via physics-constrained online learning
exported_title: Reliable virtual sensing of inter-turbine total pressure in degraded aero-engines via physics-constrained online learning

metadata.abstract: Reliable acquisition of inter-turbine total pressure P43 remains difficult in aero-engines, especially under component degradation and anomalous data conditions. This study proposes a physics-constrained virtual sensing method for reliable reconstruction of P43 in degraded aero-engines. First, building on rotor-inertia-power-balance-based temperature reconstruction, the underlying assumptions and degradation-induced mismatch characteristics of forward and backward P43 reconstruction are analyzed, and P43 is rapidly reconstructed using measurable low-temperature-region parameters and engine design information. Second, the physical reconstruction is embedded into an online sequential extreme learning machine to establish a physics-constrained learning framework. An adaptive data-physics fusion strategy and an online regression mechanism are further introduced to improve robustness under degradation, anomalous training data, and previously unseen operating conditions. Comparative simulations show that the proposed method maintains relatively low reconstruction errors under the considered degradation conditions and exhibits reduced sensitivity to physical-model mismatch compared with the evaluated physics-based and hybrid baselines. It also suppresses the influence of noisy and biased data, reduces the dependence on a high-dimensional fault-sample database, and provides stable prediction over a wide operating envelope with low computational cost. These results indicate that the proposed method offers a practical and reliable solution for monitoring degradation-sensitive parameters in complex aero-engine systems.
